items.title: From Sewers to Surveillance: Monitoring Salmonella Through Wastewater.
items.summary: Wastewater surveillance offers a population-level approach to infectious disease monitoring that can detect cases missed by clinical reporting, including asymptomatic and unreported infections. This study developed and validated methods for detecting Salmonella in wastewater, combining sample concentration through polyethylene glycol precipitation, magnetic bead-based nucleic acid extraction, and quantitative PCR. These methods were deployed across a statewide surveillance network to track Salmonella transmission over a two-year period. The surveillance system revealed seasonal transmission patterns, provided approximately one week of advance warning relative to clinical case reporting, and detected outbreak activity that passive surveillance systems failed to capture. While limitations such as low pathogen concentrations and difficulty resolving serovars remain, the findings support wastewater surveillance as a valuable early-warning and outbreak detection tool when used alongside traditional public health approaches.
items.citation: Kuhn KG, Shelton K, Rimal B et al.. From Sewers to Surveillance: Monitoring Salmonella Through Wastewater.. Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.). 2027

items.title: A Rapid Decision Framework for Wastewater and Environmental Surveillance (WES) during Rapidly Emerging and Evolving Outbreak Settings
items.citation: Ahmed W, Medlicott K, Nolan M. A Rapid Decision Framework for Wastewater and Environmental Surveillance (WES) during Rapidly Emerging and Evolving Outbreak Settings. ACS ES&T water. 2026

items.title: Machine learning-enabled wastewater-based surveillance for emerging pathogen detection and monitoring: current applications, challenges, and future prospects.
items.summary: This review examined how machine learning is being applied to wastewater-based surveillance to detect and monitor emerging pathogens at the community level. The authors conducted a narrative review of published literature, classifying methods into four tiers ranging from classical statistical models through deep learning and hybrid mechanistic approaches, and evaluated their application across five analytical tasks including forecasting, anomaly detection, and data harmonization. They found that the evidence base is heavily skewed toward studies of a single pathogen, with most other target-task combinations remaining prospective rather than validated, and that early-warning performance came predominantly from simpler statistical methods rather than more complex machine learning approaches. Reported predictive performance was consistently context-dependent, and the field faces substantial barriers related to data quality, sampling variability, inter-laboratory inconsistency, and population-level biases that limit generalizability. The authors conclude that future progress requires standardized collaborative frameworks, multimodal data integration, mechanistically informed modelling with uncertainty quantification, and attention to governance and public acceptability before broader surveillance applications can be realized.
items.citation: Song A, Jia P, Luo J et al.. Machine learning-enabled wastewater-based surveillance for emerging pathogen detection and monitoring: current applications, challenges, and future prospects.. Emerging microbes & infections. 2026

items.title: Multimodal genomic surveillance for respiratory pathogens at four U.S. international airports: A comparison of air, wastewater, clinical, and national surveillance data.
items.summary: This study evaluated whether air sampling in airport environments could serve as an effective surveillance tool for respiratory pathogens at points of international entry. Researchers monitored four major U.S. international airports over approximately ten months, collecting air samples from congregate areas and comparing the results against aviation wastewater, traveler nasal swabs, and national clinical surveillance data. Both SARS-CoV-2 and influenza A were frequently detected in air samples, with influenza A positivity showing strong correlations with other surveillance modalities, particularly national clinical data, while SARS-CoV-2 measurements did not correlate consistently across methods. Genomic sequencing of air samples successfully identified circulating viral lineages and recovered high-quality genomes for multiple respiratory viruses, including seasonal coronaviruses and bocavirus, demonstrating broad pathogen detection capability. The findings support air sampling as a complementary approach to wastewater-based surveillance at airports, though the utility varies depending on the specific pathogen and surveillance modality being compared.
items.citation: Gratalo D, Friedman CR, Morley VJ et al.. Multimodal genomic surveillance for respiratory pathogens at four U.S. international airports: A comparison of air, wastewater, clinical, and national surveillance data.. PLOS global public health. 2026

items.title: Progress and Expansion of the National Wastewater Surveillance System, United States, 2020-2024.
items.summary: The paper describes the development and expansion of the National Wastewater Surveillance System in the United States from its origins as an emergency pandemic response tool through its first four years of operation. The authors document how the system grew in national testing coverage, pathogen targets, analytical capabilities, data visualizations, and laboratory methods over this period. Collaboration across public, private, and academic sectors drove progress toward standardizing practices and translating wastewater signals into actionable public health guidance. The paper argues that wastewater surveillance has transitioned from an emergency initiative into an established component of public health infrastructure, demonstrating adaptability and scalability in supporting timely, data-driven responses to community-level health threats.
items.citation: Mark-Carew M, Bias M, Reckling S et al.. Progress and Expansion of the National Wastewater Surveillance System, United States, 2020-2024.. Emerging infectious diseases. 2026

items.title: Laboratory Evaluation of Cyclospora cayetanensis in Wastewater: Expanding Pathogen Targets for Regulatory Public Health Surveillance
items.citation: Lin C, Gonzalez DS, Poretsky RS. Laboratory Evaluation of Cyclospora cayetanensis in Wastewater: Expanding Pathogen Targets for Regulatory Public Health Surveillance. 2026

items.title: Inferring variant-specific effective reproduction numbers from combined case and sequencing data
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of accurately estimating the transmission rates of co-circulating SARS-CoV-2 variants, which is important for both scientific understanding and public health response. The authors developed a statistical method that jointly estimates variant-specific effective reproduction numbers and variant frequencies by combining confirmed case counts with genetic sequence data, rather than relying on sequence proportions alone. The approach allows for structured relationships between reproduction numbers across time series and can estimate fixed growth advantages for specific variants across different locations. Applying the method to data from United States states over a roughly fourteen-month period spanning multiple waves and variants of concern, the authors demonstrated that their framework captures richer epidemiological dynamics than frequency-based approaches and yields consistent estimates of variant growth advantages across geographic settings.
items.citation: Marlin D Figgins, Trevor Bedford. Inferring variant-specific effective reproduction numbers from combined case and sequencing data. eLife. 2026

items.title: Soil microbes are the tiny bioengineers running Earth’s underground factory
items.summary: This paper synthesizes existing research on soil microbial communities with the goal of clarifying how microbial diversity translates into ecosystem-level functions. The authors developed a function-centred framework organized around four conserved functional axes — secondary metabolism, nutrient cycling, community interactions, and stress tolerance — drawing on studies spanning ecological, agricultural, and environmental contexts. They argue that these axes collectively drive processes such as plant productivity, climate regulation, and pollutant transformation, though their expression varies strongly with context. A central theoretical claim is that soil operates as a self-organizing system in which microbial interactions produce emergent ecosystem behaviours. The framework is proposed as a foundation for predictive, ecology-informed strategies to manage soils for sustainable agriculture, environmental remediation, and climate mitigation.
items.citation: Suzanne Hassan-Dalléac, Wafa Guiga, Antonia Suau. Soil microbes are the tiny bioengineers running Earth’s underground factory. Communications Earth & Environment. 2026

items.title: Beyond the visible: metal-ion-doped inorganic UV phosphors for advanced photonics
items.summary: This review examines inorganic ultraviolet luminescent materials doped with metal ions, including rare-earth and heavy main-group metal ions, which display distinctive electronic transitions, strong photostability, and tunable emission properties. The authors systematically survey three principal luminescence modes — persistent luminescence, upconversion luminescence, and mechanoluminescence — covering their underlying mechanisms, recent advances in material design, and strategies for optimizing UV emission. Applications spanning optoelectronics, environmental remediation, and biomedicine are analyzed under the organizing principle that material performance should guide application selection. The review also identifies current challenges in the field and proposes future research directions to advance inorganic UV phosphors toward broader practical deployment.
items.citation: Yu Zhang, Yanjie Liang, Feng Liu et al.. Beyond the visible: metal-ion-doped inorganic UV phosphors for advanced photonics. Light Science & Applications. 2026

items.title: Quantitative Microbial Risk Assessment of Human H5N1 Infection From Consumption of Fluid Cow's Milk
items.summary: This study assessed the public health risk of human H5N1 influenza infection through consumption of fluid cow's milk following the spillover of a specific H5N1 clade into dairy cattle herds. Using a farm-to-table quantitative microbial risk assessment framework with stochastic modeling, researchers estimated infection probabilities per serving for pasteurized milk, farm-store-purchased raw milk, and retail-purchased raw milk, drawing on outbreak-specific literature to parameterize their models. The results demonstrated that pasteurization is highly effective at reducing H5N1 infection risk, with pasteurized milk carrying a vanishingly small probability of infection compared to raw milk products. Scenario analysis further identified bulk tank milk testing using quantitative real-time reverse transcriptase-polymerase chain reaction as an effective intervention for reducing risk associated with raw milk consumption. The authors also highlight critical knowledge gaps regarding the human dose-response relationship for H5N1 ingestion and raw milk consumption patterns, underscoring the need for additional research and the value of mechanistic epidemiologic models in guiding public health responses to outbreaks with foodborne transmission potential.
items.citation: Katherine J Koebel, Ece Bulut, Samuel David Alcaine et al.. Quantitative Microbial Risk Assessment of Human H5N1 Infection From Consumption of Fluid Cow's Milk. Risk Analysis. 2026

items.title: Antimicrobial resistance in aquaculture an overview of current status and possible solutions to the issue
items.summary: This review examines the growing problem of antimicrobial resistance in aquaculture, tracing how widespread antibiotic use in the sector has driven the development and environmental spread of resistance. The paper surveys the ecological and genetic mechanisms underlying resistance, including horizontal gene transfer, biofilm formation, and the persistence of antibiotic resistance genes in sediments and water bodies, as well as the public health risks posed by transmission through seafood and occupational exposure. Current national and international regulatory frameworks are evaluated, with the review identifying substantial gaps in monitoring, enforcement, and cross-country harmonization. The paper considers a broad range of alternative and complementary strategies to reduce antibiotic dependence, spanning vaccines, probiotics, phage therapy, plant antimicrobials, nanotechnology, and precision aquaculture, alongside molecular surveillance tools such as metagenomics and quantitative PCR. The authors advocate for a One Health approach that integrates human, veterinary, and environmental health sectors, and call for policy harmonization, capacity building, and research investment to advance sustainable and antibiotic-responsible aquaculture.
items.citation: Shafiya Mushtaq, Tasaduq Hussain Shah, Nahida Quyoom et al.. Antimicrobial resistance in aquaculture an overview of current status and possible solutions to the issue. Discover Environment. 2026

items.title: Pharmaceuticals in Water: Fate, Health Risks, Treatment and Governance for Sustainable Management
items.summary: This review examines the presence, behavior, and management of pharmaceutical compounds as emerging contaminants in aquatic environments, focusing on therapeutic classes such as antibiotics, anti-inflammatory drugs, antidepressants, hormones, and beta-blockers. The authors synthesize current evidence on how these substances enter, persist in, and move through water systems across their full lifecycle, from production and consumption through to environmental persistence. Despite occurring at trace concentrations, these compounds are shown to pose potential ecological and human health risks through various biological mechanisms even at low exposure levels. The review critically evaluates both established and emerging water treatment technologies alongside existing regulatory and governance frameworks. Based on this synthesis, the authors propose an integrated management framework combining lifecycle thinking, advanced treatment approaches, and adaptive regulatory governance to guide sustainable protection of drinking-water resources.
items.citation: Asvinidevi Arumugam, Khai Ern Lee, Pei Yuen Ng et al.. Pharmaceuticals in Water: Fate, Health Risks, Treatment and Governance for Sustainable Management. Water Air & Soil Pollution. 2026

items.title: SceneBloom: Agentic Indoor Environment Generation with Realistic and Diverse Layouts for Embodied Learning
items.summary: SceneBloom is an agentic framework designed to generate realistic and diverse indoor 3D environments for training embodied AI agents, addressing limitations in both language-guided spatial planning and visual generative approaches. The system combines a hierarchical diffusion-based sampler that generates furniture arrangements within functional zones with a contract-guided compiler that extracts spatial relations from proposals to perform geometric fitting and pose correction, ensuring physically valid scenes. Evaluated across five room types, the framework achieves the highest visual quality and physical stability among compared methods, with no detected mesh collisions or out-of-bounds objects, and produces layouts that more closely match the distribution of real rooms than all baselines. Notably, object navigation policies trained in SceneBloom-generated environments outperform those trained on an equivalent number of real indoor scans when tested on held-out real environments, suggesting the generated scenes provide effective diversity and realism for embodied learning.
items.citation: Yuhan Liu, Lianhui Qin, Shenji Wan. SceneBloom: Agentic Indoor Environment Generation with Realistic and Diverse Layouts for Embodied Learning. arXiv. 2026

items.title: MiD-VLM: Detecting and Grounding Global Semantic Misinformation in Image-Caption Pairs
items.summary: This paper investigates the detection of semantic misinformation in image-caption pairs, where an authentic image is paired with a misleading or distorted caption rather than exhibiting any pixel-level manipulation. The authors developed a multimodal model that fuses image-text representations from SigLIP with visual scene features from DINOv2 via a projection layer, then applies parameter-efficient fine-tuning through LoRA to adapt a large vision-language model. The system was designed to simultaneously classify whether a pair is authentic, identify the type of manipulation present, and localize the misleading tokens within the caption. Evaluated on a dataset targeting global semantic inconsistencies, the model achieved strong performance on binary authenticity classification, demonstrating that lightweight adaptation of vision-language models can effectively capture cross-modal semantic discrepancies. The authors conclude that while parameter-efficient adaptation is a promising direction, further work is needed to improve precise token-level grounding of misinformation.
items.citation: Tarunya Prasad, Bharatesh Chakravarthi. MiD-VLM: Detecting and Grounding Global Semantic Misinformation in Image-Caption Pairs. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Flownomaly: Single-Step Conditional-Mean Recovery for Few-Shot Anomaly Detection
items.summary: The paper addresses few-shot industrial anomaly detection, where models must learn what "normal" looks like from only a small number of defect-free images and then identify deviations in new queries. The authors propose Flownomaly, which frames the problem as recovering a normal counterpart for a given query in the feature space of a frozen pretrained vision model, using conditional flow matching to learn a velocity field that transports Gaussian noise toward normal patch features. A key design choice is that inference requires only a single evaluation of the learned velocity field rather than full trajectory integration, yielding the posterior mean of the clean normal token efficiently, and an operating time parameter is selected automatically using a normal-only Jacobian criterion that requires no anomalous validation samples. Anomaly scores are derived from squared residuals between query tokens and their recovered normal counterparts, enabling both pixel-level localization and image-level detection. Evaluated across multiple few-shot benchmarks, Flownomaly achieves state-of-the-art performance compared to recent category-specific methods, with particularly notable gains in the one-shot setting.
items.citation: Bernardo Perrone Ribeiro, Erkut Akdag, Egor Bondarev. Flownomaly: Single-Step Conditional-Mean Recovery for Few-Shot Anomaly Detection. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A Central Limit Theorem for the Driver Site Frequency Spectrum
items.summary: This paper studies the statistical properties of the driver site frequency spectrum (SFS) in a supercritical two-type continuous-time linear birth-death process that incorporates mutation and selection, where mutant individuals have a higher net-growth rate than wild-type individuals. Building on previously established law of large numbers results for the SFS, the authors derive a second-order central limit theorem by demonstrating stable convergence of a suitably scaled deviation of the SFS from its first-order limit. The central limit theorem is established under both large detection times and large detection sizes. These theoretical results are then applied to construct confidence intervals for a class of consistent estimators of the fitness advantage conferred by the driver mutation.
items.citation: Armaan Ahmed, Jasmine Foo, Kevin Leder. A Central Limit Theorem for the Driver Site Frequency Spectrum. arXiv. 2026

items.title: If at First You Don't Succeed, Backtrack: Lightweight Recovery for Frozen VLAs
items.summary: This paper addresses the brittleness of Vision-Language-Action models in robotic manipulation, specifically their tendency to fail when their own actions lead them into states underrepresented in training data. The authors introduce Backtrack, a lightweight mechanism that adds a small failure prediction head trained on outcome-labeled rollouts of a frozen policy, using the policy's existing internal representations to estimate the likelihood of episode failure without requiring recovery demonstrations, retraining, or additional models at inference time. When predicted failure probability exceeds a threshold, the system pauses the policy, physically retraces the robot arm's recent motion, and resumes the unchanged policy from an earlier configuration. The approach was evaluated across multiple VLA architectures spanning different action-generation families on robotic manipulation benchmarks, finding that it meaningfully reduces failure rates on long-horizon tasks while having a smaller effect on shorter tasks where baseline success rates are already high. The failure prediction head adds only a negligible fraction to the total parameter count, making the method broadly applicable to frozen, pretrained policies without modification.
items.citation: Thomas Landeg, Thierry Tambe. If at First You Don't Succeed, Backtrack: Lightweight Recovery for Frozen VLAs. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Generating entanglement in quantum matter with pathway-entangled photons via resonant inelastic X-ray scattering
items.summary: This paper proposes a new use for resonant inelastic X-ray scattering, shifting its role from a probe of quantum materials to a tool for actively generating entanglement within them. The protocol splits an incident X-ray photon coherently across two arms of an interferometer, directing each arm to opposite ends of a solid-state sample, then recombines the scattered photons at a second beam splitter so that detecting an energy-selected photon heralds a coherent superposition of excitations at the two sample ends. This approach is framed as the X-ray solid-state analogue of the established DLCZ heralding scheme, analyzed using a Kramers-Heisenberg formalism with quantized photon modes. The authors demonstrate the mechanism across three model systems, showing that the protocol can generate heralded Bell states between decoupled sites, reveal reflection-parity-dependent interference in a tight-binding chain, and produce entangled fractionalized edge spins in a spin-1 Haldane chain. Practical challenges for experimental realization in X-ray settings are also discussed.
items.citation: Chunjing Jia, Valentin Walther, Laimei Nie. Generating entanglement in quantum matter with pathway-entangled photons via resonant inelastic X-ray scattering. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Trends of nucleic acid – based point-of-care diagnostics for infectious diseases
items.summary: This review examines the current landscape of nucleic acid-based point-of-care diagnostics for infectious diseases, motivated by the global need for decentralized, rapid, and accessible testing beyond conventional laboratory settings. The paper systematically surveys the three core operational stages of these diagnostic platforms: nucleic acid extraction, amplification, and detection. For extraction, it covers strategies including magnetic bead-based, paper-based, and integrated microfluidic approaches designed to remain simple and equipment-free. Amplification methods reviewed include both thermal cycling approaches such as polymerase chain reaction and isothermal alternatives such as loop-mediated isothermal amplification and recombinase polymerase amplification, all adapted for portable and low-power conditions. Detection platforms are described across a spectrum from colorimetric and fluorescent lateral flow assays to advanced biosensors employing CRISPR-based systems and toehold switch principles, which offer highly sensitive and programmable nucleic acid recognition.
items.citation: Hossam Hatem, Mohamed Mysara, Raghda Ramadan. Trends of nucleic acid – based point-of-care diagnostics for infectious diseases. Journal of Biological Engineering. 2026

items.title: Rapid and Sensitive Detection of <i>Schistosoma mansoni</i> in the Intermediate Snail Hosts Using Loop-Mediated Isothermal Amplification (LAMP) Diagnostics.
items.summary: The paper studied the detection of *Schistosoma mansoni* infections in intermediate snail hosts, which is critical for controlling schistosomiasis, a neglected tropical disease. The researchers developed a novel loop-mediated isothermal amplification assay targeting the mitochondrial NADH dehydrogenase subunit 1 gene of the parasite, optimizing it for use with infected *Biomphalaria* snails in both laboratory and field settings. The assay's performance was benchmarked against conventional parasitological methods, standard PCR, and real-time PCR using samples from laboratory infections as well as field collections from two African countries. In laboratory evaluations the assay achieved complete specificity and high sensitivity, outperforming microscopy, while in field surveys it identified a higher proportion of infected snails than conventional PCR, with microscopy failing to detect any positive individuals. The authors conclude that the assay is a sensitive, specific, and field-deployable diagnostic tool suitable for routine snail surveillance and early detection of changes in schistosomiasis transmission.
items.citation: Li HM, Qin ZQ, Lv S et al.. Rapid and Sensitive Detection of <i>Schistosoma mansoni</i> in the Intermediate Snail Hosts Using Loop-Mediated Isothermal Amplification (LAMP) Diagnostics.. Tropical medicine and infectious disease. 2026

items.title: Development of loop-mediated isothermal amplification and recombinase polymerase amplification combined with lateral flow dipstick assay for the rapid detection of salmon gill poxvirus.
items.summary: The paper addressed the need for rapid field diagnostics for Salmon gill poxvirus, a pathogen capable of causing high mortality in Atlantic salmon hatcheries where early intervention is critical. Researchers developed and evaluated two isothermal amplification methods, loop-mediated isothermal amplification and recombinase polymerase amplification, each paired with a lateral flow device to enable visual detection of the virus from gill mucus samples. Both assays showed high specificity and no cross-reactivity with common co-occurring gill pathogens when tested against purified DNA, and both agreed well with a reference real-time PCR method under those conditions. However, the recombinase polymerase amplification approach was consistently inhibited by crude gill mucus, making it unsuitable for direct field use, whereas the loop-mediated isothermal amplification assay performed reliably on unextracted gill mucus, successfully detecting the virus in the large majority of field samples tested. The loop-mediated isothermal amplification combined with lateral flow detection was concluded to be a practical, non-invasive diagnostic platform capable of delivering results within approximately an hour, offering strong potential for early outbreak detection and improved disease management in salmon aquaculture.
items.citation: Sun B, Weli SC, Dale OB et al.. Development of loop-mediated isothermal amplification and recombinase polymerase amplification combined with lateral flow dipstick assay for the rapid detection of salmon gill poxvirus.. Journal of virological methods. 2026

items.title: Numerical study of the ITER divertor plasma with the B2-EIRENE code package
items.summary: The abstract is too thin to summarize, as it contains only a bibliographic reference and a note about corrections rather than any scientific content about the study's methods, scope, or findings.
items.citation: V. Kotov. Numerical study of the ITER divertor plasma with the B2-EIRENE code package. Dokumentenrepositorium der RUB (Ruhr University Bochum). 2026

items.title: Hantavirus Emergence in a Changing World: Virology, Pathogenesis, Surveillance, and One Health Preparedness
items.summary: This review examines hantaviruses as emerging rodent-borne pathogens responsible for two serious disease syndromes associated with significant illness and death globally. The authors synthesize current knowledge spanning viral biology, disease mechanisms, clinical presentation, diagnostics, and epidemiology, with particular attention to how climate change, urbanization, and ecological disruption alter rodent reservoir populations and increase the risk of spillover to humans. The review identifies critical surveillance and diagnostic gaps in tropical and Caribbean regions where hantavirus transmission may be substantially underdetected. Advances discussed include molecular and genomic diagnostic tools, vaccine candidates, monoclonal antibody therapies, and climate-informed early warning systems. The authors conclude that integrated One Health surveillance frameworks combining human, animal, and environmental monitoring, alongside strengthened laboratory capacity and regional collaboration, are essential for reducing the global burden of hantavirus disease and improving preparedness for future zoonotic threats.
items.citation: Maria E. Ramos‐Niño, Nicolette Chiem, Prakash V. A. K. Ramdass. Hantavirus Emergence in a Changing World: Virology, Pathogenesis, Surveillance, and One Health Preparedness. Microorganisms. 2026

items.title: The analysis of natural gemstones and their synthetic counterparts using analytical spectroscopy methods
items.summary: This study examined the use of Raman spectroscopy to distinguish natural gemstones from their laboratory-grown synthetic counterparts, focusing on ruby, sapphire, emerald, and spinel in the context of growing challenges to gemstone authentication. The researchers evaluated both a laboratory Raman spectrometer equipped with two different laser wavelengths and a portable Raman system, applying these tools to identify gems produced by different manufacturing methods and to determine their geographic or synthetic origin. The laboratory instrument successfully differentiated natural from synthetic gemstones and could determine the origin of gems of the same colour, with emerald analysis requiring the shorter wavelength laser specifically. The portable system could distinguish between different stone types but lacked the sensitivity needed to separate natural from synthetic specimens. Overall, Raman spectroscopy was confirmed as a reliable, non-destructive analytical approach for gemological identification, with results consistently matching reference values within an accepted wavenumber tolerance.
items.citation: Raabell Shah. The analysis of natural gemstones and their synthetic counterparts using analytical spectroscopy methods. Research Output (Edinburgh Napier University). 2026

items.title: Viral metagenomics of synanthropic urban bats: A surveillance strategy for uncovering potentially zoonotic viruses
items.summary: This study investigated the viral diversity harbored by synanthropic urban bats in Brazil as a means of identifying potential zoonotic threats to public health. The researchers developed a framework that integrated existing rabies passive surveillance infrastructure with nanopore metagenomic sequencing, using a selection algorithm to choose representative specimens from thousands of collected bats, with paired lung and intestine samples submitted for analysis. The sequencing effort detected viral genetic material spanning multiple families of public health concern, including those containing coronaviruses, arenaviruses, and paramyxoviruses, and notably uncovered a previously unknown filovirus in bats from the Americas. These findings demonstrate that existing animal surveillance systems can be repurposed to reveal undetected viral diversity and serve as an early warning mechanism for emerging pathogens. The framework was further validated by multisectoral One Health experts as a scalable and cost-effective model suitable for national expansion and adaptation in low- and middle-income countries.
items.citation: Juliana Amorim Conselheiro, Filipe Romero Rebello Moreira, Gisely Toledo Barone et al.. Viral metagenomics of synanthropic urban bats: A surveillance strategy for uncovering potentially zoonotic viruses. One Health. 2026

items.title: A Review on Artificial Intelligence Methods for Plant Disease and Pest Detection
items.summary: This review examines the application of artificial intelligence methods to the detection of plant diseases and pests in agricultural settings. The authors systematically surveyed existing literature across different sensing modalities, learning paradigms, and deployment scales, distinguishing among population-level pest monitoring, plant-level visual inspection, and field-scale surveillance, as well as between post-symptomatic and pre-symptomatic detection approaches. Beyond cataloguing recent advances, the review critically evaluates fundamental limitations including data scarcity, domain shift, poor generalization under real field conditions, and the difficulty of separating biotic from abiotic stress signals. The authors also highlight the distinction between correlation-based AI predictions and genuine causal understanding of disease processes, arguing that AI should serve as a complementary decision-support tool rather than a replacement for established diagnostic methods. Looking forward, the review identifies multimodal sensor fusion, explainable AI, edge deployment for real-time monitoring, and foundation models for unified agricultural intelligence as priority directions for future research.
items.citation: Nikolaos Giakoumoglou, Dimitrios Kapetas, Kleanthis Marios Papadopoulos et al.. A Review on Artificial Intelligence Methods for Plant Disease and Pest Detection. AI and Precision Agriculture. 2026

items.title: A probabilistic approach to separate mergers and jellyfish galaxies: Application of morphological non-parametric indexes to the DESI Legacy Survey
items.summary: This study investigates how non-parametric morphological indices can be used to classify galaxies into distinct categories—regular spirals, regular ellipticals, mergers, and jellyfish galaxies (ram-pressure-stripping candidates)—using imaging data from the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys. The researchers measured ten non-parametric morphological indices and evaluated their discriminatory power using two-dimensional diagnostic planes assessed with a Bayesian kernel-density classifier, as well as a multi-index machine learning approach using calibrated gradient boosting models. They found that combinations of Shannon entropy with asymmetry or the moment-of-light statistic were most informative for separating regular from disturbed galaxies, while distinguishing mergers from jellyfish candidates proved more difficult, with concentration-based plane combinations performing best in two dimensions. The full multi-index model achieved substantially higher accuracy for the three-class problem than for the four-class problem, and the results revealed that jellyfish candidates occupy a relatively coherent region of morphological parameter space whereas mergers span diverse, overlapping morphologies. The study delivers probabilistic classifications for nearly two million galaxies, demonstrating that non-parametric morphology reliably identifies structural disturbance broadly but struggles to pinpoint its physical origin.
items.citation: V. M. Sampaio, Y. Jaff'e, A. Moretti et al.. A probabilistic approach to separate mergers and jellyfish galaxies: Application of morphological non-parametric indexes to the DESI Legacy Survey. arXiv. 2026

items.title: CO2-Induced Shifts in the Confined Phase Transformation of CH4 in Metal-Organic Frameworks
items.summary: This paper investigated how the presence of carbon dioxide affects the phase-like adsorption transformation of methane confined within two rigid metal-organic frameworks, IRMOF-1 and IRMOF-8. The researchers employed Transition-Matrix Monte Carlo simulations across a range of pre-loaded carbon dioxide concentrations to probe changes in the methane adsorption isotherm. While carbon dioxide reduced the maximum methane uptake due to competition for pore space, it also shifted the sharp discontinuity in methane adsorption to substantially lower pressures, promoting the high-density methane phase under milder conditions. This effect was attributed to carbon dioxide altering both fluid-fluid and fluid-framework interactions, thereby reshaping the thermodynamic landscape governing confined methane. The findings establish carbon dioxide as a thermodynamic modifier of confined methane behavior and suggest that controlled co-adsorption could serve as a strategy for tuning adsorption transformations in nanoporous materials for storage and separation applications.
items.citation: Anthony Dorhauer, Bartosz Mazur, Bogdan Kuchta et al.. CO2-Induced Shifts in the Confined Phase Transformation of CH4 in Metal-Organic Frameworks. arXiv. 2026

items.title: What Mean Error Misses: Device-Clock Diagnostics for Evaluating Eye Tracking across Three Virtual Reality Headsets
items.summary: This paper evaluated the accuracy and reliability of eye tracking across three virtual reality headsets by having participants complete identical gaze protocols on each device. The study assessed spatial accuracy, temporal data quality, and validity flagging through tasks including random saccades and instructed eye closures. While mean gaze error differed across headsets and was sensitive to factors like background luminance, the authors found that this common metric conceals important device-specific problems, such as lengthy data pauses, skipped samples, and autocorrelated gaze signals. Critically, one headset continued to flag gaze samples as valid during deliberate eye closures even as recorded gaze position shifted substantially, revealing a failure of validity reporting. The authors argue that evaluations of eye trackers should move beyond mean error alone and systematically report repeated timestamps, the composition of data loss on the device clock, and the behavior of validity flags during eye closures.
items.citation: Aleksandr Chernysh, Mehedi Hasan Raju, Kamrul Hasan et al.. What Mean Error Misses: Device-Clock Diagnostics for Evaluating Eye Tracking across Three Virtual Reality Headsets. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Multimodal Generative AI Assists Comprehensive Echocardiographic Interpretation
items.summary: This paper introduces EchoChat, a generative multimodal vision-language model designed to perform comprehensive echocardiographic analysis and support clinician interpretation. The system was trained on echocardiography-instruction pairs from tens of thousands of examinations and incorporates a chain-of-thought reasoning mechanism intended to emulate the cognitive workflow of a cardiologist, grounding its conclusions in visual evidence. Evaluated across cohorts from six international medical centers, EchoChat achieved state-of-the-art performance across a broad range of cardiac conditions and quantitative measurements, outperforming existing foundation models in both condition recognition and cardiac quantification on shared tasks. In a blinded reader study, echocardiography reports co-generated with EchoChat were rated higher in diagnostic accuracy and completeness by senior echocardiographers, and substantially improved diagnostic performance compared to routine reader-only reports. The authors conclude that embedding clinical reasoning into multimodal AI has the potential to democratize specialist expertise and improve the standard of cardiovascular care globally.
items.citation: Yi Qin, Marawan Elbatel, Shanshan Song et al.. Multimodal Generative AI Assists Comprehensive Echocardiographic Interpretation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Physics Informed Neural Network for Multi-dimensional Turbulent Self-gravitating Flows
items.summary: This paper investigated whether Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) could accurately model the complex, multi-scale dynamics of isothermal molecular clouds governed by the interplay of turbulence, self-gravity, and gas pressure. The authors applied PINNs to astrophysically motivated turbulent velocity fields in both two and three dimensions, covering subsonic and supersonic regimes across multiple turbulent realizations. The predicted density and velocity fields were benchmarked against solutions from the established finite-volume code Athena++. PINNs were found to accurately recover the global flow evolution over multiple free-fall times, while their training cost showed only weak dependence on spatial resolution. The results demonstrate that PINNs offer a viable, mesh-free complementary framework for simulating realistic self-gravitating turbulent flows at substantially greater complexity than previously demonstrated.
items.citation: Tirthankar De, Sayantan Auddy, Ramit Dey et al.. Physics Informed Neural Network for Multi-dimensional Turbulent Self-gravitating Flows. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Floquet Engineering of Momentum Gaps in Magnonic Time Crystals: Slow-Drive Amplification and In-Gap Propagation
items.summary: This paper establishes the magnonic analog of photonic time crystals by studying spin waves in a thin magnetic film whose anisotropy is periodically switched in time. The authors derive the Floquet band structure of this system, confirming it through micromagnetic simulations, and show that momentum gaps — regions where waves grow exponentially but cannot propagate — require a contrast in precession ellipticity to form. They demonstrate that the shape of the switching waveform governs which higher-order gaps open, with a square-wave drive amplifying a broad comb of spin-wave bands above Gilbert damping losses even when switching edges are smoothed, unlike sinusoidal modulation. Additionally, when the Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction is present, spin-wave packets can propagate within the gap while simultaneously growing in amplitude. These findings extend time-crystal physics into magnonics and suggest a route to broadband spin-wave amplification through Floquet engineering.
items.citation: Paweł Gruszecki, Victor Pacheco-Peña. Floquet Engineering of Momentum Gaps in Magnonic Time Crystals: Slow-Drive Amplification and In-Gap Propagation. arXiv. 2026
