items.title: Mechanism-informed diagnostic accuracy of blood biomarkers for sepsis-associated encephalopathy: a systematic review and Bayesian diagnostic network meta-analysis.
items.summary: This systematic review investigated the diagnostic accuracy of blood biomarkers for sepsis-associated encephalopathy, a serious form of acute brain dysfunction occurring in sepsis patients. The researchers conducted a PRISMA-compliant systematic review combined with a Bayesian diagnostic network meta-analysis, searching multiple international databases and synthesizing evidence from studies that provided extractable diagnostic data, with attention to how biomarker sampling timing and case definition heterogeneity influenced results. Biomarkers were organized along a mechanistic immune-to-neuronal axis spanning innate immune activation, blood-brain barrier dysfunction, glial response, and neuronal injury. Blood-brain barrier and glial markers such as GFAP and S100β demonstrated more balanced diagnostic discrimination than classic neuronal injury markers, while upstream immune candidates and day-three S100β ranked highest in Bayesian comparative analysis, though many top-ranked biomarkers were supported by only single studies. The authors conclude that findings are hypothesis-generating rather than practice-changing, emphasizing the need for prospective head-to-head validation under standardized phenotyping and anchor-based sampling protocols to determine whether mechanism-staged biomarker panels provide incremental diagnostic value beyond established clinical predictors.
items.citation: Zhang Q, Zhu R, Li Y et al.. Mechanism-informed diagnostic accuracy of blood biomarkers for sepsis-associated encephalopathy: a systematic review and Bayesian diagnostic network meta-analysis.. Frontiers in molecular neuroscience. 2026

items.title: Dynamic Changes of Neutrophil Nuclear Membrane CD63 as a Potential Biomarker for Early Adjunctive Diagnosis and Prognostic Evaluation of Sepsis in Critically Ill Patients: A Prospective Cohort Study.
items.summary: This study investigated whether neutrophil nuclear membrane CD63 (nmCD63), a marker of targeted nuclear degranulation during neutrophil extracellular trap formation, could serve as an early biomarker for sepsis diagnosis and prognosis in critically ill patients. The researchers developed a flow cytometry assay to quantify nmCD63 and validated it in a two-center prospective cohort with strict external validation, enrolling a combined total of participants split between derivation and validation cohorts. They found that nmCD63 levels rose progressively with disease severity, outperformed established inflammatory markers such as C-reactive protein and procalcitonin in distinguishing infectious from non-infectious systemic inflammation, and achieved strong diagnostic accuracy for identifying sepsis when combined with organ failure scoring. Critically, dynamic changes in nmCD63 preceded shifts in all conventional biomarkers, and trajectories measured over seven days enabled reliable stratification of patient prognosis. The study concludes that nmCD63 has dual diagnostic and prognostic utility, translating a specific early pathogenic mechanism into a clinically practical sepsis biomarker.
items.citation: Gao X, Zhang M, Li L et al.. Dynamic Changes of Neutrophil Nuclear Membrane CD63 as a Potential Biomarker for Early Adjunctive Diagnosis and Prognostic Evaluation of Sepsis in Critically Ill Patients: A Prospective Cohort Study.. MedComm. 2026

items.title: Clinical utility of combined serum IL-6, PCT, and SAA assays for early diagnosis and severity stratification of neonatal sepsis.
items.summary: This study investigated whether combining three serum biomarkers—interleukin-6 (IL-6), procalcitonin (PCT), and serum amyloid A (SAA)—could improve early diagnosis and severity stratification of neonatal sepsis compared to using any single marker alone. Neonates admitted to a neonatal intensive care unit were enrolled and divided into confirmed sepsis, suspected sepsis, and non-infective control groups, with sepsis patients further classified by disease severity; all biomarkers were measured at admission before antibiotic therapy. Each individual marker showed significantly elevated levels in confirmed sepsis and in severe disease, and all three demonstrated strong discriminatory power on receiver operating characteristic analysis. The combined three-marker panel outperformed any individual biomarker, achieving superior sensitivity and specificity for diagnosing confirmed sepsis, and all markers correlated positively with severity scores. The authors conclude that simultaneous measurement of IL-6, PCT, and SAA substantially enhances early diagnostic accuracy and severity grading in neonatal sepsis, offering a rapid and minimally invasive complement to blood culture in intensive care settings.
items.citation: Jiang Y, Yang J, Yang S. Clinical utility of combined serum IL-6, PCT, and SAA assays for early diagnosis and severity stratification of neonatal sepsis.. Frontiers in medicine. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic utility of the modified inflammatory burden index and PCT/LYM ratio for sepsis stratification and early prediction of septic shock.
items.summary: This study examined whether a modified inflammatory burden index and the procalcitonin-to-lymphocyte ratio could improve early diagnosis and risk stratification of sepsis and septic shock compared with conventional single biomarkers. Using a retrospective cohort of patients with septic shock, sepsis, and non-septic infectious inflammation as controls, the researchers measured standard inflammatory markers and calculated several composite indices, then evaluated their diagnostic performance individually and in combination through multivariable logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic analyses. Both the modified inflammatory burden index and the PCT/LYM ratio increased progressively from controls through sepsis to septic shock, while lymphocyte counts fell correspondingly, and both composite indices demonstrated diagnostic accuracy comparable to established markers such as procalcitonin and interleukin-6. The PCT/LYM ratio was an independent predictor of sepsis, and the modified inflammatory burden index retained independent predictive capacity for both sepsis and septic shock after adjustment for clinical confounders. The authors conclude that integrating these routinely available, cost-effective composite indices into a combined screening framework offers advantages over single biomarkers for timely sepsis identification and severity stratification.
items.venue: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
items.citation: Ding ZZ, Li Q, Ma CY et al.. Diagnostic utility of the modified inflammatory burden index and PCT/LYM ratio for sepsis stratification and early prediction of septic shock.. Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology. 2026

items.title: Gut microbial-derived metabolites: key players in kidney disease and renal fibrosis
items.summary: This review examines the relationship between gut microbial-derived metabolites and kidney disease, focusing on how disruptions to the gut microbiome contribute to renal injury and fibrosis. The paper synthesizes current evidence showing that kidney disease leads to intestinal barrier dysfunction and microbial dysbiosis, which in turn reduces beneficial short-chain fatty acids such as acetate, butyrate, and propionate while promoting excessive accumulation of uremic toxins including indoxyl sulfate and trimethylamine-N-oxide. These metabolic alterations influence renal pathology through multiple signaling pathways, with tryptophan metabolites highlighted as particularly central to gut-kidney communication. The review covers the role of these metabolites across several forms of kidney disease, including acute kidney injury, diabetic kidney disease, and immunoglobulin A nephropathy, elucidating the underlying pathophysiological mechanisms. The authors also survey therapeutic strategies targeting gut dysbiosis, including natural products, prebiotics, probiotics, and renal replacement therapy, with the aim of identifying targets for more precise treatment approaches.
items.citation: Wan-Ying Zhang, Yu-Lu Zhang, Qing-Qing Yu et al.. Gut microbial-derived metabolites: key players in kidney disease and renal fibrosis. International Journal of Biological Sciences. 2026

items.title: A systematic literature review on the effects of exercise on human Toll-like receptor expression
items.summary: This systematic review examined how different forms and durations of exercise affect the expression of Toll-like receptors (TLRs), transmembrane pattern recognition receptors that play a central role in orchestrating inflammatory immune responses and have been implicated in chronic low-grade inflammation associated with sedentary lifestyles and non-communicable diseases. The authors searched multiple major databases for human studies using exercise as an isolated intervention, ultimately including dozens of articles categorized by exercise modality and duration, spanning acute and chronic resistance, aerobic, and combined training. Acute resistance exercise tended to upregulate TLR expression, while acute aerobic exercise showed a more neutral or downregulatory effect, particularly in healthy individuals. Chronic resistance and combined training programs predominantly resulted in unchanged or decreased TLR levels, whereas chronic aerobic training produced mixed results with most measurements showing no significant change. The authors conclude that exercise does interact with TLR signalling in a manner dependent on exercise characteristics, but highlight substantial heterogeneity across study designs and call for further research to clarify the underlying mechanisms and pathophysiological implications.
items.citation: Kasper Favere, Matthias Bosman, Peter Delputte et al.. A systematic literature review on the effects of exercise on human Toll-like receptor expression. PubMed. 2026

items.title: Federated Learning in Multimodal Healthcare Diagnostics: Privacy-Preserving AI for Biomedical Imaging, Electronic Health Records, Wearables, and Clinical Decision Support
items.summary: This review paper examines the application of federated learning as a privacy-preserving approach to training artificial intelligence models across diverse multimodal healthcare data sources, including biomedical imaging modalities, electronic health records, wearable sensor outputs, and clinical decision support systems. Rather than centralizing sensitive patient data, federated learning allows institutions to train models locally and share only model updates, thereby reducing regulatory and privacy concerns associated with conventional centralized AI pipelines. The authors conducted a broad literature review spanning multiple clinical domains, including chronic disease management, elder care, and physiological signal analysis, to assess both the successes and limitations of this approach. They highlight that while federated learning reduces direct exposure of raw patient data, privacy is not guaranteed without additional safeguards against threats such as gradient leakage, model inversion, and membership inference attacks, and that practical barriers including system heterogeneity, data imbalance, communication bottlenecks, and fairness concerns remain significant. The review concludes with actionable recommendations directed at regulators, developers, and healthcare systems to guide the development of safe, equitable, and geographically distributed federated learning implementations in medicine.
items.venue: Archives of Computational Methods in Engineering
items.citation: Shon G. Nemane, Vaishnavi M. Sarad, Dhiraj P. Tulaskar et al.. Federated Learning in Multimodal Healthcare Diagnostics: Privacy-Preserving AI for Biomedical Imaging, Electronic Health Records, Wearables, and Clinical Decision Support. Archives of Computational Methods in Engineering. 2026

items.title: Stimuli-responsive nanocarriers for precision targeted and controlled antimicrobial drug delivery in drug-resistant infections
items.summary: This review examines stimuli-responsive nanocarriers as a strategy to overcome the limitations of conventional antibiotics, which fail to maintain therapeutic concentrations at infection sites and contribute to antimicrobial resistance through indiscriminate systemic distribution. The authors analyze how infected tissues present distinct microenvironmental features—such as acidic pH, elevated reactive oxygen species, pathogen-associated enzymatic activity, and hypoxia—that can serve as triggers for targeted drug release. The review systematically evaluates the mechanistic basis of pH-, enzyme-, redox-, and multi-stimuli-responsive nanocarrier systems, focusing on how triggered physicochemical changes control drug retention, activation, and release specifically within drug-resistant infection sites. The authors compare these systems against passive nanocarriers and free antibiotics to assess conditions under which infection-synchronized delivery improves efficacy, reduces off-target toxicity, and limits selective pressure for resistance, while also addressing resistance-associated barriers including biofilm tolerance, intracellular pathogen persistence, and enzymatic antibiotic degradation. The review concludes by identifying translational obstacles—including microenvironmental heterogeneity, trigger variability, manufacturing scalability, and regulatory complexity—framing stimuli-responsive nanocarriers as a context-aware alternative to conventional antibiotic therapy that may help address antimicrobial resistance beyond the capacity of traditional drug discovery.
items.citation: Li Dai, Xiaoyan Sun. Stimuli-responsive nanocarriers for precision targeted and controlled antimicrobial drug delivery in drug-resistant infections. Frontiers in Microbiology. 2026

items.title: The Gut–Vagina Axis
items.summary: This review paper examines the emerging concept of the gut–vagina axis, which describes bidirectional communication between the gut and vaginal microbiomes in relation to female health. The authors synthesize recent advances in microbiome research to outline the key mechanisms through which these two sites may interact, including microbial migration, hormonal and immune regulation, and metabolite exchange. The review highlights how the composition of microbial communities at one site may influence the other, with downstream consequences for immune responses, hormonal balance, and metabolic activity. The authors argue that these interactions have implications for both local and systemic health outcomes in women.
items.citation: Lorenzo Agoni, Elena Roselletti, Giovanni Marasco et al.. The Gut–Vagina Axis. Microorganisms. 2026

items.title: Current status and future perspectives on the mechanistic and pathophysiological understanding of long COVID
items.summary: This review examines the current state of scientific understanding of Long COVID, the post-acute sequelae that persist following SARS-CoV-2 infection and affect hundreds of millions of people worldwide at enormous economic cost. The authors synthesized existing evidence on the biological mechanisms proposed to underlie the condition, including immune dysregulation, viral persistence, autonomic dysfunction, and microvascular pathology, while also evaluating contemporary diagnostic approaches and available treatment strategies. The review highlights that Long COVID presents as a highly heterogeneous syndrome encompassing cognitive dysfunction, severe fatigue, sleep disturbances, and post-exertional malaise, among other debilitating symptoms. Despite the scale of the problem, the authors identify substantial gaps in mechanistic understanding, the absence of validated diagnostic criteria, and a lack of rigorously evaluated therapeutic options as major obstacles to clinical consensus. They conclude that interdisciplinary research efforts are urgently needed to achieve mechanistic clarity and develop evidence-based management strategies to reduce the long-term global health burden of the condition.
items.citation: Mark A. Faghy, Rob C. I. Wüst, Daniel Martin Altmann et al.. Current status and future perspectives on the mechanistic and pathophysiological understanding of long COVID. Communications Medicine. 2026

items.title: SEMAC: Spherical Energy Matching Ambisonics Codec for Efficient Higher-Order Ambisonics Compression
items.summary: The paper addresses the challenge of efficiently compressing Higher-Order Ambisonics audio, a format used for immersive spatial audio that becomes increasingly costly to transmit as channel count grows quadratically with spherical harmonic order. The authors developed SEMAC, a codec that encodes a quantized directional energy envelope at full spherical harmonic order alongside a reduced number of transport channels coded at lower dimensionality, then reconstructs the full-order directional energy distribution at the decoder by re-imposing the captured envelope. This approach generalizes the per-band energy separation principle already used in the CELT codec to the spatial domain of directional signals. Perceptual evaluation using a MUSHRA listening test on fifth-order material showed that SEMAC using roughly half the transport channels outperformed the standard Opus Channel Mapping Family approach at matched bitrates, and also outperformed simple order truncation when using the same number of transport channels. The results indicate that transmitting fewer channels with an accurate directional energy envelope is perceptually superior to transmitting all channels at reduced precision.
items.citation: Christoph Hold, Jan Buethe, Jean-Marc Valin et al.. SEMAC: Spherical Energy Matching Ambisonics Codec for Efficient Higher-Order Ambisonics Compression. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Comprehensive Visible and Near-infrared Keck and Gemini Monitoring and Characterization of Interstellar Comet 3I/ATLAS during its Encounter with the Solar System
items.summary: This paper presents an extensive observational campaign monitoring interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS across visible and near-infrared wavelengths using multiple large ground-based telescopes, covering the object's passage through the inner Solar System from shortly after discovery through several months past perihelion. The study measured optical colors, dust activity levels, coma morphology, gas emission ratios, and near-infrared spectral properties at numerous epochs spanning this encounter. The comet's optical colors remained stable across perihelion, while its dust activity declined more steeply after perihelion passage than before, and coma structure evolved from a compact concentrated morphology to a more extended distribution. Molecular abundance ratios shifted over time, with the ratio of certain carbon-bearing species changing measurably around perihelion, and near-infrared spectroscopy revealed no robust evidence for water-ice absorption features. The authors present these observations as a comprehensive baseline record of an interstellar body's behavior during Solar System passage, intended to serve as a reference for understanding and comparing future interstellar object encounters.
items.citation: Bryce T. Bolin, Jeffrey Cooke, Brian C. Lemaux et al.. Comprehensive Visible and Near-infrared Keck and Gemini Monitoring and Characterization of Interstellar Comet 3I/ATLAS during its Encounter with the Solar System. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Shared clones make random cell halves look reproducible in pooled screens
items.summary: This paper investigated a methodological flaw in single-cell perturbation screens used to benchmark computational models of gene perturbation effects. In pooled screens like Perturb-seq, cells carrying the same guide RNA share common clonal ancestry from a limited number of transduced progenitors, meaning that randomly splitting these cells into two halves for reproducibility assessment produces pseudoreplicates rather than independent replicates. By using perturbations expected to have no effect as controls and comparing random cell halves against independently transduced replicates, the authors demonstrated that clonal sharing causes random halves to appear far more reproducible than they truly are, with null perturbations agreeing between random halves nearly universally but only at noise-expected rates between genuine replicates. The degree of inflation varied substantially across experimental systems, being most severe in primary T cells and least problematic in non-dividing neurons, and could be largely eliminated by splitting cells into halves that share no clonal lineage. As a consequence, published models predicting perturbation effects in new cell states appeared superior to baseline when evaluated within a single transduction but performed below baseline when tested against cells from an independent transduction, leading the authors to argue that reproducibility must be assessed across separate transductions.
items.citation: Xuanrui Huang. Shared clones make random cell halves look reproducible in pooled screens. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A probabilistic approach to separate mergers and jellyfish galaxies: Application of morphological non-parametric indexes to the DESI Legacy Survey
items.summary: This paper investigates how non-parametric morphological indices can classify galaxies into regular spirals, regular ellipticals, mergers, and jellyfish galaxies (ram-pressure stripping candidates) using imaging from the DESI Legacy Surveys. The researchers measured ten non-parametric morphological indices and evaluated their discriminating power through two-dimensional diagnostic planes using a Bayesian kernel-density classifier, then combined all indices with probability-calibrated gradient boosting models. They found that planes combining Shannon entropy with asymmetry or concentration indices performed best for separating regular from disturbed galaxies, while distinguishing mergers from jellyfish candidates proved more difficult due to the diverse and overlapping morphologies of mergers compared to the relatively coherent parameter-space region occupied by jellyfish candidates. The multi-class machine learning model achieved strong performance for three-class separation but was more limited for the four-class problem, and the work delivers probabilistic classifications for nearly two million galaxies. Overall, the study demonstrates that non-parametric morphology reliably identifies broad structural disturbance but struggles to pinpoint its physical origin, and that survey-specific probabilistic boundaries are necessary given the sensitivity of these diagnostics to image quality and preprocessing.
items.citation: V. M. Sampaio, Y. Jaff'e, A. Moretti et al.. A probabilistic approach to separate mergers and jellyfish galaxies: Application of morphological non-parametric indexes to the DESI Legacy Survey. arXiv. 2026

items.title: CoupleFlow: Null-Calibrated Auditory Attention Decoding With Time-Locked Brain-Speech Coupling and Flow-Matching Likelihood Ratios
items.summary: This paper addresses auditory attention decoding, the problem of identifying which talker a listener is attending to based on brief noninvasive brain recordings, and demonstrates that previously reported near-perfect accuracies are inflated by methodological artifacts such as trial leakage, eye gaze, and acoustic cues rather than genuine neural responses to speech. The authors introduce CoupleFlow, a method that decodes attention by measuring temporal coupling between neural and acoustic embeddings using a conditional flow matching head that implements a likelihood ratio decision rule based on pointwise mutual information, ensuring predictions fall to chance when no genuine brain-speech coupling is present. The system was evaluated across nine electroencephalography and magnetoencephalography datasets spanning multiple languages, recording modalities, listener populations including those with hearing impairment, and multi-talker environments, using content-disjoint data splits and null tests designed to distinguish real coupling from spurious trial recognition. CoupleFlow outperformed both linear and deep learning baselines while consistently passing null checks that prior methods fail. Additionally, the authors derived an evidence accumulation law that predicts decoding accuracy as a function of window length from a single dataset-specific parameter tied to the strength of neural speech tracking, identifying recording signal-to-noise ratio as a fundamental bottleneck on decoding speed and reliability.
items.citation: Ali Alavi, Donald S. Williamson. CoupleFlow: Null-Calibrated Auditory Attention Decoding With Time-Locked Brain-Speech Coupling and Flow-Matching Likelihood Ratios. arXiv. 2026

items.title: If at First You Don't Succeed, Backtrack: Lightweight Recovery for Frozen VLAs
items.summary: This paper addresses the brittleness of Vision-Language-Action models in robotic manipulation, specifically their tendency to fail when their own actions push them into states underrepresented in training data. The authors propose Backtrack, a lightweight mechanism that attaches a small failure prediction head to a frozen VLA, trained only on outcome-labeled rollouts without requiring additional demonstrations, policy retraining, or separate inference-time models. The failure prediction head reads the VLA's existing internal representations to estimate the probability of episode failure, and when this probability exceeds a threshold, a controller pauses execution, physically retraces the robot arm's recent motion, and returns control to the unchanged policy so it can retry from an earlier state. Evaluated across multiple VLA architectures spanning both flow-matching and autoregressive action-generation approaches, Backtrack substantially reduces failure rates on long-horizon manipulation tasks while adding negligible parameters to the base policy. The gains are most pronounced on difficult long-horizon tasks where baseline failure rates are high, with smaller but consistent improvements also observed on a separate manipulation benchmark.
items.citation: Thomas Landeg, Thierry Tambe. If at First You Don't Succeed, Backtrack: Lightweight Recovery for Frozen VLAs. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Rapid Diagnostics for Antimicrobial Resistance: From Bench to Bedside
items.citation: Mugisha N, Fawaz L, Noureddine R et al.. Artificial Intelligence in Rapid Diagnostics for Antimicrobial Resistance: From Bench to Bedside. Health science reports. 2026

items.title: Integrated evaluation of rapid diagnostic testing, genotypic-phenotypic resistance profiling, and AI-Assisted prediction models for antimicrobial stewardship and clinical outcomes in a resource-limited setting.
items.summary: This prospective observational study examined whether combining rapid diagnostic testing, molecular resistance gene profiling, and an artificial intelligence prediction model could improve antibiotic prescribing and patient outcomes in a resource-limited hospital setting. Researchers enrolled adult patients with suspected bacterial infections and compared outcomes between conventional antibiotic susceptibility testing and the integrated approach, measuring time to effective therapy, antibiotic appropriateness, hospital stay duration, and mortality. The integrated strategy dramatically shortened the time to pathogen identification and initiation of effective therapy compared with conventional methods, while substantially increasing appropriate antibiotic use and reducing reliance on broad-spectrum agents. Clinical outcomes also improved, with patients in the integrated arm experiencing shorter hospital stays and lower mortality, and the AI model demonstrated strong discriminatory performance for predicting resistance. The authors conclude that this combined diagnostic and predictive framework represents a scalable, cost-effective strategy for combating antimicrobial resistance, particularly in settings with limited resources.
items.citation: Hammad M, Arif R, Fardoos S et al.. Integrated evaluation of rapid diagnostic testing, genotypic-phenotypic resistance profiling, and AI-Assisted prediction models for antimicrobial stewardship and clinical outcomes in a resource-limited setting.. PloS one. 2026

items.title: Recent Advances and Future Perspectives in the Detection of Carbapenem-Resistant <i>Acinetobacter Baumannii</i>.
items.summary: This review examines the landscape of detection technologies for carbapenem-resistant *Acinetobacter baumannii*, a pathogen classified by the World Health Organization as a critical priority due to its multidrug resistance, nosocomial spread, and limited treatment options. The authors surveyed methods ranging from conventional phenotypic and antimicrobial susceptibility testing to molecular approaches, mass spectrometry, whole-genome and metagenomic sequencing, AI-assisted diagnostics, and biosensor or CRISPR-integrated platforms. Conventional culture-based testing remains the reference standard but is constrained by long turnaround times, whereas molecular methods such as PCR and isothermal amplification approaches substantially reduce time to result and show promise for point-of-care applications. Emerging genomic and AI-assisted tools offer comprehensive resistance profiling and outbreak surveillance capabilities, while biosensor platforms provide sensitivity and portability, though challenges around multiplexing, standardization, and clinical validation persist. The review concludes that CRAB diagnostics are shifting from culture-dependent methods toward integrated, automated platforms, and stresses the importance of balancing analytical performance, speed, cost, and point-of-care suitability.
items.citation: Ye Q, Liu Y, Zhang K et al.. Recent Advances and Future Perspectives in the Detection of Carbapenem-Resistant <i>Acinetobacter Baumannii</i>.. Infection and drug resistance. 2026

items.title: Economic Barriers to Antimicrobial Susceptibility Testing as a Structural Contributor to Antimicrobial Resistance in Low- and Middle-Income Countries: A Narrative Review.
items.summary: This narrative review examined how economic barriers to antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST) structurally drive antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). The authors conducted a systematic literature search across major databases, synthesizing evidence thematically according to established review guidelines. They identified that economic obstacles to AST operate simultaneously at the patient level, through out-of-pocket costs and transport burdens, at the laboratory level, through infrastructure deficits and reagent shortages, and at the health-system level, through chronic underinvestment and donor dependency. These compounding barriers sustain reliance on broad-spectrum empirical prescribing, which in turn accelerates the emergence of resistant pathogens including methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus, extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producing organisms, and carbapenem-resistant bacteria. The authors conclude that sustainable AMR control in LMICs requires nationally financed action plans that explicitly fund accessible, quality-assured AST alongside prescribing reform and integrated diagnostic stewardship.
items.citation: Abdi YH, Bashir SG, Ali SM. Economic Barriers to Antimicrobial Susceptibility Testing as a Structural Contributor to Antimicrobial Resistance in Low- and Middle-Income Countries: A Narrative Review.. Infection and drug resistance. 2026

items.title: Next-generation point-of-care diagnostics for urinary tract infections: a systematic review of rapid pathogen detection methods.
items.summary: This systematic review examined advances in point-of-care diagnostic technologies for the rapid detection of urinary tract infection pathogens and their antimicrobial susceptibility profiles, with the goal of addressing the delays inherent in conventional urine culture methods that take up to several days. The authors conducted a comprehensive literature search spanning nearly two decades, identifying studies describing the mechanisms, performance, and clinical applicability of emerging rapid diagnostic platforms. Technologies reviewed included paper-based assays, lateral-flow tests, microfluidic devices, hydrogel biosensors, and commercial molecular and phenotypic systems, which collectively demonstrated bacterial detection ranging from under five minutes to several hours across a wide range of bacterial concentrations. Among the evaluated platforms, a phenotypic antimicrobial susceptibility testing device achieved high specificity compared to standard microbiology within under an hour, while molecular systems enabled identification of uropathogens and resistance genes within roughly one to two and a half hours. The authors concluded that point-of-care diagnostics substantially reduce turnaround time and support antibiotic stewardship, identifying one phenotypic commercial system as the most clinically validated option and calling for broader panel development, clinical outcome validation, and integration into primary care settings.
items.citation: Juste-Alvarez S, Medina-Polo J. Next-generation point-of-care diagnostics for urinary tract infections: a systematic review of rapid pathogen detection methods.. GMS infectious diseases. 2026

items.title: Concordance of AI-driven antimicrobial recommendations using rapid molecular versus phenotypic-optimized workflows for bloodstream infections: a prospective study in a resource-limited setting
items.summary: This prospective study evaluated an integrated diagnostic-therapeutic program for bloodstream infections that combined rapid molecular diagnostics with an AI clinical decision support system for initial antimicrobial guidance, followed by conventional culture-based phenotypic susceptibility testing with AI optimization. Conducted in a resource-limited setting using consecutive monomicrobial bloodstream infection episodes, the approach aimed to quantify reductions in time to appropriate therapy and assess concordance between the molecular-AI and phenotypic-AI workflows. The molecular diagnostics substantially reduced diagnostic turnaround time compared to conventional methods, with high concordance for bacterial identification, substantial concordance for resistance detection, and moderate concordance for therapeutic recommendations between the two workflows. Resistance detection discordance emerged as the sole independent predictor of therapeutic discordance, while the phenotypic-AI optimization step ensured fully appropriate therapy in all cases. The authors conclude that this integrated strategy supports implementation in antimicrobial stewardship programs by delivering earlier appropriate therapy in the majority of cases while allowing phenotypic confirmation to correct residual discordances.
items.citation: Torre JCGdl, Frenkel A, Chavez-Lencinas C et al.. Concordance of AI-driven antimicrobial recommendations using rapid molecular versus phenotypic-optimized workflows for bloodstream infections: a prospective study in a resource-limited setting. 2026

items.title: Accelerating scientific discovery with Co-Scientist
items.summary: Co-Scientist is a multi-agent AI system built on Gemini that aims to accelerate scientific discovery by generating, critiquing, and refining novel research hypotheses conditioned on a researcher's objectives and existing scientific evidence. The system features an asynchronous task execution framework for flexible compute scaling and a tournament-based evolution process for iterative self-improvement of hypotheses, with automated evaluations demonstrating that hypothesis quality improves as test-time compute is increased. Although designed as a general-purpose tool, the system was validated across three biomedical domains: drug repurposing, novel-target discovery, and explaining mechanisms of antimicrobial resistance. Critically, hypotheses generated by Co-Scientist regarding new drug-repurposing candidates and synergistic combination therapies for acute myeloid leukaemia were confirmed through in vitro experiments, providing real-world evidence of the system's utility. The authors argue that these results demonstrate the potential for such AI systems to meaningfully augment scientific discovery and empower researchers to identify original knowledge.
items.citation: Juraj Gottweis, Wei‐Hung Weng, Alexander Daryin et al.. Accelerating scientific discovery with Co-Scientist. Nature. 2026

items.title: Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications
items.summary: This review examines how the integration of multiomics technologies and artificial intelligence is reshaping precision drug discovery and clinical translation. The authors synthesize how approaches spanning genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics generate deep molecular insights into disease mechanisms, while deep learning architectures unlock patterns within these complex datasets to build predictive models. The review covers the application of this combined framework across the drug development pipeline, including target identification, lead optimization, drug repositioning, de novo compound discovery, virtual screening, pharmacokinetic modeling, and safety assessment. Case applications in oncology, neurodegenerative diseases, and cardiovascular conditions are discussed to illustrate the translational potential of these converging technologies. The authors also acknowledge persistent challenges such as harmonizing disparate omics data, ensuring reproducibility, and reducing algorithmic bias, while arguing that overcoming these obstacles will usher in a new era of bench-to-clinic translational medicine.
items.citation: Yuqing Liu, Kun Zhu, Weijun Peng et al.. Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: Soil microbes are the tiny bioengineers running Earth’s underground factory
items.summary: This paper synthesizes current knowledge on soil microbial communities and their roles in driving key ecosystem processes, addressing the incomplete understanding of how microbial diversity translates into ecological function. The authors developed a function-centred framework built around four conserved functional axes — secondary metabolism, nutrient cycling, community interactions, and stress tolerance — drawing on studies spanning ecological, agricultural, and environmental contexts. They find that these functional axes collectively influence plant productivity, climate regulation, and pollutant transformation, though their expression is highly context dependent. The synthesis advances the concept of soil as a self-organizing system in which microbial interactions produce emergent ecosystem-level behaviour. The authors propose that this framework can underpin predictive, ecology-informed strategies for managing soils toward goals such as sustainable agriculture, environmental remediation, and climate mitigation.
items.citation: Suzanne Hassan-Dalléac, Wafa Guiga, Antonia Suau. Soil microbes are the tiny bioengineers running Earth’s underground factory. Communications Earth & Environment. 2026

items.title: Arc mediates intercellular tau transmission via extracellular vesicles
items.summary: The paper investigated the mechanisms by which misfolded tau protein spreads between cells, a process central to the progression of Alzheimer's disease and frontotemporal dementia. The researchers focused on the neuronal gene Arc, examining whether it plays a role in packaging tau into extracellular vesicles (EVs) and facilitating intercellular tau transmission using transgenic mouse models and human brain tissue. They found that Arc is essential for loading tau into EVs through a pathway involving the I-BAR protein IRSp53, and that Arc protein directly binds tau to form a complex identifiable in both mouse and human brain. When Arc was knocked out, EVs contained substantially less tau and lost the ability to seed tau aggregation, while pathological tau instead accumulated intracellularly in neurons and was associated with accelerated hippocampal neuron loss. The authors conclude that Arc-dependent packaging of tau into EVs serves a dual function, contributing both to the clearance of intracellular tau and to the cell-to-cell transmission of tau pathology.
items.citation: Mitali Tyagi, Eric de Hoog, Matthew Grega et al.. Arc mediates intercellular tau transmission via extracellular vesicles. Cell. 2026

items.title: Synthesis and multilevel evaluation of benzimidazole-based anticancer compounds: DNA/serum albumin interaction, and in-depth theoretical insights
items.summary: Two novel benzimidazole-based compounds were designed, synthesized, and evaluated for anticancer potential against multiple cancer cell lines alongside healthy cells. One compound demonstrated particularly potent cytotoxic activity against liver and breast cancer cell lines, and mechanistic studies using gene expression analysis revealed that both compounds shift the apoptotic balance by suppressing anti-apoptotic genes while elevating pro-apoptotic gene expression in breast cancer cells, alongside inducing oxidative stress, modulating antioxidant enzyme levels, and triggering cellular senescence. The compounds were shown through fluorescence spectroscopy to bind strongly to DNA via an intercalative mechanism and to interact with serum albumin with moderate affinity, suggesting favorable transport properties. Computational analyses including density functional theory calculations, reduced density gradient mapping, and molecular docking supported the experimental findings regarding reactivity and binding behavior. Collectively, the multilevel biological and theoretical evaluation positions these benzimidazole derivatives as promising candidates for further development as anticancer agents.
items.citation: Sevgi Kundu, Senem Akkoç, Yalçın Erzurumlu et al.. Synthesis and multilevel evaluation of benzimidazole-based anticancer compounds: DNA/serum albumin interaction, and in-depth theoretical insights. Molecular and Cellular Biochemistry. 2026

items.title: Delivering biomedicines with stimuli‑responsive biomaterials
items.summary: The abstract is too thin to summarize meaningfully beyond restating that the paper is a review of stimuli-responsive biomaterials as platforms for delivering biotherapeutics, covering design principles, material selection, architecture, functionalization, and classification of triggering stimuli.
items.citation: Hemant Singh, Zenab Darban, Aliakbar Ebrahimi et al.. Delivering biomedicines with stimuli‑responsive biomaterials. Communications Materials. 2026

items.title: A probabilistic approach to separate mergers and jellyfish galaxies: Application of morphological non-parametric indexes to the DESI Legacy Survey
items.summary: This paper investigates how non-parametric morphological measurements can be used to classify galaxies into distinct categories — regular spirals, regular ellipticals, merger systems, and jellyfish galaxies undergoing ram-pressure stripping — using imaging from the DESI Legacy Surveys. The authors measured ten non-parametric morphological indices and evaluated their discriminating power through two-dimensional diagnostic planes using a Bayesian kernel-density classifier, as well as through a multi-index machine learning approach using calibrated gradient-boosted models. They found that combining Shannon entropy with asymmetry or concentration indices provides the most informative separations, with the multi-index models achieving substantially higher balanced accuracies than any single diagnostic plane alone. A key finding is that while non-parametric morphology reliably identifies broad structural disturbance, distinguishing its physical origin is more difficult: jellyfish candidates occupy a relatively compact and coherent region of morphological parameter space, whereas mergers display diverse and overlapping morphologies. The study delivers probabilistic classifications for over one million galaxies, along with survey-specific diagnostic boundaries that account for image quality and preprocessing effects.
items.citation: V. M. Sampaio, Y. Jaff'e, A. Moretti et al.. A probabilistic approach to separate mergers and jellyfish galaxies: Application of morphological non-parametric indexes to the DESI Legacy Survey. arXiv. 2026

items.title: What Mean Error Misses: Device-Clock Diagnostics for Evaluating Eye Tracking across Three Virtual Reality Headsets
items.summary: This paper evaluated the accuracy and reliability of eye tracking across three virtual reality headsets by having participants complete identical gaze protocols on each device. The study measured spatial accuracy using mean error in a random-saccade task, examined the effects of background luminance on tracking performance, and analyzed temporal data quality through device-clock diagnostics. Spatial accuracy varied substantially across headsets, with one device remaining the least accurate even after recalibration and another showing degraded performance under darker display conditions. Beyond mean error, the device-clock analysis revealed hidden data quality problems, including multi-second pauses on one headset, correlated samples indicating data smoothing on another, and invalid gaze flagged as valid during deliberate eye closures. The authors argue that standard spatial accuracy metrics alone are insufficient and recommend that evaluations additionally report repeated timestamps, the composition of data loss on the device clock, and validity flagging behavior during eye closures.
items.citation: Aleksandr Chernysh, Mehedi Hasan Raju, Kamrul Hasan et al.. What Mean Error Misses: Device-Clock Diagnostics for Evaluating Eye Tracking across Three Virtual Reality Headsets. arXiv. 2026

items.title: EVSEFuzz : A Tool for Automated Testing of Protocol Implementations
items.summary: This paper addresses security vulnerabilities in electric vehicle charging infrastructure, specifically targeting the communication protocols used between charging network operators and charging equipment. The authors developed EVSEFuzz, an automated fuzzing tool that leverages Python datatype validation packages to parse and understand message structures and datatypes within protocols such as the open charge point protocol. The tool generates both valid and malformed messages to probe protocol implementations for weaknesses, functioning across both open-source and closed-source software. Testing against multiple implementations revealed several vulnerabilities, resulting in the publication of two Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures entries.
items.citation: Soham Gumaste, Michael Khan, Roland Varriale et al.. EVSEFuzz : A Tool for Automated Testing of Protocol Implementations. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Multimodal Generative AI Assists Comprehensive Echocardiographic Interpretation
items.summary: This paper introduces EchoChat, a generative multimodal vision-language model designed to perform comprehensive echocardiographic analysis and support clinical interpretation of cardiac imaging. The system was trained on a large dataset of echocardiography-instruction pairs and incorporates a chain-of-thought reasoning mechanism intended to emulate the cognitive workflow of a cardiologist, grounding diagnostic conclusions in visual evidence rather than operating as an opaque black box. Evaluated across cohorts from multiple international medical centers, EchoChat achieved state-of-the-art performance on cardiac condition recognition and quantification, supporting diagnosis across a broad range of cardiac conditions and findings. In a blinded reader study, echocardiography reports co-generated with EchoChat were rated higher in diagnostic accuracy and completeness by senior echocardiographers and substantially improved diagnostic performance compared to reports produced by routine readers alone. The authors conclude that embedding clinical reasoning into multimodal AI can help address the global shortage of specialist interpreters and raise the standard of cardiovascular care.
items.citation: Yi Qin, Marawan Elbatel, Shanshan Song et al.. Multimodal Generative AI Assists Comprehensive Echocardiographic Interpretation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Ginzburg-Landau Theory with Elastic Incompatibility Describes the Liquid-G-phase-Crystal State Diagram
items.summary: This paper develops a mechanically consistent Ginzburg-Landau theory to explain the metastable heterogeneous G state observed in deeply undercooled metallic liquids. The central idea is that elastic incompatibility between ordered crystalline cores and the surrounding amorphous matrix generates frozen internal stresses, while non-affine deformation in the disordered matrix screens those stresses over a finite length scale analogous to the London penetration depth in superconductors. A second distinct length scale governs how structural order heals, and the ratio of these two lengths defines a structural analogue of the Ginzburg-Landau parameter, enabling type-II superconductor-like mixed-state physics to emerge in a purely structural context. The framework naturally accounts for the liquid-G-phase-crystal state diagram: slow cooling selects crystal, intermediate rates produce the heterogeneous G state with finite ordered cores whose coarsening is frustrated by residual incompatibility, and rapid quenching yields a homogeneous glass. The resulting microstructure is described as an inverted Abrikosov vortex lattice, where structural order resides in the cores rather than between them, and the theory proposes specific experimental and simulation tests involving stress decay, structural healing, and non-affine susceptibility measurements.
items.citation: Alessio Zaccone, Konrad Samwer. Ginzburg-Landau Theory with Elastic Incompatibility Describes the Liquid-G-phase-Crystal State Diagram. arXiv. 2026

items.title: AFRA: Age-Threshold Frame-Based Random Access for Timely Communication in Multi-Agent Systems
items.summary: This paper addresses the problem of maintaining timely information exchange among agents in multi-agent systems, such as mobile robots sharing a wireless channel, where collisions and slow protocol convergence can degrade information freshness. The authors propose a distributed medium access control protocol called age-threshold frame-based random access (AFRA), in which each agent monitors its own age of information and, upon reaching a specified threshold, initiates a local transmission frame with a mandatory first attempt followed by at most one additional attempt in a randomly chosen remaining slot. The protocol requires only local state information and acknowledgment feedback, making it practical for decentralized deployment. The authors prove that AFRA converges almost surely to collision-free periodic operation under a specified relationship between frame length, age threshold, and number of agents, and they derive closed-form expressions for steady-state throughput, average age of information, and average peak age of information. Simulations show that AFRA achieves rapid convergence at small age thresholds and lower window-averaged age of information compared to existing age-aware random access schemes.
items.citation: Jiedan Tan, Fang Liu. AFRA: Age-Threshold Frame-Based Random Access for Timely Communication in Multi-Agent Systems. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Molecular point-of-care: technological evolution, clinical applications, and future perspectives
items.citation: Zhang D, Cui X, Zhang R et al.. Molecular point-of-care: technological evolution, clinical applications, and future perspectives. Frontiers in bioengineering and biotechnology. 2026

items.title: Translational Barriers and AI-Driven Challenges of Microfluidics-Enabled Wearables and Implantable Systems in Personalized Medicine.
items.summary: This review examines the path from laboratory prototypes to clinical deployment for wearable and implantable microfluidic systems capable of continuously sampling biomarkers from sweat, saliva, tears, and interstitial fluid. Rather than addressing materials or fabrication in isolation, the authors construct an integrated, translation-focused framework spanning functional biomaterials, fabrication techniques, diagnostic performance benchmarking, and closed-loop theranostic platforms. The review systematically analyzes how microfluidic transport, multiplexed molecular analytics, and autonomous therapeutic integration together shift these devices from passive monitoring toward adaptive intervention. A particular focus is placed on artificial intelligence integration across three pathways—sensor self-calibration, multiplexed molecular decoding, and on-device autonomous decision-making—while also critically interrogating how biofluid data heterogeneity and population baseline disparities can propagate algorithmic bias. The authors conclude that robust hardware interfaces, standardized validation benchmarks, and alignment with emerging regulatory frameworks are essential prerequisites for equitable and responsible clinical translation of these personalized medicine technologies.
items.citation: Huang K, Fong CY, Huang X et al.. Translational Barriers and AI-Driven Challenges of Microfluidics-Enabled Wearables and Implantable Systems in Personalized Medicine.. Advanced science (Weinheim, Baden-Wurttemberg, Germany). 2026

items.title: Finger-actuated microfluidic device for point-of-care circulating cell-free nucleic acid extraction.
items.summary: This paper developed a fully finger-actuated microfluidic device designed to extract cell-free nucleic acids from plasma without requiring external power or laboratory pipetting equipment, addressing a critical bottleneck in point-of-care molecular diagnostics. The device integrates manual valves, a finger-driven pump, and on-board blister packs storing all necessary reagents to complete a full sample-to-eluate workflow—including lysis, binding, washing, and elution—in approximately half an hour. Performance was benchmarked against both a manual benchtop magnetic bead protocol and an automated robotic system using DNA-spiked aqueous samples and human pooled plasma, with the device achieving extraction recoveries comparable or superior to the bench method, particularly at lower input plasma volumes. Clinical utility was demonstrated by successfully extracting and amplifying viral nucleic acids from patient samples positive for three different pathogens, with quantification cycle values closely matching those from standard protocols. The authors propose that this instrument-free extraction tool could serve as a practical bridge between lateral flow amplification technologies and decentralised diagnostics in resource-limited settings.
items.citation: Musaddaq G, Ehsan L, Yoga Y et al.. Finger-actuated microfluidic device for point-of-care circulating cell-free nucleic acid extraction.. Lab on a chip. 2026

items.title: Soil microbes are the tiny bioengineers running Earth’s underground factory
items.summary: This paper synthesizes research on soil microbial communities and their roles in governing ecosystem processes, with the goal of better understanding how microbial diversity connects to ecological function. The authors developed a function-centred framework built around four conserved functional axes — secondary metabolism, nutrient cycling, community interactions, and stress tolerance — drawing on studies spanning ecological, agricultural, and environmental contexts. They find that these functional axes collectively influence plant productivity, climate regulation, and pollutant transformation, though their expression varies strongly with context. The authors propose that soil functions as a self-organizing system in which microbial interactions produce emergent ecosystem-level behaviours. This framework is positioned as a foundation for predictive, ecology-informed strategies to manage soils for sustainable agriculture, environmental remediation, and climate mitigation.
items.citation: Suzanne Hassan-Dalléac, Wafa Guiga, Antonia Suau. Soil microbes are the tiny bioengineers running Earth’s underground factory. Communications Earth & Environment. 2026

items.title: Regulatory Challenges and Opportunities for Cell‐Derived Extracellular Vesicles in Pharmaceutical Development: A European and Global Perspective
items.summary: This paper examines the regulatory landscape governing cell-derived extracellular vesicles as therapeutic and diagnostic products, with particular attention to inconsistencies across major jurisdictions. The authors analyze how existing medicinal product frameworks in the European Union, the United States, Japan, and other regions apply to extracellular vesicle-based products, noting that their acellular nature creates classification ambiguities that map unevenly onto established regulatory categories. A key focus is the European guidance clarifying that minimally modified extracellular vesicles fall outside the advanced therapy medicinal products definition, contrasting with the approach of other regulators who treat such products as biologics or drugs subject to premarket requirements. The authors identify persistent operational grey zones around classification criteria, critical quality attributes, potency strategies, and comparability that complicate cross-regional clinical development. Without prescribing normative solutions, the review argues for consistent application of existing frameworks and greater international regulatory dialogue to support the safe and reproducible advancement of extracellular vesicle-based therapies into clinical use.
items.citation: Tania Limongi, Paola Milla, Barbara Stella et al.. Regulatory Challenges and Opportunities for Cell‐Derived Extracellular Vesicles in Pharmaceutical Development: A European and Global Perspective. Journal of Extracellular Vesicles. 2026

items.title: From selection to design: Reshaping aptamer discovery with artificial intelligence
items.summary: This review examines how artificial intelligence is transforming the discovery and design of nucleic acid aptamers, which are synthetic oligonucleotide ligands capable of antibody-like molecular recognition but with greater chemical programmability. The authors argue that traditional discovery methods such as SELEX have been limited by their stochastic, trial-and-error nature, making clinical translation slow and inefficient. The review categorizes emerging AI approaches into predictive frameworks that learn sequence-structure-function relationships from complex datasets and generative models that enable de novo aptamer design targeting specific molecular geometries. The authors also highlight translational applications in biosensors and therapeutics, while acknowledging persistent challenges around data sparsity and model interpretability. Ultimately, the review proposes a roadmap toward closed-loop ecosystems that iteratively couple computational design, experimental validation, and model refinement to accelerate next-generation aptamer development.
items.citation: Xin Yang, Shijian Ding, Meishen Ren et al.. From selection to design: Reshaping aptamer discovery with artificial intelligence. Chemical Engineering Journal. 2026

items.title: Delivering biomedicines with stimuli‑responsive biomaterials
items.summary: The abstract is too thin to summarize meaningfully, as it provides only a high-level description of the review's scope without detailing the specific studies examined, methodologies discussed, or key findings and conclusions drawn.

items.title: Machine learning-assisted paper-based chemiluminescence biosensor for choline quantification in infant milk: toward portable nutritional quality monitoring
items.summary: This paper developed a low-cost paper-based biosensor for detecting choline in infant milk formula, motivated by the importance of this micronutrient for infant neurodevelopment and the risks associated with deficiency. The sensing platform uses choline oxidase to convert choline into hydrogen peroxide, which then drives a luminol-cobalt chemiluminescent reaction whose emitted light intensity is proportional to choline concentration. Smartphone imaging captures the chemiluminescent signal, and machine learning algorithms quantify light intensity to determine choline levels without conventional calibration methods. The device operates across a defined linear detection range and achieves a detection limit suitable for practical food monitoring applications. The authors conclude that this portable, point-of-care tool offers a viable approach for nutritional surveillance and food safety monitoring in resource-limited settings.
items.citation: Jitendra B. Zalke, Vani Kaushik, Chirag M. Singhal et al.. Machine learning-assisted paper-based chemiluminescence biosensor for choline quantification in infant milk: toward portable nutritional quality monitoring. Scientific Reports. 2026

items.title: Advances in Polydopamine-Based Nanoplatforms: Antioxidant Mechanisms and Applications in Oxidative Stress-Mediated Diseases
items.summary: This review examines polydopamine (PDA), a melanin-mimicking material with abundant redox-active functional groups, as a platform for combating oxidative stress-related diseases. The authors systematically analyzed how PDA-based nanoplatforms neutralize reactive oxygen species through hydrogen atom transfer and electron transfer mechanisms, with sustained activity maintained by dynamic cycling between catechol and quinone chemical states. The review surveys a range of nanoplatform architectures—including solid, mesoporous, hollow, doped, and coated forms—and discusses how structural features such as particle size, composition, and surface charge influence antioxidant performance. The paper further organizes recent therapeutic applications around key pathological challenges, including disrupting ROS-inflammation feedback loops, overcoming biological delivery barriers, remodeling regenerative microenvironments, and regulating programmed cell death. The authors conclude that PDA-based nanoplatforms offer distinct advantages over conventional antioxidants and represent a versatile and biocompatible strategy for treating oxidative stress-mediated diseases.
items.citation: Zhilin Wang, Zhu Liu, Luming Song et al.. Advances in Polydopamine-Based Nanoplatforms: Antioxidant Mechanisms and Applications in Oxidative Stress-Mediated Diseases. Nano-Micro Letters. 2026

items.title: DexPort: A Hand-Held Skill Interface for Dexterous Hand Data Collection
items.summary: The paper addresses the challenge of collecting high-quality demonstrations for dexterous robotic manipulation, which is bottlenecked by the difficulty of teleoperation and the embodiment gap in human demonstrations. The authors introduce DexPort, a portable interface that uses the same hand hardware for both data collection and robot deployment, allowing operators to specify wrist motion while selecting from a small set of predefined skills that coordinate finger movements rather than controlling each joint independently. Demonstrations are collected across multiple real-world tasks in both laboratory and unstructured environments without requiring a full robot arm setup, and behavior cloning is then used to train visuomotor policies directly from the recorded data. The system captures both commanded joint targets and measured joint states, and the authors find that using recorded robot commands rather than states substantially improves task success, as does incorporating data collected in unstructured, in-the-wild environments.
items.citation: Amber Xie, Jiawei Fu, Xiaofeng Guo et al.. DexPort: A Hand-Held Skill Interface for Dexterous Hand Data Collection. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A probabilistic approach to separate mergers and jellyfish galaxies: Application of morphological non-parametric indexes to the DESI Legacy Survey
items.summary: This paper investigates how non-parametric morphological indices can be used to classify galaxies into regular spirals, regular ellipticals, mergers, and jellyfish galaxies (candidates for ram-pressure stripping) using imaging from the DESI Legacy Surveys. The researchers measured ten non-parametric morphological indices and evaluated their discriminating power both in two-dimensional diagnostic planes using a Bayesian kernel-density classifier and in combined multi-index models using calibrated gradient-boosted machine learning. They found that planes combining Shannon entropy with asymmetry or the moment-of-light index are most informative for separating regular from disturbed systems, while distinguishing mergers from jellyfish candidates is more difficult and benefits most from concentration-based combinations. The multi-class machine learning model achieved substantially higher accuracy than any two-dimensional diagnostic plane alone, and class probabilities were produced for nearly two million galaxies. A key scientific finding is that jellyfish candidates occupy a relatively coherent and separable region of morphological parameter space, whereas mergers exhibit diverse and overlapping morphologies, making their physical origin harder to disentangle from structural measurements alone.
items.citation: V. M. Sampaio, Y. Jaff'e, A. Moretti et al.. A probabilistic approach to separate mergers and jellyfish galaxies: Application of morphological non-parametric indexes to the DESI Legacy Survey. arXiv. 2026

items.title: One-sided-DIQKD using any pure bipartite entangled state secure against all attacks
items.summary: This paper investigates one-sided device-independent quantum key distribution, a framework in which one measurement device is trusted and the other is untrusted, motivated by practical scenarios such as secure communication between a well-resourced institution and vulnerable individual users. The resource underpinning security in this setting is quantum steering, an asymmetric form of quantum nonlocality. The authors demonstrate that any pure bipartite entangled state, not just maximally entangled states, can be used to generate a secure key in this framework, significantly broadening the class of usable quantum resources. Taking into account realistic detector efficiencies and source imperfections based on current technology, they show that states close to being separable can still yield secure keys. Additionally, the work identifies critical thresholds for detection efficiency and visibility for each pure bipartite entangled state, providing practical guidance for experimental implementations.
items.citation: Bohnishikha Ghosh, Chithra Raj, Shubhayan Sarkar. One-sided-DIQKD using any pure bipartite entangled state secure against all attacks. arXiv. 2026

items.title: What Mean Error Misses: Device-Clock Diagnostics for Evaluating Eye Tracking across Three Virtual Reality Headsets
items.summary: This paper evaluated the accuracy and reliability of eye tracking across three virtual reality headsets by having participants complete identical gaze protocols on each device. The study compared spatial accuracy, temporal data quality, and validity flagging across the Meta Quest Pro, HTC VIVE Pro Eye, and the previously unevaluated HTC VIVE Focus Vision. The researchers found that mean gaze error differed substantially across devices and that the Focus Vision remained least accurate even after recalibration, while the VIVE Pro Eye showed sensitivity to background luminance. Beyond spatial accuracy, the study identified device-clock-level failures that mean error alone would not reveal, including multi-second data pauses on the Meta Quest Pro, correlated samples on the Focus Vision, and a failure of the Meta Quest Pro to correctly flag gaze data as invalid during deliberate eye closures. The authors argue that evaluations of eye trackers should go beyond mean error to include analysis of repeated timestamps, data loss on the device clock, and validity flagging behavior during eye closures.
items.citation: Aleksandr Chernysh, Mehedi Hasan Raju, Kamrul Hasan et al.. What Mean Error Misses: Device-Clock Diagnostics for Evaluating Eye Tracking across Three Virtual Reality Headsets. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Multimodal Generative AI Assists Comprehensive Echocardiographic Interpretation
items.summary: This paper introduces EchoChat, a generative multimodal vision-language model designed to perform comprehensive echocardiographic analysis by emulating the cognitive workflow of a cardiologist, including chain-of-thought reasoning grounded in visual evidence. The model was trained on echocardiography-instruction pairs from tens of thousands of examinations and evaluated across cohorts from multiple international medical centers. EchoChat supports a broad diagnostic scope covering numerous cardiac conditions and findings, outperforming existing foundation models on both cardiac condition recognition and quantitative measurements across shared tasks. In a blinded reader study, echocardiography reports co-generated with EchoChat were rated superior in diagnostic accuracy and completeness by senior echocardiographers, and substantially improved diagnostic performance compared to reports produced by routine readers alone. The authors conclude that embedding clinical reasoning into multimodal AI can broaden access to specialist-level echocardiographic interpretation and improve the standard of cardiovascular care globally.
items.citation: Yi Qin, Marawan Elbatel, Shanshan Song et al.. Multimodal Generative AI Assists Comprehensive Echocardiographic Interpretation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Radiation damage and recovery of SiPMs exposed to low-momentum muon beams for innovative scintillation-based muon beam monitors
items.summary: This study investigated radiation damage to Silicon PhotoMultipliers (SiPMs) caused by exposure to low-momentum muon beams, which are relevant to applications in material science and particle physics due to the high energy muons deposit in detector materials. Eight SiPM models from different manufacturers were irradiated with positive muons and their electrical characteristics were measured before and after irradiation and annealing. Despite a measurable increase in dark current following irradiation, all devices maintained operational stability, demonstrating resilience to this type of radiation environment. Thermal annealing at elevated temperature was shown to recover the optimal performance characteristics of the SiPMs. This work supports the broader goal of developing scintillation-based beam monitors capable of detecting low-momentum muons.
items.citation: Riccardo Rossini, Sayani Biswas, Adrian D. Hillier et al.. Radiation damage and recovery of SiPMs exposed to low-momentum muon beams for innovative scintillation-based muon beam monitors. arXiv. 2026

items.title: 3D-printed architectures for (bio)sensing
items.summary: This perspective paper examines how three-dimensional printing is transforming biosensor fabrication by enabling fully integrated, all-in-one devices that consolidate sample preparation, fluid handling, and sensing elements within a single manufacturing workflow. The authors survey recent advances across biomedical, environmental, and wearable applications, comparing additive manufacturing techniques such as fused deposition modeling, stereolithography, and digital light processing in terms of their capabilities for sensing tasks including preconcentration, detection, and multiplexed electroanalysis. A central focus is placed on the relationship between materials and device function, covering in-house filament preparation, substrate selection, and surface functionalization strategies for conductive components and microchannels. The paper also addresses persistent challenges including print resolution, material conductivity, biomolecule stability, and sustainability, proposing solutions such as hybrid printing, low-temperature filaments, recycled materials, and chemometrics-assisted design. Looking ahead, the authors outline a roadmap emphasizing scalability, customization, and integration with artificial intelligence and the internet of things, positioning three-dimensional printing as a transformative platform for next-generation sensing systems.
items.citation: Panagiota M. Kalligosfyri, Gabriella Iula, Grazia Nota et al.. 3D-printed architectures for (bio)sensing. Biosensors and Biomolecular Electronics. 2026

items.title: Nanozyme-based biosensors for pathogenic microorganism detection: a mini-review
items.citation: Yang T, Ling Y, Zhang E et al.. Nanozyme-based biosensors for pathogenic microorganism detection: a mini-review. Frontiers in microbiology. 2026

items.title: Rapid and visual detection of group B Streptococcus based on an ERA-CasMNPs colorimetric biosensor.
items.summary: This paper addressed the need for rapid, accurate, and equipment-light detection of Group B Streptococcus, a key pathogen in perinatal infections. The researchers developed a biosensor called ERA-CasMNPs by combining enzymatic recombinase amplification targeting the GBS-specific cfb gene with CRISPR/Cas12a-mediated recognition and cleavage activity, coupled to a colorimetric readout via horseradish peroxidase-modified magnetic nanoparticles. The system produces a visible color signal without complex instrumentation and completes detection within approximately an hour and a half, achieving a very low detection limit. Validation against a large set of clinical bacterial isolates showed the biosensor's sensitivity, specificity, and overall accuracy were comparable to quantitative PCR. The authors conclude that ERA-CasMNPs offers a promising sensitive and visual diagnostic tool suited for resource-limited settings and rapid clinical testing scenarios.
items.citation: Guo H, Jiang Y, Li D et al.. Rapid and visual detection of group B Streptococcus based on an ERA-CasMNPs colorimetric biosensor.. Talanta. 2026

items.title: Advancements in biosensor Technologies for Pathogen Detection: Innovations and comparison with conventional diagnostic approaches.
items.summary: This review examines the current state of biosensor technologies for pathogen detection and compares them with established conventional diagnostic methods. The authors surveyed multiple biosensor platforms, including electrochemical, optical, nanoparticle, microfluidic, and paper-based systems, analyzing their sensing principles, design strategies, and practical applications across clinical diagnostics, food safety, and environmental monitoring. Conventional approaches such as culture-based methods, ELISA, and PCR, while analytically robust, are limited by lengthy processing times, complex instrumentation, and the requirement for trained personnel, constraining their use in rapid or on-site settings. Biosensors offer advantages including portability, high sensitivity, multiplexing capability, and suitability for point-of-care deployment, with advances in nanomaterials, biorecognition strategies, and signal-transduction mechanisms further expanding their detection potential. Nevertheless, the review identifies persistent challenges including sensor stability, reproducibility, fabrication complexity, scalability, and validation as barriers that must be overcome before widespread practical implementation can be achieved.
items.citation: Singhal P, Misra S, Prakash A et al.. Advancements in biosensor Technologies for Pathogen Detection: Innovations and comparison with conventional diagnostic approaches.. Journal of microbiological methods. 2026

items.title: Development of a NiCoFe-LDH/Ketjenblack-enhanced electrochemical antibacterial peptide biosensor for Aeromonas hydrophila detection in seawater samples.
items.summary: This paper developed an electrochemical biosensor for detecting the fish pathogen Aeromonas hydrophila in aquaculture settings, combining an antibacterial peptide as the biorecognition element with a ternary NiCoFe layered double hydroxide and Ketjenblack carbon nanocomposite as the electrode substrate. The nanocomposite was synthesized via a one-pot precipitation method and applied to a screen-printed carbon electrode, where the layered double hydroxide-carbon interface provided signal amplification while the peptide enabled selective bacterial capture. Physicochemical and electrochemical characterization confirmed the high-surface-area nanosheet structure and rapid electron transfer properties of the composite. Under optimized room-temperature conditions, the biosensor achieved detection across a broad bacterial concentration range within a short assay time, with a very low detection limit, good reproducibility, minimal cross-reactivity with other bacteria, and strong performance when tested in spiked seawater samples. The authors report this to be the first electrochemical, antibacterial peptide-based biosensor for this pathogen that has been validated in seawater, highlighting its potential relevance for real aquaculture monitoring.
items.citation: Kızılkurtlu AA, Arancı K, Gülyüz S et al.. Development of a NiCoFe-LDH/Ketjenblack-enhanced electrochemical antibacterial peptide biosensor for Aeromonas hydrophila detection in seawater samples.. Mikrochimica acta. 2026

items.title: Automated machine learning framework for interpreting paper-based biosensing of pathogens.
items.summary: This paper investigated automated machine learning approaches for interpreting colorimetric images from paper-based biosensors designed to detect microbial pathogens. The researchers evaluated several image analysis strategies, including conventional normalized intensity extraction, region-of-interest descriptors, and convolutional neural networks, finding that while these methods performed well within individual studies, their optimized decision thresholds shifted substantially between studies, degrading cross-study classification. To address this limitation, the team developed a color-space normalization method that characterizes each test signal relative to paired positive and negative controls rather than relying on single-channel intensity alone. This approach improved separation between positive and negative results across different biosensor studies and produced more consistent decision boundaries in both within-study and cross-study validation compared to conventional methods. The authors conclude that color-space normalization enables more generalizable, machine learning-assisted interpretation of paper-based biosensor images and supports the establishment of transferable classification thresholds across distinct assay contexts.
items.citation: Park S, Yang Z, He Z. Automated machine learning framework for interpreting paper-based biosensing of pathogens.. Environmental research. 2026

items.title: Self-Cleaning Electrochemical Biosensor Based on MCOF@Ag for Simultaneous Pathogen Detection and Photocatalytic Inactivation.
items.summary: This paper developed a dual-function electrochemical biosensor capable of both detecting and killing bacterial pathogens using a single electrode material.
