The researchers synthesized a silver nanoparticle-decorated metal-covalent organic framework with a nanoflower-like structure, then functionalized it with aptamers specific to *Staphylococcus aureus* to enable electrochemical quantification of the bacteria upon binding. The biosensor achieved highly sensitive detection across a broad concentration range with an exceptionally low detection limit, demonstrating logarithmic quantification suitable for real-world pathogen monitoring. Beyond detection, the material's photocatalytic activity under visible light allowed it to inactivate nearly all captured bacteria within minutes by generating reactive oxygen species, after which the electrode could be regenerated and reused. The study presents this integrated detect-and-destroy approach as a promising strategy for combining advanced biosensing with antibacterial functionality in a single platform.
items.citation: Bai Y, Xiao L, Cai L et al.. Self-Cleaning Electrochemical Biosensor Based on MCOF@Ag for Simultaneous Pathogen Detection and Photocatalytic Inactivation.. Analytical chemistry. 2026

items.title: Synergistic Multicomponent Nucleopeptide-Based Hydrogels: Harnessing DNA-Base Pairing and Electrostatic Complementarities
items.summary: This study investigated how combining charge complementarity and DNA nucleobase pairing interactions could be harnessed to create tunable multicomponent hydrogels from short hybrid peptide-nucleobase molecules called nucleopeptides. The researchers synthesized a series of peptides derived from two sequences carrying opposite charges at physiological pH, each functionalized with one of the four DNA nucleobases introduced through a peptide nucleic acid moiety, yielding multiple combinations for systematic study. Through a multiscale characterization approach, they examined how electrostatic and Watson-Crick base-pairing complementarities between components influenced key hydrogel properties including gelation time, stiffness, sol-gel transition temperature, stress resistance, and fibrillar network morphology. The results demonstrated that careful selection of complementary components allows fine-tuning of hydrogel mechanical and physicochemical properties, though the study also revealed unexpected behaviors that highlight the complexity of these bioinspired hybrid systems. Overall, the findings support nucleopeptide-based multicomponent hydrogels as a promising platform for developing high-performance supramolecular materials with potential biomedical and biotechnological applications.
items.citation: Tristan Giraud, Marine Koch, Paul Hoschtettler et al.. Synergistic Multicomponent Nucleopeptide-Based Hydrogels: Harnessing DNA-Base Pairing and Electrostatic Complementarities. ACS Materials Au. 2026

items.title: Federated Learning in Multimodal Healthcare Diagnostics: Privacy-Preserving AI for Biomedical Imaging, Electronic Health Records, Wearables, and Clinical Decision Support
items.summary: This review paper examines the application of federated learning to multimodal healthcare diagnostics, addressing the fundamental tension between the need for large-scale AI training and the privacy constraints that prevent centralizing sensitive clinical data. The authors conducted a literature review spanning multiple healthcare domains, including biomedical imaging modalities such as MRI, CT, and histopathology, as well as electronic health records, wearable physiological signals, chronic disease management, elder care, and clinical decision support. Federated learning is presented as a framework that enables multi-institutional AI model training by sharing only model updates rather than raw patient data, thereby improving regulatory alignment, though the authors emphasize that privacy is not guaranteed by default and requires additional protections against threats such as gradient leakage and membership inference attacks. The review identifies persistent implementation challenges including system heterogeneity, data imbalance, communication bottlenecks, and fairness concerns. Based on their synthesis of research and practice, the authors offer guidance to regulators, developers, and healthcare systems aimed at advancing safe and equitable federated learning deployments across diverse geographic and institutional contexts.
items.venue: Archives of Computational Methods in Engineering
items.citation: Shon G. Nemane, Vaishnavi M. Sarad, Dhiraj P. Tulaskar et al.. Federated Learning in Multimodal Healthcare Diagnostics: Privacy-Preserving AI for Biomedical Imaging, Electronic Health Records, Wearables, and Clinical Decision Support. Archives of Computational Methods in Engineering. 2026

items.title: CRISPR-Cas systems as next-generation antimicrobials: a systemic review of mechanisms, delivery strategies, and translational challenges
items.summary: This systematic review examined CRISPR-Cas systems as a potential alternative to conventional antibiotics in the context of rapidly rising multidrug-resistant bacterial infections. The authors synthesized preclinical evidence from studies using various CRISPR effectors, including Cas9, Cas12, and Cas13, evaluating their antibacterial mechanisms and delivery platforms such as bacteriophages, conjugative plasmids, and nanoparticles. The reviewed studies demonstrated that CRISPR-Cas systems could effectively kill or resensitize resistant bacteria through mechanisms including chromosomal double-strand break induction, resistance plasmid curing, and RNA-targeted cleavage, with phage-mediated delivery showing the most consistent efficacy. One CRISPR-enhanced engineered bacteriophage cocktail has already advanced to clinical evaluation, reflecting the translational momentum of this approach. Nevertheless, the review identified significant barriers to clinical adoption, including limited bacterial host range, physiological instability, emergence of escape mutations, and insufficient long-term safety data, and called for optimized delivery methods, multiplex targeting strategies, and clearer regulatory frameworks to advance the field.
items.citation: Maha S.I. Wizrah. CRISPR-Cas systems as next-generation antimicrobials: a systemic review of mechanisms, delivery strategies, and translational challenges. Frontiers in Microbiology. 2026

items.title: Traditional fermented food microbial ecosystems oriented towards industrial standards: multi-dimensional characterization and artificial regulation
items.summary: This review examines the microbial ecosystems underlying traditional fermented foods, which are shaped by complex interactions among microorganisms, substrates, and environmental conditions, but whose spontaneous and uncontrolled nature creates quality and safety variability that hinders industrial standardization. To address this, the authors synthesized current knowledge on multi-omics approaches—integrating genomic, transcriptomic, metabolomic, and related data—for comprehensively characterizing microbial composition, community dynamics, metabolite profiles, and the role of bacteriophages within these ecosystems. They also reviewed strategies for artificially regulating fermentation, encompassing the use of functional starter strains, engineered synthetic microbial communities, bacteriophage management, and physicochemical interventions. The review concludes by outlining future directions and challenges involved in transitioning traditional fermentation from empirical, artisanal practice toward predictable and scalable industrial processes.
items.citation: M T Wu, Jiayao Wang, Yu Wang et al.. Traditional fermented food microbial ecosystems oriented towards industrial standards: multi-dimensional characterization and artificial regulation. npj Science of Food. 2026

items.title: Personalized cancer vaccines: bridging immune-oncology and precision medicine for advanced therapeutics
items.summary: This review examines the current landscape of personalized cancer vaccines, which are designed to target patient-specific tumor antigens and mount tailored immune responses against cancer. The authors survey multiple vaccine platforms, including DNA-, mRNA-, peptide-, dendritic cell-, and whole-cell-based approaches, while addressing key immunological obstacles such as tumor heterogeneity, immunosuppressive microenvironments, and insufficient immune memory. To overcome these limitations, the review details conventional and nanotechnology-based delivery systems, including lipid-polymer hybrid nanovaccines, biomimetic membranes, and stimulus-responsive materials that enhance lymph node targeting, dendritic cell activation, and antigen presentation. The integration of artificial intelligence for neoantigen selection, multiomics for patient stratification, and combination regimens with immune checkpoint inhibitors is highlighted as a means to accelerate vaccine design and improve therapeutic efficacy. The authors conclude that personalized mRNA vaccines in particular have shown promising reductions in recurrence risk across cancer types, and that next-generation personalized vaccines represent a shift toward proactive, precision-controlled cancer immunotherapy.
items.citation: Leiguang Ye, Guo Zhao, Jiaxiu Ma et al.. Personalized cancer vaccines: bridging immune-oncology and precision medicine for advanced therapeutics. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: SceneBloom: Agentic Indoor Environment Generation with Realistic and Diverse Layouts for Embodied Learning
items.summary: SceneBloom is an agentic framework designed to generate realistic and diverse indoor environments for training embodied agents. The system combines a hierarchical diffusion-based sampler that generates furniture arrangements within functional zones with a contract-guided compiler that extracts spatial relations from these proposals to perform geometric fitting and pose correction, producing physically valid three-dimensional scenes. Evaluated across five room types, the framework achieves the highest visual quality and physical stability among compared methods, with no detected mesh collisions or out-of-bounds objects, and produces layouts that more closely match the distribution of real rooms than all baselines. Notably, object navigation policies trained in SceneBloom-generated environments outperform those trained on an equal number of real indoor scans when tested on held-out real scenes, demonstrating the practical utility of the generated environments for embodied learning.
items.citation: Yuhan Liu, Lianhui Qin, Shenji Wan. SceneBloom: Agentic Indoor Environment Generation with Realistic and Diverse Layouts for Embodied Learning. arXiv. 2026

items.title: MiD-VLM: Detecting and Grounding Global Semantic Misinformation in Image-Caption Pairs
items.summary: This paper addresses the problem of semantic misinformation in image-caption pairs, where an authentic image is paired with a misleading or distorted caption that alters its narrative without introducing any pixel-level artifacts. The authors studied this using a dataset designed to capture global scene and semantic inconsistencies, proposing a multimodal model that fuses image-text representations from two vision-language encoders through a projection layer and adapts a large vision-language model using parameter-efficient fine-tuning. The model is trained to simultaneously classify whether a pair is authentic, identify the type of manipulation present, and localize the specific misleading tokens in the caption. The approach achieves strong performance on binary authenticity classification, demonstrating that parameter-efficient adaptation of vision-language models is an effective strategy for detecting semantic misinformation. The authors also identify precise token-level grounding as an area warranting further investigation.
items.citation: Tarunya Prasad, Bharatesh Chakravarthi. MiD-VLM: Detecting and Grounding Global Semantic Misinformation in Image-Caption Pairs. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Flownomaly: Single-Step Conditional-Mean Recovery for Few-Shot Anomaly Detection
items.summary: Flownomaly addresses few-shot industrial anomaly detection, where models must characterize normal appearance from only a small number of defect-free reference images. The approach frames the problem as recovering a normal counterpart for any query image patch by learning a velocity field through conditional flow matching over frozen pretrained feature representations, transporting Gaussian noise toward normal feature distributions defined by the support examples. A key efficiency gain comes from recognizing that, along the straight interpolation paths used in flow matching, a single evaluation of the learned field yields the posterior mean of the clean normal token without requiring iterative trajectory integration. Because no anomalous validation samples are available during tuning, a normal-only criterion based on Jacobian gain relative to noise selects the operating time purely from the support set, and anomaly scores are derived from squared residuals between query tokens and their recovered counterparts. The method achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple few-shot benchmarks on standard industrial inspection datasets, with particularly strong gains in one-shot image-level detection on one of the benchmark datasets compared to prior methods.
items.citation: Bernardo Perrone Ribeiro, Erkut Akdag, Egor Bondarev. Flownomaly: Single-Step Conditional-Mean Recovery for Few-Shot Anomaly Detection. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A Central Limit Theorem for the Driver Site Frequency Spectrum
items.summary: This paper studies the statistical properties of the driver site frequency spectrum (SFS) arising from a supercritical two-type continuous-time linear birth-death process that incorporates mutation and selection, where mutant individuals have a higher net-growth rate than wild-type individuals. Building on previously established first-order law of large numbers results for the driver SFS, the authors derive a second-order central limit theorem by demonstrating stable convergence of an appropriately scaled deviation of the SFS from its first-order limit. The central limit theorem is established under both large detection times and large detection sizes. These theoretical results are then applied to construct confidence intervals for a class of consistent estimators of the fitness advantage conferred by the driver mutation.
items.citation: Armaan Ahmed, Jasmine Foo, Kevin Leder. A Central Limit Theorem for the Driver Site Frequency Spectrum. arXiv. 2026

items.title: If at First You Don't Succeed, Backtrack: Lightweight Recovery for Frozen VLAs
items.summary: This paper addresses the brittleness of Vision-Language-Action models in robotic manipulation, specifically their tendency to fail when their own actions push them into states underrepresented in training data. The authors introduce Backtrack, a lightweight mechanism that attaches a small failure prediction head to a frozen, unmodified policy, training it solely on outcome-labeled rollouts to read the policy's internal representations and estimate the probability of episode failure. When predicted failure exceeds a threshold, the system pauses the policy and physically retraces the robot arm's recent motion, returning it to an earlier configuration where the policy can retry without any retraining or separate recovery model. Evaluated across multiple benchmark suites and three distinct VLA architectures spanning both flow-matching and autoregressive action generation, Backtrack consistently reduces failure rates, with the largest gains observed on long-horizon multi-step tasks where baseline policies struggle most. The approach achieves these improvements while adding less than one percent to the policy's parameter count, requiring no recovery demonstrations or modifications to the underlying model.
items.citation: Thomas Landeg, Thierry Tambe. If at First You Don't Succeed, Backtrack: Lightweight Recovery for Frozen VLAs. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Generating entanglement in quantum matter with pathway-entangled photons via resonant inelastic X-ray scattering
items.summary: This paper proposes a new use for resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS), shifting its role from a probe of quantum materials to a tool for generating entanglement within them. The protocol splits an incident X-ray photon coherently across two arms of an interferometer that illuminate opposite ends of a solid-state sample, then recombines the scattered photons at a second beam splitter so that detecting an energy-selected photon heralds a coherent superposition of excitations at the two ends — an X-ray, solid-state analogue of the DLCZ heralding scheme. Using a Kramers-Heisenberg formalism with quantized photon modes, the authors show that orthogonal and degenerate end excitations produce maximally entangled states. They demonstrate the mechanism in three model systems: a pair of decoupled sites that yields a heralded Bell state, an open tight-binding chain whose interference pattern benchmarks interferometer coherence, and a spin-one Haldane chain in which the protocol generates an entangled pair of fractionalized edge spins. The paper also discusses practical challenges for implementing this interferometric RIXS protocol in realistic X-ray experiments.
items.citation: Chunjing Jia, Valentin Walther, Laimei Nie. Generating entanglement in quantum matter with pathway-entangled photons via resonant inelastic X-ray scattering. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Multiplex molecular respiratory diagnostic panels and antimicrobial use in paediatric respiratory infections: a systematic review and meta-analysis protocol.
items.citation: Bajaj R, Mehta P, Gopi A et al.. Multiplex molecular respiratory diagnostic panels and antimicrobial use in paediatric respiratory infections: a systematic review and meta-analysis protocol.. BMJ open. 2026

items.title: Development and validation of a multiplex TaqMan real-time quantitative PCR assay for the simultaneous detection of six major bacterial respiratory pathogens in goats.
items.summary: This study developed and validated two triplex TaqMan real-time quantitative PCR panels capable of simultaneously detecting six major bacterial and mycoplasmal pathogens responsible for respiratory disease in goats. The assays targeted three mycoplasmal species in one panel and three bacterial species in a second panel, with analytical performance evaluated using recombinant plasmid standards and nucleic acids from both target and non-target organisms. The assays demonstrated high specificity with no cross-reactivity against non-target pathogens, and achieved low limits of detection with strong reproducibility across both intra- and inter-assay replicates. When applied to field-collected nasal swab samples from goats, the method detected at least one pathogen in the majority of samples and revealed that a substantial proportion of animals harbored co-infections with multiple pathogens simultaneously. The authors conclude that this multiplex approach offers a rapid and reliable diagnostic tool suitable for both clinical investigation and epidemiological surveillance of caprine respiratory disease.
items.citation: Fu M, Liu Y, Zhang Z et al.. Development and validation of a multiplex TaqMan real-time quantitative PCR assay for the simultaneous detection of six major bacterial respiratory pathogens in goats.. Frontiers in veterinary science. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic accuracy of rapid integrated molecular testing for major respiratory viral infections: a systematic review and meta-analysis
items.citation: Liu C, Yu D. Diagnostic accuracy of rapid integrated molecular testing for major respiratory viral infections: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Frontiers in medicine. 2026

items.title: Respiratory Viral Infections in Febrile Children With Lymphoreticular Malignancies: A Single-Centre Descriptive Study.
items.summary: This study investigated respiratory viral infections in febrile children with lymphoreticular malignancies at a tertiary care centre in India, a setting where data on this vulnerable population are limited. Using multiplex real-time PCR targeting eighteen respiratory viral pathogens, researchers prospectively analyzed nasopharyngeal swabs from febrile episodes with respiratory symptoms in children under twelve years old, while separately screening all episodes for SARS-CoV-2 by rapid antigen test. Respiratory viruses were detected in roughly one-third of febrile episodes, with human coronavirus, human rhinovirus, parainfluenza viruses, influenza A, and human adenovirus being the most commonly identified pathogens, and upper respiratory tract infections predominating. Viral positivity was significantly associated with breathlessness, lower respiratory tract infection classification, elevated inflammatory markers, and abnormal chest radiography. Both deaths in the cohort were linked to lower respiratory tract infection caused by human parainfluenza virus type 4, highlighting this pathogen as warranting closer clinical surveillance, and the authors recommend prospective multicentre studies to guide antimicrobial stewardship in this immunocompromised population.
items.citation: M R K, Das S, Jain C et al.. Respiratory Viral Infections in Febrile Children With Lymphoreticular Malignancies: A Single-Centre Descriptive Study.. Journal of medical virology. 2026

items.title: Development and Initial Analytical Evaluation of a Multiplex PCR-Based Targeted NGS Assay for Expanded Viral Detection in Clinical Respiratory Specimens.
items.summary: This study developed an in-house multiplex PCR-based targeted next-generation sequencing method designed to detect a broad panel of viruses simultaneously in clinical respiratory specimens, addressing the limitation of conventional PCR assays that require prior etiological hypotheses and can only identify a restricted number of pathogens at once. The researchers constructed a panel targeting twenty-eight viruses, established bioinformatics pipelines for data processing, evaluated analytical sensitivity using positive control samples, and tested the method against a large collection of nasopharyngeal and oropharyngeal swabs grouped according to prior PCR results. The method showed concordance with conventional PCR results in the majority of previously positive specimens while also detecting additional co-infecting viruses in a notable subset, and it identified viral targets in a substantial proportion of PCR-negative specimens. Among hospital-derived samples, the approach uncovered coinfections and additional viral detections not found during initial routine testing, though findings involving Epstein-Barr virus and cytomegalovirus required cautious interpretation. The authors conclude that the method holds promise as an adjunctive diagnostic tool for respiratory infections but requires further optimization, validation, and standardization of interpretive criteria before broader clinical application.
items.citation: Nadtoka MI, Bukharina AY, Roev GV et al.. Development and Initial Analytical Evaluation of a Multiplex PCR-Based Targeted NGS Assay for Expanded Viral Detection in Clinical Respiratory Specimens.. Diagnostics (Basel, Switzerland). 2026

items.title: ECCO Guidelines on the Prevention, Diagnosis, and Management of Infections in Inflammatory Bowel Disease
items.summary: This paper presents updated clinical guidelines from a major European gastroenterology organization addressing infection-related risks in patients with inflammatory bowel disease. The work was motivated by the rapid expansion of immunosuppressive and biologic therapies for Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis, including newer small molecules and advanced biologics, which carry distinct infection risk profiles compared to older agents. The guideline systematically covers risk stratification along with the prevention, diagnosis, and management of viral, bacterial, mycobacterial, and vaccine-preventable infections in this immunocompromised population. Building on prior consensus statements and a previous guideline, this update integrates the most recent evidence to provide clinicians with a structured, evidence-based framework tailored to the contemporary treatment landscape. The overarching emphasis is on preventative strategies to reduce the morbidity and mortality associated with opportunistic infections in IBD patients receiving potent immune-modulating therapies.
items.venue: Journal of Crohn s and Colitis
items.citation: Henit A. Yanai, Pierre Ellul, Bram Verstockt et al.. ECCO Guidelines on the Prevention, Diagnosis, and Management of Infections in Inflammatory Bowel Disease. Journal of Crohn s and Colitis. 2026

items.title: Small extracellular vesicle signaling and mitochondrial transfer reprogram T helper cell function in human asthma
items.summary: This study investigated the role of small extracellular vesicles derived from airway myeloid-derived regulatory cells in driving T cell-mediated airway inflammation in asthma. The researchers examined how these vesicles communicate between immune cells, finding that they carry mitochondria and engage T cell receptors to promote antigen-specific activation and polarization toward pro-inflammatory Th17 and Th2 phenotypes. CD4+ T cells were found to internalize these mitochondria-containing vesicles primarily through membrane fusion, and the transferred mitochondria drive T cell activation through reactive oxygen species signaling. A Drp1-dependent mitochondrial fission mechanism was identified as responsible for packaging mitochondria into the vesicles within pro-inflammatory myeloid cells, and intranasal delivery of these vesicles in a mouse model of asthma enhanced airway inflammation in vivo. The findings reveal a previously unrecognized pathway linking mitochondrial fission and intercellular mitochondrial transfer to dysregulated T cell activation in asthma, suggesting this process may represent a novel therapeutic target.
items.citation: Kenneth P. Hough, Jennifer L. Trevor, Shaheer Ahmad et al.. Small extracellular vesicle signaling and mitochondrial transfer reprogram T helper cell function in human asthma. Nature Communications. 2026

items.title: Serologic Evidence of Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza A(H5N1) Virus Infection in a Veterinary Professional Exposed to an Infected Domestic Cat — Los Angeles County, California, December 2024–January 2025
items.summary: This study investigated potential human infection with highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) virus following an outbreak in domestic cats in Los Angeles County linked to consumption of raw animal products. Public health authorities monitored all persons exposed to the infected cats for symptoms and subsequently conducted a serological survey to detect evidence of infection, including among those without reported illness. Although none of the exposed individuals tested positive by standard PCR methods, antibody testing revealed serological evidence of H5N1 infection in one asymptomatic veterinary professional who had not used respiratory or eye protection during animal contact and had no other known risk factors. These findings provide the first serological evidence of possible cat-to-human transmission of H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b virus, extending concern about spillover beyond livestock and wild birds to domestic cats. The authors emphasize the importance of appropriate infection control practices in veterinary settings given this potential transmission route.
items.venue: MMWR Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report
items.citation: Aisling Vaughan, Allison Joyce, Elizabeth Traub et al.. Serologic Evidence of Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza A(H5N1) Virus Infection in a Veterinary Professional Exposed to an Infected Domestic Cat — Los Angeles County, California, December 2024–January 2025. MMWR Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report. 2026

items.title: Inflammation-driven immune reprogramming in sepsis: from cytokine storm to immunoparalysis
items.summary: This narrative review reframes sepsis not as a uniform inflammatory syndrome but as an inflammation-driven immune reprogramming disorder characterized by distinct biological subtypes and time-evolving trajectories. The authors synthesize recent advances in human immune profiling to trace how early innate sensing, endothelial injury, coagulation-inflammation coupling, and cytokine networks drive progression from hyperinflammation to immune paralysis, lymphocyte loss, functional exhaustion, and chronic critical illness. A central argument is that hyperinflammatory and low-response states can arise simultaneously and shift across compartments, meaning static or single-biomarker monitoring fails to capture the true patient state. The review proposes a dynamic immune monitoring framework emphasizing composite signals and longitudinal trends, and attributes many past trial failures to misalignment between patient immune state, therapeutic direction, and timing of intervention. The authors call for next-generation trial designs featuring bidirectional immunomodulation, repeated phenotyping, enriched enrollment of biologically defined subtypes, and outcome measures that encompass secondary infections, organ recovery, and longer-term functional status.
items.citation: Sha Zhu, J Inghorn He. Inflammation-driven immune reprogramming in sepsis: from cytokine storm to immunoparalysis. Frontiers in Immunology. 2026

items.title: Effects of a clinical metagenomics intervention on clinical outcomes, healthcare costs, and health-related quality of life in patients with sepsis or septic shock: results of the randomized-controlled DigiSep trial
items.summary: This multicenter randomized controlled trial investigated whether adding metagenomic next-generation sequencing of microbial circulating cell-free DNA to standard microbiological diagnostics could improve outcomes for patients with sepsis or septic shock in intensive care units. Patients were assigned to receive either standard-of-care microbiology alone or standard-of-care microbiology supplemented with metagenomic sequencing, with the primary endpoint being an antibiotic risk-adjusted composite outcome ranking score measured at 28 days. The primary endpoint was not significantly improved by the metagenomic intervention. However, exploratory secondary analyses suggested benefits including shorter duration of mechanical ventilation, faster resolution of shock, and improved health-related quality of life at 90 days, while healthcare costs over 180 days did not differ between groups.
authors: on behalf of the German Society of Anaesthesiology and Intensive Care (GSAIC) Trials Group
items.citation: Thorsten Brenner, Annabell Skarabis, Stefan Josef Schaller et al.. Effects of a clinical metagenomics intervention on clinical outcomes, healthcare costs, and health-related quality of life in patients with sepsis or septic shock: results of the randomized-controlled DigiSep trial. Intensive Care Medicine. 2026

items.title: mRNA-based influenza vaccine expands the B cell response breadth in humans
items.summary: This study compared the immune responses elicited by a conventional split-virion influenza vaccine against those from an investigational mRNA-based quadrivalent influenza vaccine in healthy young adults across two consecutive vaccination seasons. The researchers assessed B cell responses in blood and draining lymph nodes, combining antibody titer measurements, memory B cell quantification, proteomic serum IgG repertoire analysis, and B cell lineage tracing. The mRNA vaccine consistently induced higher antibody titers and greater frequencies of memory B cells, and stimulated germinal center reactions in lymph nodes that persisted for at least six months after vaccination in a subset of participants. Proteomic analyses revealed that mRNA vaccination increased the number of distinct vaccine-elicited serum IgG clonotypes and drove intraclonal expansion within pre-existing clonotypes, with expanded clonotypes mapping to germinal center-associated B cell lineage branches consistent with ongoing affinity maturation. Critically, this remodeling of the antibody repertoire translated into broader binding against antigenically divergent influenza viruses, highlighting sustained germinal center activity as a key mechanism for widening vaccine-induced antibody coverage.
items.citation: Hanover C. Matz, Tae-Geun Yu, Kritika Dixit et al.. mRNA-based influenza vaccine expands the B cell response breadth in humans. Nature Immunology. 2026

items.title: Polyhedral RIS Architecture with Quantum-Assisted Facet Selection for Uniform Coverage
items.summary: This paper investigates a chamfered hexagonal polyhedral reconfigurable intelligent surface architecture designed to provide nearly uniform coverage for moving user equipment, addressing practical challenges such as discrete phase control, uncertain facet positions, and continuous UE mobility. The authors derive closed-form bounds on gain loss from facet selection relative to an ideal reflecting facet, incorporating quantization loss and joint random mounting errors across all facets. For a precoded multi-user downlink, the facet-selection subproblem within a max-min rate design is formulated as an exact quadratic unconstrained binary optimization problem amenable to repeated time-constrained solving. The polyhedral architecture is shown to dramatically reduce dead zones compared to vertical planar panels and substantially increase minimum user rates relative to a simultaneous transmitting and reflecting panel baseline. Among the optimization approaches tested, simulated annealing reliably finds the optimal solution in the vast majority of cases, while the quantum approximation algorithm fails to match this performance.
items.citation: Noha Hassan, Halim Yanikomeroglu. Polyhedral RIS Architecture with Quantum-Assisted Facet Selection for Uniform Coverage. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Local Polynomial Estimation in Irregular Correlated Random Coefficient Panel Data Models
items.summary: This paper studies identification and estimation of the average partial effect in a correlated random coefficients panel data model where identification is irregular because the relevant density can degenerate at the origin. The authors extend a foundational framework by allowing the determinant of the regressor matrix to have a density that vanishes or diverges at zero at a polynomial rate, and they prove that the key parameters remain identified across this entire family of degeneracy conditions. They propose a three-step local polynomial estimator that fits time effects among "stayer" units, extrapolates a conditional mean just outside a trimming region, and then imputes these values back into the stayer region rather than discarding those observations. By exploiting higher-order smoothness through local polynomial regression of order greater than zero, the estimator achieves convergence rates substantially faster than the prior benchmark, with the rate approaching a limit that improves markedly as polynomial order increases, and joint asymptotic normality is established across three regimes defined by the sign of the degeneracy parameter. Simulations confirm reduced bias and root mean squared error, and the method is applied to reanalyze a markup model allowing for correlated random elasticities.
items.citation: Yelong Chen, Hua Jin, Yuxuan Ren. Local Polynomial Estimation in Irregular Correlated Random Coefficient Panel Data Models. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Every Edge Needs a Quote: Building a Quote-Grounded Knowledge Graph of Healthcare Software Adoption with Language-Model Agents
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of building a reliable knowledge graph of healthcare software adoption—specifically which hospitals use which products and which systems they integrate with—from publicly scattered web sources. The researchers developed a pipeline combining a deterministic crawl of vendor websites with a budget-constrained agent that searches the broader web, extracting customer and integration relationships only when each claim can be anchored to a verbatim quote from its source page. A layered verification stage employs referent resolution, deterministic string checks, and a voting panel of multiple model calls judging extracted relations against nine criteria to filter out incorrect claims. Evaluated against a page-level reference set of thousands of candidate relations, the pipeline achieved high precision and moderate recall, with a confidence score derived from the voting panel enabling a favorable precision-recall tradeoff. The paper also discusses how decomposing the task into narrow, bounded language-model calls with string-matched evidence and ensemble voting mitigates issues of long-context degradation and run-to-run variability.
items.citation: Juan Felipe Duran, Arthur Tobler, Martin Vallières. Every Edge Needs a Quote: Building a Quote-Grounded Knowledge Graph of Healthcare Software Adoption with Language-Model Agents. arXiv. 2026

items.title: When Agents Fail: Model or Harness--Who's to Blame?
items.summary: This paper investigates how to attribute performance failures in large language model agents to either the underlying model or the execution harness that orchestrates it, arguing that these two components must be evaluated together rather than in isolation. The authors developed a framework of five complementary measures capturing valid completion rates, model-harness fit, cross-model fit, interaction residuals, and token load to disentangle the contributions of each component. They tested four general-purpose harnesses paired with four core models across six benchmarks spanning diverse agentic challenges, generating a large collection of evaluation trajectories under varied conditions including stress tests and native model-harness baselines. The study found that harness rankings shift substantially depending on which model they are paired with and which benchmark is used, and that similar task performance scores can mask very different underlying execution profiles. The authors conclude that model-harness interactions should be evaluated explicitly, that models should be trained to transfer harness-use capabilities more effectively, and that harness designs should be adapted to specific models and tasks.
items.citation: Shao Zhang, Hangfan Zhang, Yuanyuan Shi et al.. When Agents Fail: Model or Harness--Who's to Blame?. arXiv. 2026

items.title: National-Scale Multimodal Accessibility Fields from Open Geospatial Data
items.summary: This paper presents MAPPER, an open-data computational pipeline designed to produce large-area, multimodal accessibility analyses in a reproducible and transparent manner. The system integrates walking, cycling, car, and public transport routing using OpenStreetMap and GTFS data, harmonizes points-of-interest and land-use layers, and computes continuous accessibility fields via network kernel density estimation, with outputs sampled to a uniform hexagonal grid. A key technical contribution is a high-performance compute core using contraction-hierarchy routing and parallel processing that makes national-scale analysis feasible on standard hardware. A full production run covering Germany generated a dataset of tens of millions of grid cells spanning nearly a thousand mode-layer combinations, and validation against an empirical mobility panel showed low mean bias for walking, cycling, and car modes, while public transport estimates were treated more cautiously. A regional case study in Bavaria applied the framework to evaluate accessibility to basic services under state spatial planning targets, revealing pronounced differences in accessibility depending on travel mode.
items.citation: Till Zacher, Louis Stille-Hönig, Markus Lienkamp. National-Scale Multimodal Accessibility Fields from Open Geospatial Data. arXiv. 2026

items.title: ALLMTS: Automated LLM-based Medical Triage System
items.summary: This paper investigated whether large language models can reliably perform telephone medical triage, a safety-critical task requiring a clinician to assign callers to appropriate levels of care ranging from ambulance dispatch to self-care at home. The authors developed ALLMTS, a system that does not ask a language model to reason about triage independently but instead uses it to select and execute the same commercially maintained telehealth guidelines that trained nurses follow, producing dispositions deterministically from the first positive answer to guideline assessment questions. The system was evaluated against a set of synthetic, expert-validated scenarios spanning a range of dispositions, with a curated subset released as an open benchmark and compared against a panel of nursing experts. ALLMTS achieved substantially higher accuracy than a raw language model baseline and reduced over-triage rates from as high as half of all cases in the baseline to nearly zero, while maintaining low under-triage rates comparable to expert nurses. The findings support a hybrid approach in which language model capabilities are constrained by executable clinical guidelines rather than used for unconstrained clinical reasoning.
items.citation: Michał Remigiusz Janiszewski, Artur Stopa, Łukasz Lenkiewicz et al.. ALLMTS: Automated LLM-based Medical Triage System. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Two Pentaplex Real-Time Fluorescent PCR Assays for Simultaneous Detection of Ten Ovine Respiratory and Reproductive Pathogens.
items.summary: The paper describes the development and validation of two pentaplex real-time fluorescent PCR assays designed to simultaneously detect ten important pathogens affecting sheep, covering both respiratory and reproductive disease categories. Each panel was designed to identify five distinct pathogens using multiple fluorescent detection channels, with targets including viruses, bacteria, and parasites. Laboratory validation demonstrated very low limits of detection, excellent linearity, and minimal variation within and between assays, along with high specificity and no cross-reactivity among the ten targets. Testing against a large collection of clinical samples from multiple geographic regions confirmed strong agreement with established reference diagnostic methods. The resulting multiplex assay offers a rapid and reliable approach for differential diagnosis and large-scale surveillance of major ovine pathogens.
items.citation: Wang S, Bai Z, Wan B et al.. Two Pentaplex Real-Time Fluorescent PCR Assays for Simultaneous Detection of Ten Ovine Respiratory and Reproductive Pathogens.. Viruses. 2026

items.title: Nanobodies: A Promising Toolkit for Diagnostic Applications
items.summary: This paper reviews nanobodies — single-domain antigen-binding fragments derived from camelid heavy-chain-only antibodies — as tools for diagnostic applications. The authors examine the structural and biochemical properties of nanobodies, including their small size, high solubility, and stability, which collectively enable recognition of less accessible epitopes and improved tissue penetration compared to conventional antibodies. The review surveys how nanobodies have been integrated into a broad range of detection platforms, encompassing immunoassay formats such as ELISA and lateral flow assays, biosensors, and in vivo imaging modalities including PET and SPECT. The authors also cover technical advances such as multivalent designs, site-specific conjugation, and optimized expression systems that have improved diagnostic performance, and they discuss ongoing clinical trials. The paper concludes by highlighting emerging strategies for developing scalable, sensitive, and application-ready nanobody-based diagnostic platforms.
items.citation: Wei Wu, Abid Ali, Li Sun et al.. Nanobodies: A Promising Toolkit for Diagnostic Applications. SmartMat. 2026

items.title: Machine-learning-integrated NLRC3 and cardiac troponin T dual-analyte lateral-flow biosensor for point-of-care acute coronary syndrome screening and acute myocardial infarction-unstable angina discrimination.
items.summary: This paper developed a point-of-care lateral-flow biosensor designed to both screen for acute coronary syndrome and distinguish between acute myocardial infarction and unstable angina, two tasks that remain difficult with existing troponin-based assays alone. The biosensor simultaneously measures two biomarkers — the inflammatory marker NLRC3 and the myocardial injury marker cardiac troponin T — using europium nanoparticle time-resolved fluorescence in a dual-channel format that returns results within twenty minutes. A Naïve Bayes machine-learning classifier was applied to integrate the two analyte signals and improve diagnostic discrimination beyond what either marker could achieve individually. In clinical evaluation, the combined dual-analyte approach outperformed NLRC3 alone, reaching improved sensitivity, specificity, and overall accuracy for differentiating acute myocardial infarction from unstable angina. The authors conclude that pairing inflammatory-risk detection with myocardial-injury detection in a single lateral-flow platform offers a practical decentralized triage tool for acute coronary syndrome.
items.citation: Gu X, Teng P, Li X et al.. Machine-learning-integrated NLRC3 and cardiac troponin T dual-analyte lateral-flow biosensor for point-of-care acute coronary syndrome screening and acute myocardial infarction-unstable angina discrimination.. Mikrochimica acta. 2026

items.title: Smartphone AI-Enabled Lateral Flow Immunoassay Platform Using Advanced Quantum Dots for Intelligent Quantitative Diagnostics.
items.citation: Atta S, Thorsen TL, Vasse T et al.. Smartphone AI-Enabled Lateral Flow Immunoassay Platform Using Advanced Quantum Dots for Intelligent Quantitative Diagnostics.. ACS applied materials & interfaces. 2026

items.title: Recent advances in lateral flow immunoassay for virus detection: current achievements, challenges and future prospects.
items.summary: This review examines the current state and future potential of lateral flow immunoassay technology for detecting viral pathogens in the context of global infectious disease management. The authors systematically surveyed recent advances across three areas: signal generation and transduction strategies using diverse nanomaterials such as colorimetric, fluorescent, magnetic, surface-enhanced Raman scattering, and photothermal systems; multimodal and multiplex detection approaches; and the integration of machine learning for signal interpretation and optimization. The review also covers applications of this technology in detecting viral antigens, antibodies, and nucleic acids. A central argument of the paper is that lateral flow immunoassay should be reconceptualized beyond a point-of-care testing tool and repositioned as a point-of-need self-testing platform capable of supporting large-scale epidemic surveillance and pandemic preparedness. The authors conclude by identifying current limitations including sensitivity, specificity, cost, and stability, while proposing future directions centered on advanced nanomaterials, intelligent data processing, and multi-target detection to strengthen decentralized diagnostic capacity globally.
items.citation: Li L, Liu F, He X et al.. Recent advances in lateral flow immunoassay for virus detection: current achievements, challenges and future prospects.. Talanta. 2026

items.title: Rational Control of Antibody Orientation for Enhancing Sensitivity and Specificity in Lateral Flow Immunoassays With Clinical Validation.
items.summary: This paper investigated strategies to improve the sensitivity and specificity of lateral flow immunoassays, which are commonly used in point-of-care diagnostics but are constrained by inefficient antibody orientation and poor signal transduction. The researchers developed a universal approach combining orientation-controlled antibody conjugation on immunoprobes with a biotin-streptavidin-modified test line to maximize antigen accessibility and reduce nonspecific binding and false-positive signals. This optimized configuration achieved dramatically lower detection limits for cancer biomarkers compared to conventional randomly conjugated probes, with sensitivity improvements on the order of more than an order of magnitude for the biomarkers tested. The strategy was validated across multiple clinically relevant cancer biomarkers and extended to a multiplexed fluorescent format enabling simultaneous detection of two analytes with minimal cross-reactivity. Clinical validation using patient serum samples demonstrated strong agreement with established hospital reference methods, supporting the practical utility of the approach.
items.citation: Wang PH, Shunmuga Nainar SN, Zhuang BH et al.. Rational Control of Antibody Orientation for Enhancing Sensitivity and Specificity in Lateral Flow Immunoassays With Clinical Validation.. Advanced healthcare materials. 2026

items.title: Ligand-directed Janus self-assembly with dual-aggregation enabling magneto-optical switching for enhanced lateral flow immunoassay.
items.citation: Liu T, Sun J, Huang J et al.. Ligand-directed Janus self-assembly with dual-aggregation enabling magneto-optical switching for enhanced lateral flow immunoassay.. Biosensors & bioelectronics. 2026

items.title: Synergistic Multicomponent Nucleopeptide-Based Hydrogels: Harnessing DNA-Base Pairing and Electrostatic Complementarities
items.summary: This study investigated hybrid molecules called nucleopeptides, which are short peptides functionalized with DNA nucleobases, as building blocks for multicomponent low-molecular-weight hydrogels. The researchers designed two series of peptides with complementary electrostatic charges at physiological pH, each functionalized with one of the four DNA nucleobases introduced via a peptide nucleic acid moiety, yielding six distinct compounds whose pairwise combinations could exploit both charge complementarity and nucleobase-pairing interactions. Through a systematic multiscale characterization, the team assessed how these two types of molecular complementarity influence hydrogel properties including gelation time, sol-gel transition temperature, mechanical stiffness, stress resistance, and fibrillar network morphology. The results demonstrated that deliberate selection of complementary components allows fine-tuning of hydrogel physicochemical and mechanical properties, while also revealing unexpected behaviors that highlight the complexity of these bioinspired multicomponent systems. Overall, the findings underscore the potential of combining electrostatic and nucleobase-pairing complementarities as a strategy for engineering high-performance supramolecular hydrogels.
items.citation: Tristan Giraud, Marine Koch, Paul Hoschtettler et al.. Synergistic Multicomponent Nucleopeptide-Based Hydrogels: Harnessing DNA-Base Pairing and Electrostatic Complementarities. ACS Materials Au. 2026

items.title: Microneedle array platforms for drug delivery and biomarker sensing: From skin mechanics guided design to scalable manufacture for clinical utility
items.summary: This review paper examines microneedle array platforms designed for transdermal and intradermal drug delivery and biomarker sensing, focusing on the gap between laboratory prototypes and clinically approved products. The authors analyze the competing mechanical design requirements of microneedles, which must be slender enough to penetrate skin painlessly yet robust enough to carry therapeutically relevant doses, alongside the anatomical and biomechanical properties of skin tissue that govern needle insertion. Fabrication methods are compared with attention to scalability, cost efficiency, and manufacturing throughput, while biocompatibility and dissolution behavior of microneedle materials in the dermal environment are also considered. The review further addresses applicator designs, their mechanisms of force delivery, and the regulatory science landscape that products must navigate to reach commercial approval. The authors conclude by highlighting the technical, commercial, and regulatory challenges that continue to hinder the translation of microneedle systems into self-applied, on-demand therapeutic products for patients.
items.citation: Jiachi Zhou, Lei Wu, Minna Wyttenbach et al.. Microneedle array platforms for drug delivery and biomarker sensing: From skin mechanics guided design to scalable manufacture for clinical utility. Journal of Controlled Release. 2026

items.title: Recent advances in Alzheimer’s disease: From molecular mechanisms to therapeutic strategies
items.summary: This review paper examines the current state of Alzheimer's disease research, covering both the biological mechanisms underlying the disease and emerging therapeutic approaches. The authors synthesize recent advances across several areas, including the role of apolipoprotein E biology, neuroimmunology, and biomarker discovery, alongside the classical hallmarks of amyloid plaques and neurofibrillary tangles. The review highlights that the pathological landscape of Alzheimer's disease is more complex than previously appreciated, involving a broad array of processes that together drive neurodegeneration and cognitive decline. New disease-modifying therapies capable of removing amyloid plaques from the brain have shown promise in slowing cognitive decline, though treatments that halt or prevent the disease entirely remain out of reach. The authors conclude that these collective advances are transforming how Alzheimer's disease is diagnosed and treated, raising the prospect that the condition may one day be both treatable and preventable.
items.citation: Michelle Diane Rudman, Jason D. Ulrich, David M. Holtzman. Recent advances in Alzheimer’s disease: From molecular mechanisms to therapeutic strategies. Cell. 2026

items.title: The Oral–Gut–Brain Axis: From Periodontal Dysbiosis to Neuroinflammation—Mechanistic Pathways, Salivary and Intestinal Biomarkers, and Therapeutic Targets: A Narrative Review
items.summary: This narrative review examined the proposed mechanistic connections between periodontal disease, gut microbiome disruption, and neuroinflammation, conceptualized as the oral–gut–brain axis. The authors synthesized evidence from a broad literature search to characterize how periodontal dysbiosis—driven particularly by pathogens such as Porphyromonas gingivalis and Fusobacterium nucleatum—may propagate systemic inflammation through disruption of intestinal barrier integrity, alteration of microbial composition, and subsequent effects on blood–brain barrier permeability and neuroinflammatory processes including microglial activation and amyloid-beta accumulation. The review also evaluated salivary and intestinal biomarkers as potential non-invasive tools for monitoring inflammatory burden across this tripartite pathway, and identified pharmacological targets within it. The authors found that while the oral–gut–brain axis offers a plausible integrative framework linking periodontal, cardiometabolic, and neurodegenerative diseases through shared low-grade chronic inflammation, the existing evidence remains largely associative and derived predominantly from preclinical models. They conclude that longitudinal human studies are needed to establish causal directionality, and that salivary biomarkers represent promising candidates for systemic risk screening pending further clinical validation.
items.citation: Caterina Nela Dumitru, Alina Oana Dumitru, Gabriel Valeriu Popa et al.. The Oral–Gut–Brain Axis: From Periodontal Dysbiosis to Neuroinflammation—Mechanistic Pathways, Salivary and Intestinal Biomarkers, and Therapeutic Targets: A Narrative Review. Dentistry Journal. 2026

items.title: Hantavirus Emergence in a Changing World: Virology, Pathogenesis, Surveillance, and One Health Preparedness
items.summary: This review examines hantaviruses as emerging rodent-borne pathogens responsible for hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome and hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome, synthesizing current knowledge across virology, epidemiology, pathogenesis, clinical presentation, and diagnostics. The authors analyze how environmental change, climate variability, urbanization, and land-use transformation drive rodent reservoir dynamics and increase spillover risk to human populations. Particular attention is given to surveillance and diagnostic gaps in tropical and Caribbean regions where hantavirus circulation is likely underrecognized. The review also covers advances in molecular diagnostics, genomic surveillance, vaccine development, monoclonal antibody therapies, and climate-based early warning systems. The authors argue that integrated One Health surveillance combining human, animal, and environmental monitoring, alongside strengthened laboratory capacity and regional collaboration, is essential for reducing the global burden of hantavirus disease and improving preparedness for future zoonotic threats.
items.citation: Maria E. Ramos‐Niño, Nicolette Chiem, Prakash V. A. K. Ramdass. Hantavirus Emergence in a Changing World: Virology, Pathogenesis, Surveillance, and One Health Preparedness. Microorganisms. 2026

items.title: Fréchet Kriging for Metric Space-Valued Spatial Data
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of spatial prediction for data that belong to general metric spaces rather than traditional Euclidean settings, such as probability distributions, symmetric positive definite matrices, and network-valued data. The authors introduce Fréchet kriging, a framework that extends classical ordinary kriging by replacing the weighted average with a weighted Fréchet mean while characterizing spatial dependence through a generalized variogram, thereby preserving the intrinsic geometry of the data space without requiring embedding into a linear space. Theoretical properties are established, including a surrogate optimality result and consistency of the predictor under variogram misspecification given suitable regularity conditions. Simulation studies for distributional and matrix-valued data show that Fréchet kriging performs favorably compared to existing approaches. The method is further demonstrated on real-world applications involving temperature exceedance probabilities, joint temperature density functions, and inter-industry monetary flow networks.
items.citation: Ryo Okano, Daisuke Kurisu, Hans-Georg Müller. Fréchet Kriging for Metric Space-Valued Spatial Data. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Flownomaly: Single-Step Conditional-Mean Recovery for Few-Shot Anomaly Detection
items.summary: The paper addresses few-shot industrial anomaly detection, where a model must learn what "normal" looks like from only a small number of defect-free images without access to any anomalous examples during training or validation. The proposed method, Flownomaly, frames the problem as recovering a normal counterpart for a query image by learning a velocity field through conditional flow matching over frozen patch-level features from a pretrained vision model, allowing transport of Gaussian noise toward normal feature distributions. A key contribution is that inference requires only a single evaluation of the learned field rather than full trajectory integration, and a normal-only criterion based on Jacobian gain-to-noise ratio automatically selects the operating time without needing anomalous validation samples. Anomaly signals for both pixel-level localization and image-level detection are derived from squared residuals between query tokens and their recovered normal counterparts. Evaluated across standard few-shot benchmarks, the method achieves state-of-the-art performance against category-specific approaches, with notable gains in image-level detection on challenging datasets.
items.citation: Bernardo Perrone Ribeiro, Erkut Akdag, Egor Bondarev. Flownomaly: Single-Step Conditional-Mean Recovery for Few-Shot Anomaly Detection. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A probabilistic approach to separate mergers and jellyfish galaxies: Application of morphological non-parametric indexes to the DESI Legacy Survey
items.summary: This paper investigated how non-parametric morphological indices can be used to classify galaxies into regular spirals, regular ellipticals, mergers, and jellyfish galaxies (ram-pressure stripping candidates) using imaging from the DESI Legacy Surveys. The authors measured ten non-parametric morphological indices and evaluated their discriminating power using two-dimensional diagnostic planes assessed with a cross-validated Bayesian kernel-density classifier, then combined all indices using calibrated gradient-boosted machine learning models. They found that planes combining Shannon entropy with either the moment of light or asymmetry indices best separated regular from perturbed galaxies, while distinguishing mergers from jellyfish candidates proved more difficult and benefited most from combinations involving concentration. The multi-class machine learning models achieved strong performance for three-class separation but lower accuracy when mergers and jellyfish were treated as distinct classes, reflecting that jellyfish galaxies occupy a relatively coherent region of morphological parameter space while mergers display diverse and overlapping morphologies. The study ultimately produced probabilistic classifications for nearly two million galaxies, demonstrating that non-parametric morphology reliably identifies structural disturbance but struggles to pinpoint its physical origin.
items.citation: V. M. Sampaio, Y. Jaff'e, A. Moretti et al.. A probabilistic approach to separate mergers and jellyfish galaxies: Application of morphological non-parametric indexes to the DESI Legacy Survey. arXiv. 2026

items.title: CoupleFlow: Null-Calibrated Auditory Attention Decoding With Time-Locked Brain-Speech Coupling and Flow-Matching Likelihood Ratios
items.summary: This paper addresses auditory attention decoding, the task of identifying which talker a listener is attending to based on brief noninvasive brain recordings, and demonstrates that recently reported near-perfect decoding accuracies stem from methodological artifacts rather than genuine neural signals. The authors show that existing models exploit trial leakage, eye gaze, and acoustic cues rather than speech-evoked neural activity, causing performance to collapse when tested on unseen speech. To address this, they developed CoupleFlow, a method that decodes attention through temporal coupling between neural and acoustic embeddings using conditional flow matching and a likelihood ratio decision rule grounded in pointwise mutual information, which is theoretically Bayes optimal and produces chance-level predictions when no genuine brain-speech coupling is present. CoupleFlow was evaluated across nine electroencephalography and magnetoencephalography datasets spanning multiple languages, listener populations including those with hearing impairment, and various recording conditions, consistently outperforming linear and deep learning baselines while passing null tests that verify the absence of shortcut learning. Additionally, the authors derived an evidence accumulation law relating decoding accuracy to window length through a single dataset-specific parameter linked to the strength of neural speech tracking, framing recording signal-to-noise ratio as the fundamental limit on decoding speed and reliability.
items.citation: Ali Alavi, Donald S. Williamson. CoupleFlow: Null-Calibrated Auditory Attention Decoding With Time-Locked Brain-Speech Coupling and Flow-Matching Likelihood Ratios. arXiv. 2026

items.title: If at First You Don't Succeed, Backtrack: Lightweight Recovery for Frozen VLAs
items.summary: This paper addresses the brittleness of Vision-Language-Action models in robotic manipulation, specifically their tendency to fail when their own actions push them into states underrepresented in training data. The authors propose Backtrack, a lightweight mechanism that attaches a small failure prediction head to a frozen, unmodified policy, training this head solely on outcome-labeled rollouts to read the policy's internal representations and estimate the probability of episode failure. When predicted failure probability exceeds a threshold, the system pauses the policy, physically retraces the robot arm's recent motion, and then resumes the original policy from the earlier configuration to retry. Evaluated across multiple benchmark suites and three distinct policy architectures spanning two action-generation families, Backtrack substantially reduces failure rates on long-horizon multi-step tasks while having a more modest effect where policies already perform near ceiling. The approach requires no recovery demonstrations, policy retraining, or additional inference-time models, and adds only a negligible fraction to the policy's parameter count.
items.citation: Thomas Landeg, Thierry Tambe. If at First You Don't Succeed, Backtrack: Lightweight Recovery for Frozen VLAs. arXiv. 2026

items.title: What Mean Error Misses: Device-Clock Diagnostics for Evaluating Eye Tracking across Three Virtual Reality Headsets
items.summary: This paper evaluated the accuracy and reliability of eye tracking across three virtual reality headsets by having participants complete standardized gaze tasks on each device. The researchers compared spatial accuracy, data quality, and temporal characteristics of the Meta Quest Pro, HTC VIVE Pro Eye, and HTC VIVE Focus Vision, with the last representing a novel evaluation. They found meaningful differences in mean gaze error across devices, with the Focus Vision performing least accurately even after recalibration, and the VIVE Pro Eye showing sensitivity to background luminance. Beyond spatial accuracy, the study revealed critical device-clock anomalies that standard mean error metrics obscure, including lengthy data pauses on the Meta Quest Pro, sample skipping on the Focus Vision, and the Meta Quest Pro falsely flagging gaze samples as valid during deliberate eye closures. The authors conclude that eye tracker evaluations should adopt more comprehensive reporting standards that include temporal data integrity, loss composition assessed via device clocks, and validity flagging behavior during eye closures.
items.citation: Aleksandr Chernysh, Mehedi Hasan Raju, Kamrul Hasan et al.. What Mean Error Misses: Device-Clock Diagnostics for Evaluating Eye Tracking across Three Virtual Reality Headsets. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Beyond lateral flow: vertical flow immunoassays as thermodynamically assisted rapid diagnostics.
items.summary: This review examines vertical flow immunoassays (VFAs) as an advanced alternative to the dominant lateral flow immunoassay format used in point-of-care diagnostics. The authors analyze how the conventional lateral flow architecture suffers from four fundamental physical limitations—poor analyte capture kinetics, high non-specific background, one-dimensional multiplexing with analyte depletion, and the hook effect at high analyte concentrations—and how VFAs address each of these through a stacked-membrane design that separates convective delivery from immunoreaction kinetics. They review how this architecture enables highly selective thermodynamic washing, two-dimensional multiplexing arrays, and elimination of the hook effect, while coupling with signal enhancement technologies such as surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy, electrochemical transduction, nanoparticle amplification, and deep-learning inference pushes sensitivity into the sub-picogram-per-milliliter range. Head-to-head comparisons with chemistry-matched lateral flow assays demonstrate large improvements in detection limits in favor of VFAs. Despite this substantial sensitivity advantage, the review identifies the engineering and commercial barriers that have prevented widespread adoption and outlines a pathway toward practical deployment across clinical diagnostics, food safety, and environmental monitoring.
items.citation: Nainar SNS, Chu YY, Lin HC et al.. Beyond lateral flow: vertical flow immunoassays as thermodynamically assisted rapid diagnostics.. Chemical communications (Cambridge, England). 2026

items.title: Validation and performance of a rapid HIV-1 viral load assay.
items.summary: The paper investigated whether a rapid quantitative nucleic acid test, the Xpert HIV-1 Viral Load XC assay, could serve as a primary diagnostic tool within HIV-1 testing workflows, potentially enabling both diagnosis and viral load measurement in a single clinical encounter. The researchers evaluated the assay's analytical range, precision, and agreement against standard-of-care platforms, as well as four other HIV assays, using HIV-positive and HIV-negative plasma samples. The assay demonstrated strong linearity across its measurable range and showed complete agreement with a reference quantitative assay on a panel of positive and negative samples, while achieving turnaround times far shorter than conventional batch testing. However, positive agreement with other comparator assays was imperfect, with most discrepancies occurring in samples below the lower limit of quantification, and the assay produced a small proportion of invalid results. The findings suggest that while rapid molecular HIV diagnostics offer meaningful advantages for linkage to care, current limitations in sensitivity at low viral loads highlight the need for continued development of approaches that are both rapid and highly sensitive.
items.citation: Uhteg K, Bayan MH, Boudreau A et al.. Validation and performance of a rapid HIV-1 viral load assay.. Microbiology spectrum. 2026

items.title: Patient perspectives on point-of-care HIV nucleic acid tests for viral load monitoring in Seattle, WA.
items.summary: This study examined patient perspectives on using point-of-care nucleic acid testing for HIV viral load monitoring as a faster alternative to standard laboratory-based tests, which can take days to return results. Participants receiving a semi-quantitative point-of-care test through a dedicated study protocol completed acceptability surveys and in-depth interviews about their experiences with the technology. Patients generally found the point-of-care approach acceptable and preferred its faster turnaround time and the convenience of fingerstick blood collection performed directly in the clinic compared to conventional viral load testing. However, participants expressed a preference for an even shorter result turnaround and a lower limit of detection than the tested device currently offers. The authors conclude that point-of-care nucleic acid testing holds promise for people with HIV, particularly those incompletely engaged in care, but that improvements in detection sensitivity and speed would be needed for optimal implementation in United States clinical settings.
items.citation: Niemann LA, Murphy M, Violette LR et al.. Patient perspectives on point-of-care HIV nucleic acid tests for viral load monitoring in Seattle, WA.. AIDS care. 2026

items.title: Feasibility, Acceptability, and Test Performance of Point-of-Care Nucleic Acid Tests for HIV Testing and Viral Load Monitoring in the United States: Prospective Longitudinal Mixed-Methods Study.
items.summary: This paper describes the design and enrollment procedures of the GAIN study, a prospective longitudinal mixed-methods investigation evaluating point-of-care nucleic acid tests for HIV diagnosis and viral load monitoring in clinical and community settings in the United States. The study enrolled participants across two sites in Seattle, Washington, including individuals seeking HIV testing, pre-exposure prophylaxis, or post-exposure prophylaxis, as well as people already living with HIV, and assessed both a qualitative and a semiquantitative whole blood point-of-care nucleic acid test alongside standard laboratory testing. A randomized clinical trial component compared standard care with and without the addition of point-of-care viral load monitoring for people with HIV, while qualitative interviews and acceptability surveys captured participant perspectives on the testing approach. The abstract presents only the study protocol and enrollment figures, noting that analyses of test performance, clinical outcomes, and acceptability data are anticipated in future publications. As such, no findings or conclusions regarding feasibility, acceptability, or diagnostic performance are yet available from this report.
items.citation: Niemann LA, Violette LR, Cornelius-Hudson A et al.. Feasibility, Acceptability, and Test Performance of Point-of-Care Nucleic Acid Tests for HIV Testing and Viral Load Monitoring in the United States: Prospective Longitudinal Mixed-Methods Study.. JMIR research protocols. 2026

items.title: Can exercise affect immune function to increase susceptibility to infection?
items.summary: This debate article examined the longstanding question in exercise immunology of whether exercise itself can suppress immune function and increase susceptibility to infection. The paper contrasted evidence that regular moderate-intensity exercise benefits immune defense, particularly in older and chronically ill individuals, with observations that high-performance athletes and military personnel experience elevated infection burdens during intense training periods. Opposing expert groups contested whether athletes are genuinely more infection-prone than the general population, whether exercise independently drives increased infection risk apart from confounding factors such as sleep disruption, nutritional deficits, anxiety, and environmental extremes, and whether current biomarkers and study designs are adequate to address these questions. Both sides agreed that infection susceptibility is multifactorial in origin, but the debate left unresolved whether arduous exercise is itself a causative contributor to elevated infection risk. The authors conclude that more rigorous empirical research is needed to disentangle the specific immunological effects of exercise from the many overlapping stressors present in high-performance and military populations.
items.citation: Richard J. Simpson, Richard J. Simpson, Maree Gleeson et al.. Can exercise affect immune function to increase susceptibility to infection?. PubMed. 2026

items.title: Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications
items.summary: This review examines how the integration of multiomics technologies and artificial intelligence is reshaping precision drug discovery and translational medicine. The authors surveyed multiomics approaches encompassing genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic methodologies alongside AI techniques such as deep learning to analyze how these tools are being applied across the drug development pipeline. The review covers specific applications including target deconvolution, drug repositioning, de novo compound discovery, virtual screening, pharmacokinetic modeling, and safety assessment, with case illustrations drawn from oncology, neurodegenerative diseases, and cardiovascular conditions. The authors find that combining multiomics data with AI accelerates target identification, streamlines lead optimization, and enables more precise clinical trial design, while also acknowledging persistent challenges such as harmonizing disparate data streams, ensuring reproducibility, and mitigating algorithmic biases. They conclude that the convergence of these technologies opens new pathways for therapeutic innovation and marks a new era in bench-to-clinic translational medicine.
items.citation: Yuqing Liu, Kun Zhu, Weijun Peng et al.. Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: Trial design and end points in hepatocellular carcinoma: an EASL–AASLD–ILCA consensus statement
items.citation: Josep Maria Llovet, Ezequiel Mauro, Lorenza Rimassa et al.. Trial design and end points in hepatocellular carcinoma: an EASL–AASLD–ILCA consensus statement. Nature Reviews Clinical Oncology. 2026

items.title: CRISPR-Cas systems as next-generation antimicrobials: a systemic review of mechanisms, delivery strategies, and translational challenges
items.summary: This systematic review examined the potential of CRISPR-Cas systems as precision antimicrobials against multidrug-resistant bacteria, evaluating their mechanisms of action, delivery strategies, preclinical evidence, and translational challenges. The authors synthesized findings from preclinical studies investigating CRISPR effectors — including Cas9, Cas12, and Cas13 — applied to antibacterial killing or antibiotic resensitization across various bacterial targets and delivery platforms. The reviewed studies demonstrated that CRISPR-Cas systems could effectively eliminate or resensitize resistant bacteria through mechanisms such as chromosomal double-strand break induction, resistance plasmid curing, and RNA-targeted cleavage, with phage-mediated delivery showing the most consistent efficacy. One CRISPR-enhanced engineered bacteriophage cocktail has advanced to clinical evaluation, reflecting the field's translational momentum. Despite promising results, significant obstacles remain, including limited bacterial host range, physiological instability, emergence of escape mutations, and insufficient safety data, and the authors conclude that overcoming these barriers will require optimized delivery platforms, multiplex targeting approaches, and standardized regulatory frameworks.
items.citation: Maha S.I. Wizrah. CRISPR-Cas systems as next-generation antimicrobials: a systemic review of mechanisms, delivery strategies, and translational challenges. Frontiers in Microbiology. 2026

items.title: European consensus-based interdisciplinary guideline for invasive cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma. Part 1: Diagnostics and prevention – Update 2026
items.summary: This paper presents an updated European consensus guideline for the diagnostics and prevention of invasive cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma, one of the most common cancers in white populations. A multidisciplinary collaboration of experts from several major European oncology and dermatology organizations revised recommendations based on current literature and expert consensus, updating a previous version from 2023. The guideline introduces a new classification system dividing difficult-to-treat cases into five distinct groups, ranging from complex common tumors through locally advanced disease to locoregional and distant metastatic disease. Diagnostic evaluation proceeds in three steps: initial clinical and dermatoscopic assessment confirmed by histopathology, followed by staging procedures including physical examination and imaging where indicated, and finally integration of findings into established staging systems. Prevention recommendations include oral nicotinamide and sun protection measures, and the guideline addresses both immunocompetent and immunosuppressed patient populations.
items.citation: Alexander J. Stratigos, Clio Dessinioti, Claus Garbe et al.. European consensus-based interdisciplinary guideline for invasive cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma. Part 1: Diagnostics and prevention – Update 2026. European Journal of Cancer. 2026

items.title: APASL clinical practice guidelines on the management of chronic hepatitis B infection: a 2026 update
