items.summary: This paper presents updated clinical practice guidelines from the Asian Pacific Association for the Study of the Liver (APASL) for the management of chronic hepatitis B infection. The guidelines were developed by a dedicated Viral Elimination Taskforce comprising key opinion leaders across member countries and regions in response to the persistent and growing burden of hepatitis B-related complications, including acute-on-chronic liver failure, end-stage cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma. The taskforce incorporated evolving epidemiological trends, socioeconomic considerations, and technological advances into the guideline development process. The resulting document provides recommendations across multiple major areas encompassing screening, vaccination, antiviral treatment, and hepatocellular carcinoma surveillance, with an emphasis on practical and cost-effective decision-making for healthcare professionals, policymakers, and patients. The guidelines represent a coordinated regional effort aimed at reducing the disease burden of chronic hepatitis B and advancing elimination goals across the Asia Pacific region.
items.citation: Hong You, Rakhi Maiwall, Jing Chen et al.. APASL clinical practice guidelines on the management of chronic hepatitis B infection: a 2026 update. Hepatology International. 2026

items.title: Reducing 6G Energy Consumption: TDD-Aligned Drain Voltage Modulation for Power Amplifiers
items.summary: This paper addresses the energy inefficiency of power amplifiers in base stations, which waste supply headroom when operating at partial load back-off from peak output power. The authors propose TDD-Aligned Drain Voltage Modulation, a scheme that selects an appropriate drain voltage level once per Time-Division Duplex period based on downlink resource utilization, switching voltages during the uplink window to avoid costly frequent hardware switching. The approach is paired with a previously developed link adaptation technique called POLITE, which spreads transmit power across unused resources to shift the power amplifier into a regime where a lower drain voltage is sufficient. Using system-level simulations based on a standardized urban macro scenario, the authors evaluated their scheme across a range of traffic loads and compared it against conventional approaches. They found that TDD-Aligned Drain Voltage Modulation combined with POLITE achieves substantial power savings while maintaining packet failure performance comparable to full drain voltage operation, reaching approximately half the gain of an idealized reference scheme.
items.citation: Meizhen Zhuo, Gunter Wolff, Stephan ten Brink et al.. Reducing 6G Energy Consumption: TDD-Aligned Drain Voltage Modulation for Power Amplifiers. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Multi-Timescale Context-Aware Radio Resource Optimization for Harmonious NTN-TN Coexistence: A Digital Twin and Open RAN Enabled Framework
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of harmful interference that terrestrial network downlink transmissions can cause to low-Earth orbit satellite receivers when non-terrestrial and terrestrial networks must coexist in future wireless systems. The authors developed DT-STABLE, a framework combining digital twin technology with Open Radio Access Network architecture to enable context-aware, proactive interference management using site-specific environmental information rather than continuous real-time measurements. The framework jointly optimizes beam activation and user association under radio frequency chain constraints, load balancing requirements, and aggregate satellite interference limits, with the authors proving this joint optimization problem is NP-hard before proposing an efficient scheduling algorithm. DT-STABLE operates across multiple timescales, coupling short-timescale radio resource adaptation with periodic digital twin updates through standardized interfaces. Simulations at millimeter-wave frequencies under demanding satellite geometry conditions demonstrated high interference constraint satisfaction rates, competitive spectral efficiency, dramatic reductions in beam measurement overhead compared to exhaustive approaches, and substantially faster computation relative to exact optimization benchmarks.
items.citation: Ecem Izde Kaya, Md. Zoheb Hassan, Georges Kaddoum. Multi-Timescale Context-Aware Radio Resource Optimization for Harmonious NTN-TN Coexistence: A Digital Twin and Open RAN Enabled Framework. arXiv. 2026

items.title: CARES: Coverage-Aware Replay Exemplar Selection for Continual Learning
items.summary: This paper addresses the problem of catastrophic forgetting in continual learning, specifically focusing on how to construct an effective replay buffer under a fixed memory budget. The authors propose CARES, a method that selects buffer exemplars by exploiting the geometric structure of a frozen pretrained feature space through class-aware, density-weighted coverage, entirely avoiding repeated optimization of the continual model during buffer updates. Unlike recent coreset-based approaches that rely on model-derived gradients or auxiliary optimization and incur heavy computational costs, CARES operates without any training signal from the continual learner. The method is evaluated across diverse conditions including balanced, imbalanced, and label-noisy data streams in both online class-incremental and task-incremental settings, achieving substantially faster buffer selection than existing coreset methods. Despite using no continual learning signal, CARES matches or surpasses state-of-the-art baselines across these settings, with particularly notable gains under class imbalance conditions.
items.citation: Arundhati S. Shanbhag, Brian B. Moser, Federico Raue et al.. CARES: Coverage-Aware Replay Exemplar Selection for Continual Learning. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Generalization properties of the token perceptron: the role of embedding and vocabulary
items.summary: This paper investigates how the geometry of token embeddings influences the learning and generalization properties of language model-like systems, framed as a classification problem over a finite vocabulary. The authors introduce a minimal model called the token perceptron, a linear predictor that maps sequences of embedded tokens to an output through position-specific matrices, and analyze it in a teacher-student framework. Using the replica method, they derive exact generalization error expressions in the limit of many positions while keeping the embedding dimension and vocabulary size finite. For continuous embeddings on a hypersphere, they find that the teacher weights can be perfectly recovered above a critical sample complexity that scales with the square of the embedding dimension, and that spherical cross-entropy achieves this threshold at large inverse temperature. For discrete vocabulary embeddings, where each training example constrains the output to a Voronoi cell rather than a precise direction, they derive the Bayes-optimal error and show that the optimal learner preferentially resolves the directions of greatest variance in the embedding matrix, even when the teacher is isotropic.
items.citation: Dario Bocchi, Matteo Negri, Flavio Nicoletti et al.. Generalization properties of the token perceptron: the role of embedding and vocabulary. arXiv. 2026

items.title: The solution of the Hopfield model with Gaussian patterns
items.summary: The paper studies the Hopfield neural network model with Gaussian-distributed patterns, a variant of the classical associative memory model, with the goal of rigorously establishing its thermodynamic behavior across all memory loads and temperatures. By applying a Hubbard–Stratonovich transformation, the authors map the model onto a system of Ising spins coupled to Gaussian hidden units, reducing it to an Ising-spherical spin glass that can be solved exactly through an explicit variational principle for the free energy. This framework recovers the classical Amit–Gutfreund–Sompolinsky replica-symmetric theory as a special case while also identifying a rigorous boundary of the annealed region, selecting a unique spin-glass solution among the AGS equations, and providing an equation of state for a new thermodynamic variable characterizing the hidden layer. The authors further prove that below this temperature boundary, replica symmetry is broken throughout the phase diagram, and they connect this instability to the de Almeida–Thouless condition of the Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model. The work thereby places the thermodynamics of the Gaussian Hopfield model on a rigorous mathematical footing while clarifying the structure of its spin-glass phase.
items.citation: Francesco Camilli, Pierluigi Contucci, Emanuele Mingione. The solution of the Hopfield model with Gaussian patterns. arXiv. 2026

items.title: When Agents Fail: Model or Harness--Who's to Blame?
items.summary: This paper investigates how to attribute performance failures in large language model agent systems, where a model and an execution harness jointly determine benchmark outcomes. The authors argue that harnesses cannot be evaluated independently of the models they are paired with, and they develop a framework of five complementary measures capturing valid completion rates, model-harness fit, cross-model fit, interaction residuals, and token load. They applied this framework across four general-purpose harnesses and four core models on six benchmarks spanning diverse agentic capabilities, generating a large set of evaluation trajectories. Key findings show that harness rankings shift depending on the model and benchmark used, that task performance and valid completion do not always favor the same pairings, and that similar task scores can conceal very different execution profiles. The authors conclude that evaluating model-harness interactions as a unit is essential, and advocate for training models with transferable harness-use capabilities alongside harness designs tailored to specific models and tasks.
items.citation: Shao Zhang, Hangfan Zhang, Yuanyuan Shi et al.. When Agents Fail: Model or Harness--Who's to Blame?. arXiv. 2026

items.title: An Evaluation of Perinatal Human Immunodeficiency Virus Transmissions in New York State, 2007-2020.
items.summary: This population-based retrospective cohort study examined predictors of perinatal HIV transmission and unsuppressed viral load near delivery among birthing parents living with HIV in New York State over a roughly fourteen-year period. Using linked surveillance, laboratory, and medical record data, researchers applied multivariable models to identify factors associated with both transmission and viral non-suppression. The overall rate of perinatal HIV transmission was very low, yet unsuppressed viral load at the test closest to delivery was the strongest predictor of transmission. Key predictors of having an unsuppressed viral load included not using antiretroviral therapy during pregnancy, documented illicit substance use during pregnancy, and later initiation of prenatal care. The findings highlight that while perinatal transmission has become rare, targeting viral suppression through early prenatal engagement, antiretroviral therapy uptake, and substance use support remains critical for eliminating the remaining cases.
items.citation: Swain CA, Wong C, Stolz A et al.. An Evaluation of Perinatal Human Immunodeficiency Virus Transmissions in New York State, 2007-2020.. O&G open. 2026

items.title: A Multistate Analysis of Longitudinal Care Outcomes Among People Newly Linked to Human Immunodeficiency Virus Care in Missouri.
items.summary: This study examined longitudinal patterns of HIV care engagement and viral suppression among people newly linked to HIV care in Missouri, a priority state under the Ending the HIV Epidemic initiative. Using multistate analytic methods applied to clinic records over three years following linkage, researchers tracked individuals across nine mutually exclusive states defined by clinic engagement and viral load status. They found that by one year after linkage, a substantial proportion of patients had disengaged from care, with reengaged individuals showing meaningfully lower rates of viral suppression compared to those continuously retained. Younger individuals and those from historically marginalized communities faced elevated risks of disengagement, reengagement, and viremia. The authors conclude that longitudinal methods reveal important treatment gaps obscured by routine cross-sectional reporting, and argue that HIV care efforts should prioritize sustained long-term engagement rather than focusing narrowly on preventing isolated missed appointments.
items.citation: Ramakrishnan A, Vo D, Barrette EP et al.. A Multistate Analysis of Longitudinal Care Outcomes Among People Newly Linked to Human Immunodeficiency Virus Care in Missouri.. Open forum infectious diseases. 2026

items.title: Association Between Housing Instability and HIV Care Outcomes Among People With HIV in the United States.
items.summary: This study examined how housing instability affects HIV care outcomes among people with HIV who were already engaged in clinical care across the United States. Using clinical and patient-reported data from a large multi-site cohort collected between 2019 and 2025, the researchers applied regression analyses to assess relationships between self-reported housing status and key markers including viral suppression, antiretroviral therapy use and adherence, and CD4 cell count. Roughly one in ten participants reported some form of housing instability, and those experiencing homelessness or unstable housing had meaningfully lower rates of viral suppression, reduced antiretroviral use and adherence, and lower CD4 counts compared to stably housed individuals. These associations persisted after adjustment for demographic factors and when stratified by substance use and depression status. The findings underscore that lack of stable housing functions as a structural barrier to effective HIV management even among those already receiving care, with implications for efforts to end the HIV epidemic in the United States.
items.venue: Journal of acquired immune deficiency syndromes (1999)
items.citation: Fahey CA, Whitney BM, Drumright LN et al.. Association Between Housing Instability and HIV Care Outcomes Among People With HIV in the United States.. Journal of acquired immune deficiency syndromes (1999). 2026

items.title: A qualitative study exploring factors associated with the accuracy of recording malaria rapid diagnostic test results in two high-burden regions of Côte d'Ivoire.
items.summary: This study investigated why healthcare workers in two high-burden regions of Côte d'Ivoire sometimes fail to accurately record malaria rapid diagnostic test results, a problem that undermines surveillance data quality. Using a qualitative approach embedded within a broader mixed-methods evaluation, researchers photographed RDTs performed by healthcare workers and had them independently interpreted by an external panel, then conducted semi-structured interviews with workers whose self-recorded results showed either high or low agreement with the external readings. The primary factor distinguishing the two groups was not a lack of knowledge or access to guidelines, but rather differing levels of confidence in negative RDT results, particularly fear that a negative result in a symptomatic patient might be a false negative with serious consequences. Workers with low agreement more frequently reported prescribing antimalarials despite negative results and deliberately falsifying register entries—such as recording negative results as positive—to align documentation with their treatment decisions. The authors conclude that interventions should focus on improving clinical decision-making for RDT-negative fevers, expanding non-malarial diagnostic options, and redesigning documentation systems to allow transparent recording of guideline non-adherence without creating incentives for misreporting.
items.citation: Kouakou OMA, Bédia-Tanoh VA, Arnzen A et al.. A qualitative study exploring factors associated with the accuracy of recording malaria rapid diagnostic test results in two high-burden regions of Côte d'Ivoire.. Malaria journal. 2026

items.title: Comparative evaluation of a multi-antigen malaria rapid diagnostic test against qPCR and microscopy in a co-endemic area of Southern Ethiopia.
items.summary: This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of a new multi-antigen rapid diagnostic test for malaria in a region of southern Ethiopia where both *Plasmodium falciparum* and *Plasmodium vivax* co-circulate, and where limitations of conventional HRP2-based tests are well recognized. Researchers enrolled febrile patients from health facilities during peak transmission season and compared the multi-antigen test, which detects HRP2 and dual pLDH markers for both species, against conventional RDTs, expert microscopy, and quantitative PCR. The multi-antigen RDT showed high specificity and strong agreement with microscopy, but its sensitivity declined when qPCR served as the reference standard, revealing that submicroscopic, low-density infections were frequently missed. qPCR identified the highest overall malaria prevalence and detected more species-specific and mixed infections than either microscopy or the RDT. The authors conclude that while the multi-antigen RDT is suitable for routine clinical diagnosis, more sensitive tools are needed for malaria surveillance and elimination efforts in endemic settings.
items.citation: Bogale A, Mitiku A, Tefera S et al.. Comparative evaluation of a multi-antigen malaria rapid diagnostic test against qPCR and microscopy in a co-endemic area of Southern Ethiopia.. Scientific reports. 2026

items.title: The spatial proteome of the Plasmodium falciparum schizont illuminates the composition and evolutionary trajectories of its organelles
items.summary: This paper investigated the spatial organization of proteins within the malaria parasite *Plasmodium falciparum* during its invasive erythrocytic schizont stage, aiming to address the large proportion of parasite proteins with unknown cellular location or function. The researchers applied a high-resolution spatial proteomics approach called hyperLOPIT combined with supervised machine learning to map the subcellular localization of thousands of parasite proteins, including those found within compartments of the infected host red blood cell. The resulting maps resolved a large number of distinct cellular compartments and successfully assigned a substantial fraction of the detected proteome to specific niches. By integrating these localization data with comparative genomic analyses, the study illuminated the evolutionary trajectories of *Plasmodium* organelles and the adaptive pressures shaping parasite biology. The work provides a comprehensive resource for understanding the unique cellular architecture that underpins the parasite's ability to invade and develop within erythrocytes.
items.citation: Scott A. Chisholm, Victor Flores, Alison Kemp et al.. The spatial proteome of the Plasmodium falciparum schizont illuminates the composition and evolutionary trajectories of its organelles. Nature Communications. 2026

items.title: Real‐world comprehensive care of people living with schizophrenia: recommendations across different settings and clinical stages
items.summary: This paper addresses the global challenge of managing schizophrenia by developing the first comprehensive, real-world care recommendations spanning different clinical stages, treatment approaches, and resource settings. The recommendations were produced through a critical review of scientific literature combined with collaborative input from clinical academics treating people with schizophrenia across diverse countries and settings, including the Global South, with involvement from people with lived experience. The resulting framework covers a broad range of care domains, including early detection, pharmacological and psychological treatments, psychosocial interventions, community and inpatient care, and population-level prevention. A central recommendation is to implement evidence-based, culturally sensitive care that reduces disparities between high- and low-resource settings by leveraging local resources, task-sharing with non-professional workers and traditional healers, and incorporating digital solutions to extend care reach. The authors emphasize that meaningful progress requires stronger mental health funding, improved access to care, and attention to the social determinants of health across all settings.
items.citation: Paolo Fusar‐Poli, Toby Pillinger, Robert Ali McCutcheon et al.. Real‐world comprehensive care of people living with schizophrenia: recommendations across different settings and clinical stages. World Psychiatry. 2026

items.title: ECCO Guidelines on the Prevention, Diagnosis, and Management of Infections in Inflammatory Bowel Disease
items.summary: This paper presents updated clinical guidelines from the European Crohn's and Colitis Organisation on preventing, diagnosing, and managing infections in patients with inflammatory bowel disease. The guidelines were developed in response to the rapid expansion of immunosuppressive and biologic therapies, including newer small molecules and advanced biologics, which carry distinct infection risk profiles compared to older agents. The authors conducted a comprehensive review and synthesis of current evidence to provide structured, evidence-based recommendations covering risk stratification and viral, bacterial, mycobacterial, and vaccine-preventable infections. The update emphasizes a preventative strategy tailored to the contemporary treatment landscape, recognizing that potent immune modulation increasingly places patients at risk for opportunistic infections that can cause significant morbidity or mortality. These guidelines represent a revision of prior consensus statements and are intended to equip clinicians with practical guidance aligned with evolving therapeutic paradigms in inflammatory bowel disease management.
items.venue: Journal of Crohn s and Colitis
items.citation: Henit A. Yanai, Pierre Ellul, Bram Verstockt et al.. ECCO Guidelines on the Prevention, Diagnosis, and Management of Infections in Inflammatory Bowel Disease. Journal of Crohn s and Colitis. 2026

items.title: Clinical profile and genomic characterization of the 2026 Bundibugyo virus index case in Uganda
items.summary: This case report describes Uganda's index case of Bundibugyo virus disease detected in 2026, involving a male patient who had traveled from the Democratic Republic of the Congo and presented with prolonged gastrointestinal symptoms before hospital admission in Kampala. The patient's condition deteriorated rapidly across multiple organ systems and he died within days of admission, with posthumous testing confirming orthoebolavirus RNA that was subsequently identified as Bundibugyo virus by quantitative reverse transcription PCR. Genomic sequencing achieved near-complete genome coverage and revealed that the 2026 strain forms a distinct lineage roughly equidistant from previously characterized variants from earlier outbreaks, with approximately one percent sequence divergence from those strains. The authors use this case to highlight the challenges posed by nonspecific early symptoms, cross-border movement, and delayed recognition in containing high-consequence pathogens. They argue the case demonstrates the importance of fatality surveillance, private-sector healthcare engagement, national specimen referral systems, and rapid molecular-genomic diagnostics for early detection and public health response.
items.citation: Andrew Nsawotebba, Isaac Ssewanyana, Alisen Ayitewala et al.. Clinical profile and genomic characterization of the 2026 Bundibugyo virus index case in Uganda. Nature Medicine. 2026

items.title: SEMAC: Spherical Energy Matching Ambisonics Codec for Efficient Higher-Order Ambisonics Compression
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of efficiently compressing Higher-Order Ambisonics (HOA) spatial audio, which conventionally requires bitrates that grow quadratically with spherical harmonic order. The authors introduce SEMAC, a codec that represents an HOA signal using a quantized directional energy envelope computed at full order alongside a reduced set of lower-order transport channels coded with the CELT algorithm. The decoder then uses the preserved directional energy envelope to restore the full spatial energy distribution from the lower-dimensional transport signal, generalizing the per-band energy separation principle already used in CELT to the directional domain. Perceptual evaluation using MUSHRA listening tests on fifth-order material showed that SEMAC using roughly half the transport channels of a full-order representation was rated above the standard Opus Channel Mapping Family approach at matched bitrates. The results indicate that transmitting fewer transport channels at higher fidelity combined with directional envelope restoration is perceptually preferable to transmitting all HOA channels at reduced precision.
items.citation: Christoph Hold, Jan Buethe, Jean-Marc Valin et al.. SEMAC: Spherical Energy Matching Ambisonics Codec for Efficient Higher-Order Ambisonics Compression. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Comprehensive Visible and Near-infrared Keck and Gemini Monitoring and Characterization of Interstellar Comet 3I/ATLAS during its Encounter with the Solar System
items.summary: This paper presents an extensive observational campaign monitoring interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS across visible and near-infrared wavelengths using multiple instruments on the Keck and Gemini telescopes, spanning nearly a year bracketing the comet's perihelion passage. The study tracked the comet's photometric colors, coma morphology, dust activity, and molecular gas composition through spectroscopy and imaging. The comet's optical colors remained stable across perihelion, while dust activity declined more steeply after perihelion than before, and substantial dust mass loss was estimated over the observation period. Gas abundance ratios evolved with time, showing a near-doubling of the C₂-to-CN ratio after perihelion while the C₃-to-CN ratio declined, suggesting compositional or photochemical changes in the coma. Near-infrared spectroscopy revealed no robust evidence for water-ice absorption features, and the authors present these comprehensive observations as a lasting benchmark for understanding interstellar objects visiting the Solar System.
items.citation: Bryce T. Bolin, Jeffrey Cooke, Brian C. Lemaux et al.. Comprehensive Visible and Near-infrared Keck and Gemini Monitoring and Characterization of Interstellar Comet 3I/ATLAS during its Encounter with the Solar System. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Shared clones make random cell halves look reproducible in pooled screens
items.summary: This paper investigated a methodological flaw in how single-cell perturbation screens, such as Perturb-seq, assess the reproducibility of measured perturbation effects. The standard practice of splitting a perturbation's cells into two random halves assumes those halves are independent replicates, but because cells in pooled screens descend from a limited number of transduced ancestors, the two halves share the same clonal lineages—a form of pseudoreplication invisible in the data. By comparing random half-splits against genuinely independent replicates from separate transductions, and by splitting cells into halves that share no clonal ancestry, the authors demonstrated that clonal sharing artificially inflates agreement between halves. This inflation was largest in primary T cells and in vivo settings, and one to two orders of magnitude smaller in cell lines, with its magnitude determined by the proportion of expression variation attributable to clonal identity relative to the effective number of clones per perturbation. As a consequence, benchmarks that evaluate models predicting perturbation effects are systematically overoptimistic when training and scoring draw from the same transduction, and most published models were found to perform below a perturbation-agnostic baseline when evaluated against cells from an independent transduction, leading the authors to recommend that reproducibility always be assessed across separate transductions.
items.citation: Xuanrui Huang. Shared clones make random cell halves look reproducible in pooled screens. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A probabilistic approach to separate mergers and jellyfish galaxies: Application of morphological non-parametric indexes to the DESI Legacy Survey
items.summary: This paper investigates whether non-parametric morphological indices can reliably classify galaxies into regular spirals, regular ellipticals, mergers, and jellyfish galaxies — the latter being candidates for ram-pressure stripping — using imaging from the DESI Legacy Surveys. The authors measured ten non-parametric morphological indices and evaluated their discriminating power both in two-dimensional diagnostic planes using a cross-validated Bayesian kernel-density classifier and in combined multi-index models using calibrated gradient-boosted decision tree classifiers. They found that planes combining Shannon entropy with asymmetry or concentration-related indices performed best for separating broad morphological classes, and that the multi-index machine learning models substantially outperformed two-dimensional approaches, with the three-class model achieving notably higher accuracy than the four-class version. A key finding is that while non-parametric morphology reliably identifies structural disturbance in general, distinguishing its physical origin is more difficult: jellyfish candidates cluster in a relatively coherent region of morphological parameter space, whereas mergers exhibit diverse and overlapping morphologies. The study delivers probabilistic classifications for nearly two million galaxies, providing a large catalog for further investigation of environmentally and interaction-driven galaxy evolution.
items.citation: V. M. Sampaio, Y. Jaff'e, A. Moretti et al.. A probabilistic approach to separate mergers and jellyfish galaxies: Application of morphological non-parametric indexes to the DESI Legacy Survey. arXiv. 2026

items.title: CoupleFlow: Null-Calibrated Auditory Attention Decoding With Time-Locked Brain-Speech Coupling and Flow-Matching Likelihood Ratios
items.summary: This paper addresses auditory attention decoding, the problem of identifying which talker a listener is attending to based on brief noninvasive brain recordings, and reveals that recently reported near-perfect decoding accuracies are largely attributable to methodological artifacts such as trial leakage, eye gaze, and acoustic cues rather than genuine neural tracking of speech. The authors introduce CoupleFlow, a method that decodes attention by measuring temporal coupling between neural and acoustic embeddings using a conditional flow matching framework that implements a likelihood ratio decision rule based on pointwise mutual information, ensuring predictions fall to chance when no informative brain-speech coupling is present. The system is evaluated using content-disjoint data splits and null tests designed to distinguish genuine neural-speech coupling from spurious trial recognition across nine electroencephalography and magnetoencephalography datasets spanning multiple languages, recording modalities, listeners with hearing impairment, and multi-talker environments. CoupleFlow outperforms both linear and deep learning baselines while consistently passing null tests that confirm its reliance on true neural coupling rather than shortcuts. The authors additionally derive an evidence accumulation law that predicts decoding accuracy as a function of window length from a single per-dataset parameter, linking performance limits to the signal-to-noise ratio of neural speech tracking and enabling estimation of the recording duration required to reach a desired accuracy target.
items.citation: Ali Alavi, Donald S. Williamson. CoupleFlow: Null-Calibrated Auditory Attention Decoding With Time-Locked Brain-Speech Coupling and Flow-Matching Likelihood Ratios. arXiv. 2026

items.title: If at First You Don't Succeed, Backtrack: Lightweight Recovery for Frozen VLAs
items.summary: This paper addresses the brittleness of Vision-Language-Action models in robotic manipulation, specifically their tendency to fail when their own actions push them into states underrepresented in training data. The authors propose Backtrack, a lightweight mechanism that attaches a small failure prediction head to a frozen policy, trained solely on outcome-labeled rollouts, which reads the policy's internal representations to estimate the likelihood of episode failure in real time. When predicted failure probability crosses a threshold, the system pauses the policy and physically retraces the robot arm's recent motion, returning to an earlier configuration so the unchanged policy can retry. The approach requires no recovery demonstrations, no retraining, and no separate inference-time model, adding less than one percent to the policy's parameter count. Evaluated across multiple VLA architectures and task suites, Backtrack substantially reduces failure rates on long-horizon tasks while having modest effects on shorter tasks where baseline success rates are already high.
items.citation: Thomas Landeg, Thierry Tambe. If at First You Don't Succeed, Backtrack: Lightweight Recovery for Frozen VLAs. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Pulmonary Tuberculosis Detection with MiniDock MTB Using Swab Samples
items.summary: This prospective, cross-sectional study evaluated the diagnostic accuracy and usability of MiniDock MTB, a novel test for detecting pulmonary tuberculosis, across outpatient centers in seven countries spanning multiple continents. Patients aged twelve or older with presumptive pulmonary tuberculosis were tested using both sputum swabs and tongue swabs, with results benchmarked against sputum culture, smear microscopy, and the established Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra assay. MiniDock MTB demonstrated high sensitivity with sputum swabs and somewhat lower but still substantial sensitivity with tongue swabs, while specificity exceeded the threshold set by World Health Organization targets for both sample types. Performance with sputum closely paralleled that of Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra and markedly outperformed smear microscopy for both sample types. The test met WHO accuracy targets for near-point-of-care tuberculosis diagnostics, showed good usability scores, and raised no safety concerns, supporting its potential utility in peripheral health settings where improved diagnostic access is critically needed.
items.citation: Seda Yerlikaya, Masuzyo Chirwa, Bukola Ajide et al.. Pulmonary Tuberculosis Detection with MiniDock MTB Using Swab Samples. New England Journal of Medicine. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic performance and testing costs of pooled testing for molecular detection of tuberculosis in seven countries: a prospective, observational, diagnostic accuracy study.
items.summary: This study evaluated whether pooled sputum testing could maintain diagnostic accuracy for tuberculosis while reducing the number of costly cartridges required for molecular testing. Conducted across seven countries using a prospective observational design, the researchers combined sputum specimens from multiple individuals into pools of up to four samples and tested these on Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra, comparing results against both individual Xpert Ultra testing and microbiological culture as the reference standard. Pooled testing achieved slightly higher specificity than individual testing but showed modestly lower sensitivity, with the greatest loss of agreement occurring for specimens with very low or trace bacterial loads. Crucially, pooled testing reduced cartridge consumption by approximately half compared with individual testing. The authors conclude that this approach could meaningfully expand access to WHO-recommended rapid molecular diagnostics in low to moderate tuberculosis prevalence settings without requiring additional laboratory infrastructure.
items.citation: Garg T, Sander M, Byrne RL et al.. Diagnostic performance and testing costs of pooled testing for molecular detection of tuberculosis in seven countries: a prospective, observational, diagnostic accuracy study.. The Lancet. Global health. 2027

items.title: Advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarkers, 2020-26: scientific evidence, recommendations, gaps, and developmental priorities.
items.summary: This review synthesizes major advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarker research from 2020 to 2025, examining how new tools and evidence have shaped updated WHO policy guidance that consolidates recommendations for detecting tuberculosis disease and drug resistance into a single framework. Digital chest radiography supported by computer-aided detection has emerged as a core screening and triage tool, while decentralised molecular diagnosis has expanded through multiple classes of nucleic acid amplification tests, novel specimen types such as tongue swabs, and workflow innovations including sputum pooling. Rapid molecular drug-resistance testing has progressed alongside targeted next-generation sequencing for comprehensive drug-susceptibility profiling at reference laboratory level, and urine lipoarabinomannan assays offer improved diagnostic yield in people with HIV and advanced disease, though with performance limitations. Host blood transcriptomic signatures show promise for short-term prognosis and triage, and proteomic, metabolomic, and other biomarker classes are advancing through clinical evaluation. Nevertheless, significant performance, implementation, and equity gaps persist, and no biomarker has yet met WHO target product profile criteria for a point-of-care test capable of reliably distinguishing tuberculosis infection from disease, including subclinical presentations.
items.citation: Walzl G, McHugh TD, Chakaya J et al.. Advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarkers, 2020-26: scientific evidence, recommendations, gaps, and developmental priorities.. The Lancet. Microbe. 2027

items.title: The changing landscape of diagnosing HIV-associated tuberculosis.
items.summary: This narrative review examined the evolving landscape of diagnosing tuberculosis in people with HIV from 1990 to the present. The authors explored the clinical and diagnostic challenges posed by HIV-associated tuberculosis, including lower bacillary loads in sputum, high rates of extrapulmonary disease, and nonspecific clinical features that overlap with other opportunistic infections, requiring rapid diagnosis particularly in those with advanced HIV disease. The review traces the progression from smear microscopy—long the only rapid diagnostic tool but with reduced sensitivity in people with HIV—through to the development of nucleic acid amplification tests and urine lipoarabinomannan lateral flow assays, as well as the impact of antiretroviral therapy on both tuberculosis incidence and mortality. Despite these advances, no currently available rapid diagnostic test achieves ideal sensitivity, and only urine lipoarabinomannan detection combines affordability with point-of-care simplicity. The authors conclude that a continued need exists for novel, accurate, and affordable point-of-care diagnostics to further reduce the burden of HIV-associated tuberculosis.
items.venue: South African medical journal = Suid-Afrikaanse tydskrif vir geneeskunde
items.citation: Maartens G. The changing landscape of diagnosing HIV-associated tuberculosis.. South African medical journal = Suid-Afrikaanse tydskrif vir geneeskunde. 2026

items.title: Development and validation of a blood-based diagnostic model for pulmonary tuberculosis combining GBP5 expression and routine laboratory indicators.
items.summary: This study addressed the challenge of diagnosing pulmonary tuberculosis, where conventional laboratory methods suffer from poor sensitivity despite high specificity, leaving many patients undetected. The researchers developed a blood-based, non-sputum diagnostic model by conducting a retrospective case-control study comparing patients with active tuberculosis against those with other pulmonary diseases. Using univariate and multivariate logistic regression, they identified GBP5 gene expression, white blood cell count, platelet count, and prothrombin time as key predictors, which were then combined into a model using the AdaBoost machine learning algorithm. The resulting model outperformed traditional diagnostic methods—including smear microscopy, culture, Xpert MTB/RIF, and IGRA—achieving comparable discriminatory performance across both training and test sets. The authors conclude that this blood-based AdaBoost model shows promise as a rapid clinical diagnostic tool for active tuberculosis, though validation in larger patient cohorts is required before clinical implementation.
items.citation: Zhao M, Hu Q, Wang Q et al.. Development and validation of a blood-based diagnostic model for pulmonary tuberculosis combining GBP5 expression and routine laboratory indicators.. Medicine. 2026

items.title: Clinical Utility of Cartridge-Based Nucleic Acid Amplification Test for Tuberculosis and Rifampicin Resistance Detection in the Vindhya Region of India: A Retrospective Study.
items.summary: This retrospective study evaluated the clinical utility of cartridge-based nucleic acid amplification testing (CBNAAT) for diagnosing tuberculosis and detecting rifampicin resistance at a tertiary care center in the Vindhya region of Central India. Researchers analyzed records from over two thousand patients with clinically suspected tuberculosis who underwent CBNAAT testing, with rifampicin-resistant specimens subsequently confirmed by line probe assay. CBNAAT detected Mycobacterium tuberculosis in roughly one in five patients overall, with pulmonary specimens yielding substantially higher detection rates than extrapulmonary specimens. Male sex, rural residence, diabetes mellitus, HIV infection, pulmonary specimen type, and a history of previous antituberculosis treatment were independently associated with test positivity, while a meaningful proportion of confirmed cases demonstrated rifampicin resistance, including multidrug-resistant tuberculosis identified on line probe assay. The authors conclude that CBNAAT is a valuable rapid diagnostic tool in this setting and recommend expanding molecular diagnostic services and prioritizing them as the primary screening method across all levels of care to support national tuberculosis elimination goals.
items.citation: Agrawal RP, Sinha A, Chaubey P et al.. Clinical Utility of Cartridge-Based Nucleic Acid Amplification Test for Tuberculosis and Rifampicin Resistance Detection in the Vindhya Region of India: A Retrospective Study.. Cureus. 2026

items.title: Efficient differential expression analysis of large-scale single-cell transcriptomics data using Dreamlet
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of performing differential expression analysis on large-scale single-cell and single-nucleus transcriptomics datasets spanning hundreds of subjects and millions of cells. The authors developed an open-source R package called dreamlet, which employs a pseudobulk approach based on precision-weighted linear mixed models to identify genes differentially expressed with traits of interest across subjects within individual cell clusters. The method is specifically designed to handle complex statistical models while controlling the false positive rate, and it achieves substantially faster runtimes and lower memory usage compared to existing workflows. Performance was validated on published datasets as well as a novel large-scale dataset of over a million single nuclei derived from postmortem brain tissue of Alzheimer's disease cases and controls.
items.citation: Gabriel E. Hoffman, Donghoon Lee, Jaroslav M. Bendl et al.. Efficient differential expression analysis of large-scale single-cell transcriptomics data using Dreamlet. Nature Communications. 2026

items.title: A systematic literature review on the effects of exercise on human Toll-like receptor expression
items.summary: This systematic review examined how different forms of exercise influence the expression of Toll-like receptors, a family of immune pattern recognition receptors implicated in inflammatory signalling and linked to chronic low-grade inflammation associated with sedentary behaviour and non-communicable diseases. The authors searched multiple databases and included studies in which exercise was the sole intervention in human participants, categorising findings by exercise modality and duration into acute versus chronic, and resistance versus aerobic versus combined protocols. Acute resistance exercise tended to upregulate TLR expression, while acute aerobic exercise more often produced neutral or downregulatory responses, particularly in healthy individuals. Chronic resistance and combined training programs predominantly left TLR levels unchanged or reduced them, whereas chronic aerobic training yielded mixed results with most measurements showing no significant change. The authors conclude that an exercise–TLR interaction exists and appears to depend on exercise characteristics, but caution that substantial heterogeneity across study designs limits firm conclusions and that further research is needed to clarify the mechanisms and pathophysiological relevance.
items.citation: Kasper Favere, Matthias Bosman, Peter Delputte et al.. A systematic literature review on the effects of exercise on human Toll-like receptor expression. PubMed. 2026

items.title: SEMAC: Spherical Energy Matching Ambisonics Codec for Efficient Higher-Order Ambisonics Compression
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of efficiently compressing Higher-Order Ambisonics (HOA) spatial audio, which becomes increasingly costly to transmit as the number of audio channels grows quadratically with spherical harmonic order. The authors introduce SEMAC, a codec that represents an HOA signal using a quantized directional energy envelope captured at full order combined with a reduced set of lower-order transport channels coded with the existing CELT framework, rather than transmitting every HOA channel individually. The decoder then uses the stored directional energy envelope to restore the full spatial energy distribution, compensating for the dimensionality reduction introduced by using fewer transport channels. Perceptual evaluation using a standard MUSHRA listening test on fifth-order HOA material showed that SEMAC using roughly half the full number of transport channels was rated above full-order Opus coding at matched bitrates, and outperformed simple order truncation when using the same number of transport channels. The results indicate that coding fewer channels at higher precision while preserving directional energy through an envelope is perceptually preferable to coding all HOA channels at lower precision.
items.citation: Christoph Hold, Jan Buethe, Jean-Marc Valin et al.. SEMAC: Spherical Energy Matching Ambisonics Codec for Efficient Higher-Order Ambisonics Compression. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Comprehensive Visible and Near-infrared Keck and Gemini Monitoring and Characterization of Interstellar Comet 3I/ATLAS during its Encounter with the Solar System
items.summary: This paper presents an extensive observational campaign characterizing the interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS across optical and near-infrared wavelengths using multiple large ground-based telescopes over roughly ten months spanning its perihelion passage. The study monitored the comet's color evolution, dust activity, coma morphology, and gas emission ratios through both imaging and spectroscopy. The comet's optical colors remained stable across perihelion, while dust activity declined more steeply after perihelion than before, and the coma structure transitioned from a concentrated, directionally structured morphology to a more extended dust distribution over time. Molecular abundance ratios of cometary gases changed notably around perihelion, with carbon-chain species showing distinct temporal trends, and near-infrared observations revealed no robust detection of water-ice absorption features. The authors present these observations as a benchmark dataset for understanding interstellar object composition and activity, and for comparison with future interstellar visitors to the Solar System.
items.citation: Bryce T. Bolin, Jeffrey Cooke, Brian C. Lemaux et al.. Comprehensive Visible and Near-infrared Keck and Gemini Monitoring and Characterization of Interstellar Comet 3I/ATLAS during its Encounter with the Solar System. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Shared clones make random cell halves look reproducible in pooled screens
items.summary: This paper examined a methodological flaw in how single-cell perturbation screens, such as Perturb-seq, are evaluated for reproducibility. The standard approach splits each perturbation's cells into two random halves and treats them as independent replicates, but because cells in pooled screens descend from a limited number of transduced progenitors, both halves contain the same clonal lineages, constituting pseudoreplication. Using null perturbations as controls and clone-aware splitting strategies, the researchers demonstrated that random halves show artificially inflated agreement compared to truly independent replicates from separate transductions, with the effect being most severe in primary T cells and cells transferred into mice, and much smaller in cell lines and non-dividing neurons. The degree of inflation depends on the proportion of expression variation attributable to clonal identity divided by the effective number of clones per perturbation. As a consequence, published models that predict perturbation effects appear to outperform a perturbation-ignorant baseline when evaluated within a single transduction, but most fall below that baseline when evaluated against cells from a separate transduction, leading the authors to conclude that reproducibility assessments and model benchmarks must be conducted across independent transductions.
items.citation: Xuanrui Huang. Shared clones make random cell halves look reproducible in pooled screens. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A probabilistic approach to separate mergers and jellyfish galaxies: Application of morphological non-parametric indexes to the DESI Legacy Survey
items.summary: This study investigates how non-parametric morphological indices can classify galaxies into regular spirals, regular ellipticals, mergers, and jellyfish galaxies (ram-pressure stripping candidates) using imaging from the DESI Legacy Surveys. The researchers measured ten non-parametric indices and evaluated their discriminatory power through two-dimensional diagnostic planes using a Bayesian kernel-density classifier, then combined all indices with calibrated gradient-boosted machine learning models. They found that planes combining Shannon entropy with either the moment of light or asymmetry indices are most effective for separating regular from disturbed galaxies, while distinguishing mergers from jellyfish candidates is more difficult, with concentration-based planes performing best among two-dimensional combinations. The multi-class machine learning model substantially outperforms two-dimensional diagnostics, and the study delivers probabilistic classifications for nearly two million galaxies. A key conclusion is that while non-parametric morphology reliably identifies structural disturbance, determining its physical origin is challenging because jellyfish galaxies occupy a coherent region of parameter space whereas mergers display diverse and overlapping morphologies.
items.citation: V. M. Sampaio, Y. Jaff'e, A. Moretti et al.. A probabilistic approach to separate mergers and jellyfish galaxies: Application of morphological non-parametric indexes to the DESI Legacy Survey. arXiv. 2026

items.title: CoupleFlow: Null-Calibrated Auditory Attention Decoding With Time-Locked Brain-Speech Coupling and Flow-Matching Likelihood Ratios
items.summary: This paper investigates auditory attention decoding, which aims to identify which talker a listener is attending to based on brief noninvasive brain recordings. The authors first demonstrate that existing high-performing EEG decoders exploit methodological artifacts such as trial leakage, eye gaze, and acoustic cues rather than genuine neural responses to speech, causing their accuracy to fail to generalize to unseen speech. To address this, they developed CoupleFlow, a method that decodes attention through temporal coupling between neural and acoustic embeddings using a conditional flow matching head that implements a likelihood ratio decision rule based on pointwise mutual information, ensuring predictions fall to chance when no informative brain-speech coupling is present. Evaluated across nine EEG and MEG datasets spanning multiple languages, listener populations, and recording conditions, CoupleFlow outperforms linear and deep learning baselines while consistently passing null tests that detect spurious decoding. The authors additionally derive an evidence accumulation law that predicts decoding accuracy as a function of window length from a single dataset-specific parameter, identifying recording signal-to-noise ratio as the fundamental bottleneck limiting decoding speed and reliability.
items.citation: Ali Alavi, Donald S. Williamson. CoupleFlow: Null-Calibrated Auditory Attention Decoding With Time-Locked Brain-Speech Coupling and Flow-Matching Likelihood Ratios. arXiv. 2026

items.title: If at First You Don't Succeed, Backtrack: Lightweight Recovery for Frozen VLAs
items.summary: This paper addresses the brittleness of Vision-Language-Action models in robotic manipulation, specifically their tendency to fail when their own actions push them into states underrepresented in training data. The authors propose Backtrack, a lightweight mechanism that attaches a small failure prediction head to a frozen policy, training it only on outcome-labeled rollouts to detect impending failures using the policy's existing internal representations. When the predicted failure probability crosses a threshold, the system pauses the policy, physically retraces the robot arm's recent motion, and re-engages the unchanged policy from an earlier configuration, requiring no recovery demonstrations, retraining, or additional models at inference time. Evaluated across multiple VLA architectures representing different action-generation paradigms and tested on both LIBERO and MetaWorld benchmarks, Backtrack consistently reduces failure rates, with the largest gains observed on long-horizon multi-step tasks where base policies fail most frequently. The failure prediction head is extremely parameter-efficient, adding less than one percent to the policy's parameter count while delivering meaningful improvements in task success rates.
items.citation: Thomas Landeg, Thierry Tambe. If at First You Don't Succeed, Backtrack: Lightweight Recovery for Frozen VLAs. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A case for eliminating Widal testing for enteric fever, India.
items.venue: Bulletin of the World Health Organization

items.title: Current Data to Inform Point-of-Care Testing for Sexually Transmitted Infections in United States Healthcare Settings: A Narrative Review.
items.summary: This narrative review examined the current evidence base for point-of-care testing for sexually transmitted infections across United States healthcare settings, including emergency departments, sexual health clinics, primary care, gynecology clinics, and urgent care centers. The authors reviewed literature on the clinical impact of point-of-care tests for gonorrhea, chlamydia, trichomoniasis, and syphilis, incorporating studies from other high-income countries where domestic data were limited, and stratified findings by clinical setting, sex, and priority patient groups such as symptomatic individuals and STI contacts. Some evidence supported improved clinical outcomes, particularly for symptomatic women presenting to emergency departments, but most studies did not stratify results by priority population and predominantly evaluated slower tests that returned results only after the patient visit had ended. The review concludes that substantial evidence gaps remain, especially regarding rapid tests capable of returning actionable results within the clinical encounter, workflow integration strategies, and cost-effectiveness analyses specific to the United States context. The authors call for additional research targeting priority populations and settings to better inform reimbursement decisions and guide appropriate, targeted adoption of point-of-care STI testing.
items.citation: Otsyina BE, Lorenz ZW, Widdice LE et al.. Current Data to Inform Point-of-Care Testing for Sexually Transmitted Infections in United States Healthcare Settings: A Narrative Review.. Sexually transmitted diseases. 2026

items.title: Interventions to Improve Care for Bacterial Sexually Transmitted Infections in Emergency Departments: A Narrative Review.
items.summary: This narrative review examined interventions designed to improve the diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up of bacterial sexually transmitted infections — specifically chlamydia, gonorrhea, and syphilis — within emergency department settings in the United States. The authors searched published literature spanning several decades and identified studies evaluating a range of approaches including universal screening protocols, electronic health record prompts, point-of-care testing, patient-directed tools, and bundled multi-step interventions. Universal screening strategies led to substantial increases in testing and case detection, electronic prompts enhanced screening uptake, and point-of-care testing improved same-visit diagnosis and treatment while reducing unnecessary antibiotic use. Bundled interventions that addressed multiple stages of the care pathway appeared to produce the greatest overall impact, though variability across interventions made direct comparisons difficult. The authors conclude that future research should prioritize implementation feasibility, sustainability, health equity, and cost-effectiveness across diverse emergency department contexts.
items.citation: Andonian KS, Giri H, Goodman GR et al.. Interventions to Improve Care for Bacterial Sexually Transmitted Infections in Emergency Departments: A Narrative Review.. Sexually transmitted diseases. 2026

items.title: Community peer-led STI/HIV point-of-care testing and knowledge, attitude and practice (KAP) survey in men who have sex with men (MSM) attending an NGO-led clinic in the outskirts of Beirut (Lebanon).
items.summary: This pilot study examined the utility of point-of-care testing for HIV, syphilis, and hepatitis among men who have sex with men attending an NGO-led clinic in Beirut, Lebanon, while also assessing their knowledge, attitudes, and practices related to sexual health. Using a cross-sectional design over several months, researchers conducted sexual health consultations, administered STI and HIV tests, and had participants complete an anonymous questionnaire covering demographics, condom use, chemsex, sexual violence, and perceived HIV-related stigma. The cohort was predominantly young, educated Lebanese and Syrian men, among whom a notable proportion were living with HIV, and high levels of STI and HIV awareness coexisted with condomless sex and recreational drug use. Perceived community stigma emerged as a significant barrier to testing-seeking behaviour, and HIV-related stigma was linked to engagement in riskier sexual practices. The authors conclude that integrating point-of-care testing into sexual health services enables same-day counselling and rapid linkage to confirmatory testing and care, making it a valuable tool for this population.
items.citation: Abou Shahla W, Rossoni I, Padovese V. Community peer-led STI/HIV point-of-care testing and knowledge, attitude and practice (KAP) survey in men who have sex with men (MSM) attending an NGO-led clinic in the outskirts of Beirut (Lebanon).. Sexually transmitted infections. 2026

items.title: Mean-Field Limit of Non-exchangeable Multi-agent Systems Over Hypergraphs with Unbounded Rank
items.summary: This paper studies multi-agent interacting particle systems that involve higher-order interactions, meaning individuals can interact simultaneously in groups rather than only in pairs, with the underlying network structure represented by a hypergraph of potentially nonuniform and unbounded rank. The authors develop a mathematical framework combining partial differential equations, stochastic analysis, kinetic theory, and graph theory to derive the mean-field limit of such systems as the population becomes large. A key innovation is the introduction of the unbounded-rank hypergraphon as the appropriate limiting object encoding the structure of dense, nonuniform hypergraphs in this setting. The main result establishes, for the first time, that when interaction kernels are sufficiently regular, the large-population limit is governed by a Vlasov-type equation in which the mean-field force incorporates infinitely many orders of interaction. This extends classical mean-field theory beyond binary interactions and pairwise graph-based models to a substantially more general class of collective dynamics.
items.citation: Nathalie Ayi, Nastassia Pouradier Duteil, David Poyato. Mean-Field Limit of Non-exchangeable Multi-agent Systems Over Hypergraphs with Unbounded Rank. Journal of Nonlinear Science. 2026

items.title: Flatline constructs : Gothic materialism and cybernetic theory-fiction
items.summary: This thesis examines the claim that cyberpunk fiction is the supreme literary expression of postmodernism or late capitalism, arguing instead that a more productive framework lies in the intersection of cybernetics, the Gothic, and fiction. Drawing on Deleuze-Guattari's materialist reworking of the Gothic through Wilhelm Worringer's concept of nonorganic continuum, the study moves away from supernatural conventions to analyse cyberpunk as centrally concerned with the collapse of the boundary between animate and inanimate. Key texts including Blade Runner, Videodrome, Neuromancer, and The Atrocity Exhibition are read through this lens, with the analysis structured around the concept of the "flatline," understood as both a state of unlife or undeath and a condition of radical immanence. The thesis further engages Baudrillard's theory of cybernetic simulation to argue that in an era of third-order simulacra, the conventional boundaries between theory and fiction, and between science fiction and reality, themselves collapse. Through four thematic chapters addressing the flatlining of cybernetics, the body, reproduction, and fiction, the work proposes that cyberpunk converges Gothic and cybernetic thought in ways that resist reduction to postmodernist cultural categories.
items.venue: Warwick Research Archive Portal (University of Warwick)
items.citation: Mark Fisher. Flatline constructs : Gothic materialism and cybernetic theory-fiction. Warwick Research Archive Portal (University of Warwick). 2026

items.title: The many behind the few : the lives and emotions of Erks and WAAFs of RAF bomber command 1939-1945
items.summary: This thesis investigates the largely overlooked experiences of ground personnel — both men and women — who served in Royal Air Force Bomber Command during the Second World War, a group that constituted the vast majority of the command yet has received little scholarly attention compared to aircrew. The research examines how a gendered and classed hierarchy of occupational trades structured the lives, identities, and emotional experiences of these personnel, shaped by RAF culture, beliefs about heroism and stoicism, pay, and perceived contribution to the bombing mission. The study also explores how ground personnel navigated the psychological strain of witnessing high aircrew loss rates while serving in a home front context, and how the RAF medical services responded to those who suffered mental breakdowns. By recovering the voices of this underrepresented group, the thesis makes contributions to histories of the RAF, military medicine and psychiatry, the study of emotions, and broader understandings of wartime work, gender, and citizenship.
items.venue: Warwick Research Archive Portal (University of Warwick)
items.citation: Dan Ellin. The many behind the few : the lives and emotions of Erks and WAAFs of RAF bomber command 1939-1945. Warwick Research Archive Portal (University of Warwick). 2026

items.title: APASL clinical practice guidelines on the management of chronic hepatitis B infection: a 2026 update
items.summary: These clinical practice guidelines address the ongoing burden of chronic hepatitis B infection in the Asia Pacific region, where the disease continues to drive significant morbidity and mortality through complications including acute-on-chronic liver failure, end-stage cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma. The guidelines were developed by a dedicated Viral Elimination Taskforce comprising key opinion leaders from member countries and regions under the auspices of APASL, incorporating shifts in hepatitis B epidemiology, socioeconomic changes, and technological advances. The resulting recommendations span thirteen major areas encompassing screening, vaccination, antiviral treatment, and hepatocellular carcinoma surveillance, with an emphasis on practical and cost-effective decision-making for healthcare professionals, policy-makers, and patients. The overarching goal of the guidelines is to facilitate elimination of the disease burden attributable to chronic hepatitis B infection across the Asia Pacific region.
items.citation: Hong You, Rakhi Maiwall, Jing Chen et al.. APASL clinical practice guidelines on the management of chronic hepatitis B infection: a 2026 update. Hepatology International. 2026

items.title: Girls, gifts, and gender : an ethnography of the materiality of care in rural Mpumalanga, South Africa
items.summary: This ethnographic thesis examined social relations of care involving young people in rural South Africa amid the AIDS epidemic and rising economic inequality, focusing on how care operates as a form of gift exchange. Drawing on extensive fieldwork with non-profit organisations serving orphans and vulnerable children, as well as participant households, the research analysed three care relations: children's labour exchanged for guardian care, girls' labour and sexual exchange for material support from men, and the local construction of orphan identities to attract charitable giving from tourist-philanthropists. The study developed the concept of the "materiality of care" to theorise how Western and local understandings of childhood, orphanhood, and care intersect through orphan-targeted aid programmes. The research argues that care for young people affected by AIDS and poverty must be understood within local cultural practices and the broader historical and political-economic context rather than through externally imposed frameworks. Its findings contribute to critical scholarship on orphan-targeted interventions in sub-Saharan Africa, arguing that such programmes fail to account for the familial contexts of parentless children and the shared hardships experienced by both orphaned and non-orphaned young people.
items.venue: Warwick Research Archive Portal (University of Warwick)
items.citation: Annalise Weckesser. Girls, gifts, and gender : an ethnography of the materiality of care in rural Mpumalanga, South Africa. Warwick Research Archive Portal (University of Warwick). 2026

items.title: Hydrogels: current biomedical applications and future directions
items.summary: This review paper examines hydrogels as versatile biomedical materials, focusing on their design principles and expanding therapeutic applications. The authors systematically survey the structural construction and functional regulation strategies underlying hydrogel development, including advances in polymer chemistry, crosslinking methods, stimuli-responsive design, and fabrication technologies. The review comprehensively covers current biomedical uses spanning drug delivery, tissue engineering, biosensing, diagnostics, and organoid systems. Particular emphasis is placed on hydrogel-based therapeutic progress across a wide range of diseases, including wound healing, musculoskeletal repair, cancer, neurological and cardiovascular conditions, autoimmune disorders, and reproductive system diseases. The authors conclude by discussing the clinical translation prospects of hydrogels, positioning them as multifunctional systems capable of overcoming key limitations of conventional therapies such as poor targeting, systemic side effects, and inadequate tissue restoration.
items.citation: Haoming Wu, Guanghao Piao, Qiuqi Chen et al.. Hydrogels: current biomedical applications and future directions. Molecular Biomedicine. 2026

items.title: SEMAC: Spherical Energy Matching Ambisonics Codec for Efficient Higher-Order Ambisonics Compression
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of efficiently compressing Higher-Order Ambisonics audio, a spatial audio format whose channel count grows quadratically with spherical harmonic order, making it costly to transmit at high fidelity. The authors introduce SEMAC, a codec that represents an Ambisonics signal using a quantized directional energy envelope captured at full spherical harmonic order combined with a reduced set of transport channels coded at higher precision. By generalizing the per-band energy envelope separation principle from the CELT codec to the directional domain, SEMAC allows the decoder to reconstruct the full-order directional energy distribution even though fewer transport channels span only a lower-dimensional subspace. Perceptual listening tests using the MUSHRA methodology on fifth-order material showed that SEMAC using roughly half the transport channels of a full-order representation was rated above the standard Opus Channel Mapping Family approach at matched bitrates, and also outperformed simple order truncation when transport channel counts were equalized. The key finding is that coding fewer channels with accurate directional energy restoration is perceptually superior to coding all Higher-Order Ambisonics channels at reduced precision.
items.citation: Christoph Hold, Jan Buethe, Jean-Marc Valin et al.. SEMAC: Spherical Energy Matching Ambisonics Codec for Efficient Higher-Order Ambisonics Compression. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Comprehensive Visible and Near-infrared Keck and Gemini Monitoring and Characterization of Interstellar Comet 3I/ATLAS during its Encounter with the Solar System
items.summary: This paper presents an extensive observational campaign monitoring interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS across visible and near-infrared wavelengths using multiple large ground-based telescopes, spanning nearly a year encompassing its perihelion passage. The study tracked the comet's photometric colors, dust activity, coma morphology, and gas emission ratios through imaging and spectroscopy at numerous epochs. The dust activity showed an asymmetric response around perihelion, declining more steeply outbound than inbound, and the coma structure evolved from a compact, concentrated feature with a sunward plume to a more extended morphology over the months following closest approach. Gas emission ratios between carbon-bearing species changed significantly across the observation window, suggesting compositional or sublimation-driven evolution, while near-infrared spectroscopy revealed no robust detection of water-ice absorption. The authors conclude that these observations constitute a detailed record of how this interstellar visitor evolved during its solar encounter and provide a reference dataset for characterizing future interstellar objects.
items.citation: Bryce T. Bolin, Jeffrey Cooke, Brian C. Lemaux et al.. Comprehensive Visible and Near-infrared Keck and Gemini Monitoring and Characterization of Interstellar Comet 3I/ATLAS during its Encounter with the Solar System. arXiv. 2026

items.summary: This paper addresses auditory attention decoding, the task of identifying which talker a listener is attending to based on brief noninvasive brain recordings, and identifies a critical methodological flaw in prior work: high reported accuracies stem from models exploiting trial leakage, eye gaze, and acoustic cues rather than genuine neural responses to speech. They evaluate the approach using content-disjoint data splits and null tests specifically designed to distinguish true temporal coupling from spurious trial recognition, applying this framework across a large and diverse collection of electroencephalography and magnetoencephalography datasets spanning multiple languages, listener populations including those with hearing impairment, and multi-talker room conditions. CoupleFlow consistently outperforms linear and deep learning baselines while passing all null tests, demonstrating genuine reliance on neural speech tracking rather than shortcuts. Additionally, the authors derive an evidence accumulation law that predicts decoding accuracy across different time window lengths from a single dataset-specific parameter tied to neural speech tracking strength, framing recording signal-to-noise ratio as the fundamental bottleneck on decoding speed and reliability.

items.title: If at First You Don't Succeed, Backtrack: Lightweight Recovery for Frozen VLAs
items.summary: This paper addresses the brittleness of Vision-Language-Action models in robotic manipulation, specifically their tendency to fail when their own actions push them into states underrepresented in training data. The authors developed Backtrack, a lightweight mechanism that attaches a small failure prediction head to a frozen policy, training it only on outcome-labeled rollouts to estimate failure probability using the policy's existing internal representations. When predicted failure probability crosses a threshold, the system pauses the policy and physically retraces the robot arm's recent motion, returning to an earlier configuration from which the unmodified policy retries the task. The failure prediction head adds only a negligible fraction of parameters to the base policy, requiring no recovery demonstrations, retraining, or separate inference-time models. Evaluated across multiple VLA architectures and benchmark suites, Backtrack substantially reduced failure rates on long-horizon tasks where policies struggled most, while showing smaller but consistent improvements on shorter tasks where baseline performance was already high.

items.title: Certain Quantum States Already Require Quantum Time Evolution
items.summary: This paper investigates whether the dynamical aspects of quantum theory can be tested in a model-independent way, analogous to how Bell inequality violations test static properties. Working within a class of generalized phase-space theories, the authors examine the consistency between quantum state spaces and dynamical laws. They find that certain quantum states are inherently incompatible with non-quantum time evolution, because evolving them under anharmonic potentials using alternative dynamical rules would produce unphysical negative marginal distributions. Remarkably, the existence of the first excited state of the harmonic oscillator alone is shown to be sufficient to single out the Moyal bracket—the quantum mechanical equation of motion—to leading order in the relevant expansion parameter. The authors propose that theory-independent Wigner tomography of this state could serve as an empirical test to exclude non-quantum dynamical theories.
items.citation: Joel D. Huber, Matthias Kleinmann. Certain Quantum States Already Require Quantum Time Evolution. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Clinical utility of nucleic acid amplification testing for detection of sexually transmitted infections in women with symptomatic bacterial vaginosis and vulvovaginal candidiasis identified by conventional versus molecular diagnoses.
items.summary: This study examined whether molecular diagnostic methods improve the detection of sexually transmitted infections in women presenting with symptomatic vaginitis, specifically bacterial vaginosis and vulvovaginal candidiasis. The researchers compared STI nucleic acid amplification test results across women whose vaginitis was diagnosed by three different approaches: clinician clinical assessment, conventional laboratory methods, and molecular vaginitis testing. They found that women who tested positive for bacterial vaginosis by molecular methods had significantly higher rates of co-occurring STIs compared to those diagnosed by conventional laboratory or clinician methods, and a positive molecular bacterial vaginosis result was associated with nearly double the relative risk of any STI. The pattern was similar, though not statistically significant, for vulvovaginal candidiasis. The authors conclude that an all-molecular testing strategy combining vaginitis and STI diagnostics on a single specimen provides superior case-finding and risk stratification compared to conventional or clinician-based diagnostic approaches.
items.citation: Getman D, Seña AC, Nenninger A et al.. Clinical utility of nucleic acid amplification testing for detection of sexually transmitted infections in women with symptomatic bacterial vaginosis and vulvovaginal candidiasis identified by conventional versus molecular diagnoses.. Journal of clinical microbiology. 2026

items.title: Pre-exposure prophylaxis adherence and risks of HIV and sexually transmitted infection among adult men before vs during the COVID-19 pandemic.
items.summary: This study examined how the COVID-19 pandemic affected PrEP adherence patterns, HIV incidence, and sexually transmitted infection rates among adult men newly starting PrEP. Using a large commercially insured administrative claims database, researchers applied group-based trajectory modeling to characterize adherence patterns and used weighted Cox and Poisson regression models to compare HIV and STI outcomes between those who initiated PrEP before versus during the pandemic. Men who began PrEP during the pandemic showed worse adherence trajectories, with a substantially higher proportion falling into an early discontinuation category compared to those who initiated before the pandemic. Initiating PrEP during the pandemic was associated with more than double the risk of HIV acquisition, while STI rates were similar between the two groups. The findings highlight the need for targeted strategies to sustain HIV prevention services and PrEP continuity during public health emergencies.
items.venue: Journal of managed care & specialty pharmacy
items.citation: Unigwe IF, Jenjai C, Goodin AJ et al.. Pre-exposure prophylaxis adherence and risks of HIV and sexually transmitted infection among adult men before vs during the COVID-19 pandemic.. Journal of managed care & specialty pharmacy. 2026
