items.title: Next-generation CRISPR-based molecular diagnostics for veterinary parasitology: From laboratory innovation to one health surveillance.
items.summary: This review examines the application of CRISPR-based diagnostic technologies to the detection of veterinary parasites, encompassing protozoan, helminthic, and arthropod-borne organisms affecting livestock, companion animals, and wildlife. The authors critically synthesize the principles underlying CRISPR/Cas12, Cas13, and emerging Cas14 detection systems, as well as their integration with complementary technologies such as isothermal amplification, lateral flow assays, fluorescence detection, and portable biosensors. Compared with conventional approaches relying on microscopy, serology, and culture, CRISPR-based platforms offer substantially greater sensitivity, specificity, and suitability for field deployment. The review also identifies persistent challenges including sample preparation complexity, assay standardization, multiplex detection capability, and the regulatory and commercial hurdles that must be overcome before widespread adoption. Looking forward, the authors discuss the promise of amplification-free CRISPR assays and artificial intelligence-assisted interpretation as means of further advancing point-of-care parasite surveillance within a One Health framework.
items.citation: Basit A, Hanif M. Next-generation CRISPR-based molecular diagnostics for veterinary parasitology: From laboratory innovation to one health surveillance.. Molecular and biochemical parasitology. 2026

items.title: Scaffold RNA Reengineering for a Leakage-Suppressed CRISPR/Cas12a Cascade System Toward Precise Nucleic Acid Diagnostics.
items.summary: This paper addresses a major limitation of amplification-free CRISPR-based nucleic acid diagnostics: high background signal that compromises detection accuracy. The researchers engineered the CRISPR/Cas12a guide RNA by introducing a three-prime DNA extension to the scaffold RNA, creating a conformational switch that imposes steric hindrance as an activation barrier, effectively converting the system into a threshold-controlled molecular switch. This redesigned system, called CALCas, uses DNA-mediated allosteric regulation to keep Cas12a in an inhibited state until a target nucleic acid is present, at which point precise activation occurs without the self-activation leakage that typically plagues cascaded CRISPR approaches. The platform achieves femtomolar sensitivity far exceeding that of a single Cas12a system, enables detection of HPV16 and HPV18, and completes assays in under thirty minutes. The authors propose that this crRNA engineering strategy offers a broadly applicable route to reprogram Cas12a enzymatic activity for precise quantitative nucleic acid diagnostics.
items.citation: Li X, Hu H, Jiang X et al.. Scaffold RNA Reengineering for a Leakage-Suppressed CRISPR/Cas12a Cascade System Toward Precise Nucleic Acid Diagnostics.. Advanced science (Weinheim, Baden-Wurttemberg, Germany). 2026

items.title: Molecular Diagnostics of Infectious Diseases.
items.summary: This review paper examines the current landscape of molecular diagnostic technologies used to detect and characterize pathogens responsible for infectious diseases. The paper surveys nucleic acid amplification approaches, including various polymerase chain reaction formats optimized for speed, quantification, automation, and point-of-care deployment, as well as isothermal amplification methods that operate without thermal cycling equipment and are therefore well suited to resource-limited settings. It also covers CRISPR-based detection systems, which are frequently paired with isothermal amplification to identify amplified nucleic acids at constant temperature. Next-generation sequencing is highlighted for its capacity to identify novel pathogens, diagnose complex infections, trace outbreak transmission routes, monitor pathogen evolution, and analyze microbiomes as potential disease biomarkers. The authors conclude that the future of molecular infectious disease diagnostics lies in overcoming current limitations and integrating these diverse technologies into hybrid platforms.
items.citation: Takata M, Chikumi H, Yoshifuji A. Molecular Diagnostics of Infectious Diseases.. Yonago acta medica. 2026

items.title: Synergistic Multicomponent Nucleopeptide-Based Hydrogels: Harnessing DNA-Base Pairing and Electrostatic Complementarities
items.summary: This paper investigated how combining electrostatic and nucleobase-pairing interactions within peptide-based hydrogels can be used to control and fine-tune their physicochemical and mechanical properties. The researchers designed a series of nucleopeptides derived from two complementary tetrapeptide sequences — one negatively charged and one positively charged at physiological pH — each functionalized with one of the four DNA nucleobases introduced via a peptide nucleic acid moiety. Using a systematic multiscale approach, they examined how charge complementarity and nucleobase-pair complementarity, individually and together, influence hydrogel properties including gelation time, stiffness, sol-gel transition temperature, stress resistance, and fibrillar network morphology. The study found that careful selection of complementary components allows meaningful tuning of hydrogel behavior, though the results also revealed unexpected and complex emergent properties in these multicomponent systems. Overall, the work demonstrates the promise of nucleopeptide-based multicomponent hydrogels as a versatile platform for developing advanced supramolecular materials with tailored performance.
items.citation: Tristan Giraud, Marine Koch, Paul Hoschtettler et al.. Synergistic Multicomponent Nucleopeptide-Based Hydrogels: Harnessing DNA-Base Pairing and Electrostatic Complementarities. ACS Materials Au. 2026

items.title: Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications
items.summary: This review examines how the integration of multiomics technologies and artificial intelligence is reshaping precision drug discovery and translational medicine. The authors survey how genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic approaches collectively illuminate the molecular underpinnings of disease, while deep learning architectures extract meaningful patterns from these complex datasets. The paper analyzes how this combined framework can accelerate target identification, lead optimization, drug repositioning, and de novo compound discovery, as well as improve virtual screening, pharmacokinetic modeling, and clinical trial design. The review draws on examples from oncology, neurodegenerative diseases, and cardiovascular conditions to illustrate practical applications, while also acknowledging persistent challenges such as harmonizing disparate data streams, ensuring reproducibility, and reducing algorithmic bias. The authors conclude that convergence of multiomics and artificial intelligence represents a foundational shift toward more precise, data-driven therapeutic development across the bench-to-clinic continuum.
items.citation: Yuqing Liu, Kun Zhu, Weijun Peng et al.. Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: CRISPR-Cas systems as next-generation antimicrobials: a systemic review of mechanisms, delivery strategies, and translational challenges
items.summary: This systematic review examined the potential of CRISPR-Cas systems as precision antimicrobials against multidrug-resistant bacteria, which have increasingly rendered conventional antibiotics ineffective. The authors synthesized preclinical and experimental evidence on different CRISPR effector types, focusing on their mechanisms of antibacterial action, delivery platforms, and safety profiles. The findings indicate that CRISPR-Cas systems can effectively kill resistant bacteria or restore antibiotic sensitivity through mechanisms such as chromosomal double-strand break induction, resistance plasmid elimination, and RNA-targeted cleavage, with Cas9 being the most commonly studied effector. Among delivery strategies evaluated—including bacteriophages, conjugative plasmids, and nanoparticles—phage-mediated delivery showed the most consistent efficacy, and one CRISPR-enhanced phage cocktail has progressed to clinical evaluation. Despite this promise, the review identifies substantial translational barriers including limited bacterial host range, physiological instability, emergence of escape mutations, and insufficient long-term safety data, highlighting the need for optimized delivery systems, multiplex targeting approaches, and clearer regulatory frameworks.
items.citation: Maha S.I. Wizrah. CRISPR-Cas systems as next-generation antimicrobials: a systemic review of mechanisms, delivery strategies, and translational challenges. Frontiers in Microbiology. 2026

items.title: MXene quantum dot polymer nanocomposites as smart platforms for targeted drug delivery and multifunctional biomedical applications: an updated review
items.summary: This review examines MXene quantum dot polymer nanocomposites and their potential as multifunctional platforms for targeted drug delivery and broader biomedical applications. The paper surveys how the exceptional electrical conductivity, flexibility, and biocompatibility of MXenes and their composites enable the design of smart microrobots capable of precise navigation and controlled therapeutic release, particularly in cancer treatment. Combining MXenes with quantum dots in polymer matrices merges electrical, optical, and catalytic properties, expanding utility across drug delivery, tissue engineering, flexible electronics, and energy storage. Stimuli-responsive polymers within these systems allow controlled activation of therapeutic agents, and the customizable surfaces of these materials support co-delivery of multiple drugs for synergistic treatment effects. The review concludes that while significant promise exists, challenges in scalable production, long-term stability, and regulatory translation must be addressed before clinical implementation can be realized.
items.citation: Mohammad Hossein Karami, Omid Moini Jazani. MXene quantum dot polymer nanocomposites as smart platforms for targeted drug delivery and multifunctional biomedical applications: an updated review. Discover Nano. 2026

items.title: Direct cell-to-cell transmission of retrotransposons
items.summary: This paper investigated how certain transposable elements move between cells, challenging the assumption that retrotransposons are restricted to the cell in which they are expressed. Using genetics, imaging, and electron microscopy in the Drosophila ovary, the researchers discovered that a group of long terminal repeat retrotransposons can transmit from somatic cells to the germline without the fusogenic Envelope protein normally required for retroviral entry. Instead, these retrotransposons encode a short transmembrane protein called sORF2 that has structural similarities to viral cell-cell fusogens and localizes to invasive somatic protrusions that carry retroviral capsids and physically contact the oocyte membrane. Eliminating sORF2 abolished both protrusion formation and soma-to-germline capsid transmission, demonstrating its essential role in this process. The researchers further found that sORF2-like proteins are broadly distributed among insect retrotransposons and appear in certain fish and bird viruses, indicating that this Envelope-independent transmission mechanism is shared across retrotransposons and non-enveloped viruses.
items.citation: Maya Voichek, Andreas Bernhard, Lea Lauterjung et al.. Direct cell-to-cell transmission of retrotransposons. Cell. 2026

items.title: Influence of protein aggregates, extracellular vesicles, and lipoprotein fusion on ionizable lipid nanoparticles protein corona analysis
items.summary: This perspective paper examines the analytical challenges inherent in studying the protein corona that forms around ionizable lipid nanoparticles used in nucleic acid therapeutics. The central problem addressed is that blood-borne contaminants, including extracellular vesicles, lipoproteins, and protein aggregates, co-isolate with lipid nanoparticles during analysis and obscure the true composition of the protein corona. The authors argue that because apolipoprotein adsorption drives rapid hepatic uptake, accurately characterizing the corona is essential for engineering lipid nanoparticles with organ-specific delivery properties. The paper proposes that the protein corona on these soft lipid-based materials is fundamentally more fluid and dynamic than the rigid coronas observed on inorganic nanoparticles, necessitating tailored proteomic strategies rather than conventional approaches. The authors advocate for refined investigative methods capable of distinguishing genuine corona proteins from co-isolated impurities as a prerequisite for rational design of extrahepatic delivery systems.
items.citation: Babak Borhan, Amanda M. Murray, Amir Ata Saei et al.. Influence of protein aggregates, extracellular vesicles, and lipoprotein fusion on ionizable lipid nanoparticles protein corona analysis. Nature Communications. 2026

items.title: SceneBloom: Agentic Indoor Environment Generation with Realistic and Diverse Layouts for Embodied Learning
items.summary: SceneBloom is a framework for generating realistic and diverse indoor 3D environments to support the training of embodied agents. The approach combines a hierarchical diffusion-based sampler that generates furniture arrangements within functional zones with a contract-guided compiler that extracts spatial relations from these proposals to perform geometric fitting and pose correction into physically valid scenes. Evaluated across five room types, the method produces layouts with higher visual quality and physical stability than compared baselines, with no detected mesh collisions or out-of-bounds objects, and distributions closer to those of real rooms. Notably, object navigation policies trained in the generated environments outperform those trained on an equivalent number of real indoor scans when tested on held-out real environments.
items.citation: Yuhan Liu, Lianhui Qin, Shenji Wan. SceneBloom: Agentic Indoor Environment Generation with Realistic and Diverse Layouts for Embodied Learning. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Distributed Quantum-Centric Supercomputing with Multi-Layered Generative Learning for Intermolecular Interactions
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of applying quantum-centric supercomputing to large molecular systems, where conventional approaches are limited by qubit counts, circuit depth, and computational cost. The authors developed a distributed framework that decomposes complex molecular electronic structure problems into smaller parallel sub-problems, each requiring fewer qubits and shallower quantum circuits. A two-step aggregation scheme reconstructs the global solution by mapping local results to global indices and recovering inter-fragment correlations using a multi-layered generative machine learning architecture built on a physics-informed generative solver. Applied to water and formamide dimers as well as the water hexamer, the framework dramatically reduces the diagonalization dimension while improving energy accuracy by an order of magnitude compared to conventional sample-based quantum diagonalization. The water hexamer demonstration is particularly notable, as it successfully partitions a large qubit problem into much smaller monomer subsystems and reassembles the solution with accuracy comparable to classical reference methods.
items.citation: Chayan Patra, Prayas Ghosh, Adwait Patkhedkar et al.. Distributed Quantum-Centric Supercomputing with Multi-Layered Generative Learning for Intermolecular Interactions. arXiv. 2026

items.title: MiD-VLM: Detecting and Grounding Global Semantic Misinformation in Image-Caption Pairs
items.summary: This paper investigates the detection of semantic misinformation in image-caption pairs, where an authentic image is combined with a misleading caption that distorts its narrative without introducing any pixel-level manipulations. To address this challenge, the authors developed a multimodal model that fuses image-text representations with visual scene features through a projection layer and fine-tunes a large vision-language model using parameter-efficient adaptation via low-rank approximation. The system was evaluated on a dataset specifically designed for global semantic inconsistency detection, where it jointly classifies whether a pair is authentic, identifies the type of manipulation, and localizes the misleading tokens within the caption. The model achieved strong performance on binary authenticity classification, demonstrating that parameter-efficient adaptation of vision-language models is an effective strategy for detecting semantic misinformation. The authors also highlight that precise token-level grounding of misleading content remains an open challenge warranting further investigation.
items.citation: Tarunya Prasad, Bharatesh Chakravarthi. MiD-VLM: Detecting and Grounding Global Semantic Misinformation in Image-Caption Pairs. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Flownomaly: Single-Step Conditional-Mean Recovery for Few-Shot Anomaly Detection
items.summary: This paper addresses few-shot industrial anomaly detection, where models must learn to identify defects from only a small number of defect-free reference images. The proposed method, Flownomaly, reframes the task as recovering a normal counterpart for a given query image by learning a velocity field through conditional flow matching over frozen patch-level features from a pretrained vision model. A key innovation is that the optimal transport path between Gaussian noise and normal features is straight, enabling single-step recovery of the posterior mean without iterative trajectory integration, and a normal-only Jacobian-based criterion selects the operating time without requiring any anomalous examples. Anomaly signals are then derived by comparing query tokens to their recovered normal counterparts, enabling both pixel-level localization and image-level detection. Evaluated across multiple few-shot benchmarks on standard industrial inspection datasets, Flownomaly achieves state-of-the-art performance, including notable improvements over the strongest baselines in challenging low-data settings.
items.citation: Bernardo Perrone Ribeiro, Erkut Akdag, Egor Bondarev. Flownomaly: Single-Step Conditional-Mean Recovery for Few-Shot Anomaly Detection. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Robotic Optical Coherence Tomography-Guided Geometric Modeling of Soft Tissue: 3D Representations for Data-Driven Closed-Loop Shape Control
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of controlling soft-tissue deformation in medical robotics at the microscale, where localized changes are difficult to observe and represent while physics-based approaches are computationally demanding. The researchers developed a data-driven framework that uses optical coherence tomography to provide high-resolution volumetric feedback, learning tissue manipulation policies from user demonstrations and executing them in closed-loop fashion. They systematically compared multiple three-dimensional tissue representations—including full-volume, tissue-masked sparse-volume, and voxelized point-cloud approaches—combined with or without residual conditioning, across both deterministic and generative diffusion policy architectures. Testing across hundreds of phantom rollouts on depth and directional manipulation tasks showed that residual conditioning consistently improved shape accuracy, with voxelized point-cloud representations paired with residual conditioning achieving the best performance, and the framework generalized to ex vivo porcine tissue with geometric errors comparable to human demonstrations. The work establishes volumetric OCT as an effective source of both current and goal state representations for learned closed-loop tissue shape control.
items.citation: Chaoyu Zhang, Guangshen Ma, Mark Draelos. Robotic Optical Coherence Tomography-Guided Geometric Modeling of Soft Tissue: 3D Representations for Data-Driven Closed-Loop Shape Control. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A probabilistic approach to separate mergers and jellyfish galaxies: Application of morphological non-parametric indexes to the DESI Legacy Survey
items.summary: This study investigates how non-parametric morphological indices can classify galaxies into regular spirals, regular ellipticals, mergers, and jellyfish galaxies (ram-pressure-stripping candidates) using imaging from the DESI Legacy Surveys. The researchers measured ten non-parametric morphological indices and evaluated their discriminating power in two-dimensional diagnostic planes using a cross-validated Bayesian kernel-density classifier, while also combining all indices through calibrated gradient-boosted machine learning models. They found that planes combining Shannon entropy with asymmetry or concentration indices perform best for separating regular from disturbed galaxies, and that a multi-class machine learning model achieves strong performance for broad structural classification, delivering probabilistic classifications for over a million galaxies. Distinguishing mergers from jellyfish candidates proved more difficult, as jellyfish galaxies occupy a relatively coherent region of morphological parameter space while mergers display diverse and overlapping morphologies. The results demonstrate that non-parametric morphology reliably detects structural disturbance but struggles to identify its physical origin, highlighting a fundamental limitation in using imaging alone to disentangle environmental from interaction-driven processes.
items.citation: V. M. Sampaio, Y. Jaff'e, A. Moretti et al.. A probabilistic approach to separate mergers and jellyfish galaxies: Application of morphological non-parametric indexes to the DESI Legacy Survey. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Multiplexed Nucleic Acid Detection Using Sequence-Specific Cleavage Mediated by Repair Endonucleases.
items.summary: This paper introduces TIMBER, a non-CRISPR nucleic acid detection platform designed to overcome limitations of existing diagnostic methods for infectious disease and cancer applications. Rather than relying on the collateral nuclease activity characteristic of CRISPR-based diagnostics, TIMBER employs repair endonucleases that cleave abasic-site-containing probes only when hybridized to a matched target sequence, conferring high specificity including single-nucleotide polymorphism discrimination. The platform achieves sensitive detection both with and without preamplification, and results can be read by visual fluorescence or lateral flow, supporting point-of-care deployment. The authors validated TIMBER by detecting SARS-CoV-2 in clinical saliva samples and demonstrated simultaneous multiplexed detection of four targets, including identification of cancer-relevant mutations in lung tumor samples. Overall, TIMBER is presented as a flexible, low-instrument-burden solution for diverse nucleic acid diagnostics spanning viral surveillance and cancer genotyping.
items.citation: Garden PM, Li Y, Murugan V et al.. Multiplexed Nucleic Acid Detection Using Sequence-Specific Cleavage Mediated by Repair Endonucleases.. ACS sensors. 2026

items.title: Smartphone-Based Peptide Nucleic Acid (PNA) Probe-Assisted Potentiometric Biosensor for Point-of-Care Testing of SARS-CoV-2 Nucleic Acid
items.summary: This paper developed a potentiometric biosensor for detecting SARS-CoV-2 nucleic acid suitable for point-of-care applications. The system used electrostatically neutral peptide nucleic acid probes immobilized on amine-functionalized magnetic beads and combined with a screen-printed carbon electrode modified with a plasticized polymeric membrane, exploiting the neutrality of peptide nucleic acids to reduce biofouling caused by positively charged biomolecules adhering to conventional negatively charged DNA probes. After the peptide nucleic acid probe bound its complementary viral DNA target, cationic magnetic nanoparticles were added, and a magnetic field was applied to concentrate the complex at the electrode surface for potentiometric signal readout. The optimized biosensor achieved detection of SARS-CoV-2 DNA across a wide linear range at attomolar concentrations, with high recovery rates when tested in human saliva samples. A smartphone-based near-field communication electrochemical analyzer was integrated into the platform to enable wireless, portable measurements, demonstrating the potential of this antifouling approach for sensitive COVID-19 screening in biological samples.
items.citation: Tuğba Özer, Sakda Jampasa, Atchara Lomae et al.. Smartphone-Based Peptide Nucleic Acid (PNA) Probe-Assisted Potentiometric Biosensor for Point-of-Care Testing of SARS-CoV-2 Nucleic Acid. Analytical Chemistry. 2026

items.title: The Oral–Gut–Brain Axis: From Periodontal Dysbiosis to Neuroinflammation—Mechanistic Pathways, Salivary and Intestinal Biomarkers, and Therapeutic Targets: A Narrative Review
items.summary: This narrative review examined the biological connections linking periodontal disease, gut health, and brain function within a proposed oral–gut–brain axis, with a focus on how oral dysbiosis may drive systemic inflammation culminating in neurodegeneration. The authors synthesized evidence from a broad literature search spanning over two decades, evaluating molecular mechanisms, relevant biomarkers, and potential therapeutic targets across this tripartite pathway. Key findings indicate that periodontal pathogens, particularly certain gram-negative bacteria, can translocate to the gut, disrupting intestinal barrier integrity and altering microbial community composition, changes that have been associated with increased blood–brain barrier permeability, microglial activation, and amyloid-beta accumulation. Salivary and intestinal biomarkers reflecting inflammatory burden were identified as promising non-invasive tools for monitoring disease risk across the entire axis. The authors conclude that while the oral–gut–brain axis offers a plausible unifying framework for understanding shared comorbidities among periodontal, cardiometabolic, and neurodegenerative conditions, existing evidence remains largely associative and preclinical, necessitating longitudinal human studies to establish causal directionality and validate therapeutic interventions.
items.citation: Caterina Nela Dumitru, Alina Oana Dumitru, Gabriel Valeriu Popa et al.. The Oral–Gut–Brain Axis: From Periodontal Dysbiosis to Neuroinflammation—Mechanistic Pathways, Salivary and Intestinal Biomarkers, and Therapeutic Targets: A Narrative Review. Dentistry Journal. 2026

items.title: Consented Universal Newborn Screening for Congenital Cytomegalovirus Infection Using Dried Blood Spot and Dried Saliva Spot Specimens: Implementation and Relative Programmatic Accuracy.
items.summary: This study evaluated two specimen types — dried blood spots and dried saliva spots — for use in universal newborn screening for congenital cytomegalovirus infection, comparing their diagnostic accuracy and practical implementation across a large multi-center prospective pilot. Both specimen types were collected from newborns at birth and tested using quantitative PCR assays, with positive screens confirmed by urine testing. Dried saliva spots did not significantly improve sensitivity for detecting congenital cytomegalovirus compared to dried blood spots, while generating a substantially higher false positive rate, meaning each additional true case identified by saliva testing came at the cost of multiple unnecessary confirmatory work-ups. Saliva-based screening also extended turnaround times, frequently preventing confirmatory testing within the window required to definitively distinguish congenital from postnatal infection. Based on this performance profile, the authors concluded that dried saliva spot screening did not support population-wide implementation in their program.
items.citation: Santander E, Reuvers E, Lacaria M et al.. Consented Universal Newborn Screening for Congenital Cytomegalovirus Infection Using Dried Blood Spot and Dried Saliva Spot Specimens: Implementation and Relative Programmatic Accuracy.. International journal of neonatal screening. 2026

items.title: Vitamin D<sub>3</sub> oral rinsing reduces salivary SARS-CoV-2 antigen detectability: a clinical trial with public health implications.
items.summary: This clinical trial investigated whether rinsing with a Vitamin D₃ oral rinse before saliva collection could affect the results of SARS-CoV-2 rapid antigen tests (RAT). Adults with confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection provided paired saliva samples immediately before and after a one-minute Vitamin D₃ oral rinse, with samples analyzed by both rapid antigen testing and RT-PCR under blinded conditions. The oral rinse converted a large majority of RAT-positive samples to RAT-negative, substantially reducing antigen positivity, while RT-PCR positivity and cycle threshold values remained largely unchanged, indicating that viral RNA was still present despite reduced antigen detection. The strong concordance between paired RT-PCR results confirmed that the viral genetic material persisted even when antigen testing failed to detect infection. The authors conclude that Vitamin D₃ oral rinsing represents a previously unrecognized pre-analytical variable that can compromise the accuracy of saliva-based antigen screening, with important implications for infectious disease surveillance and public health testing programs.
items.citation: Feteih SMN, Heaphy ELG, Aljagthmi A et al.. Vitamin D<sub>3</sub> oral rinsing reduces salivary SARS-CoV-2 antigen detectability: a clinical trial with public health implications.. Frontiers in oral health. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of Molecular Testing on Saliva and Oral Swabs for Pulmonary Tuberculosis.
items.summary: This study evaluated whether molecular testing on saliva and oral swabs could serve as accurate, non-sputum alternatives for diagnosing pulmonary tuberculosis, addressing a key gap in TB detection. A nested case-control study was conducted within a prospective cohort of adults and children being evaluated for pulmonary TB at primary care centers in Colombia, with participants providing sputum for liquid mycobacterial culture alongside saliva and nylon-flocked oral swabs tested using Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra. Saliva demonstrated high sensitivity and specificity against culture-confirmed TB, exceeding the World Health Organization's target threshold for a low-complexity non-sputum diagnostic, while oral swabs showed somewhat lower sensitivity but similarly high specificity. Saliva outperformed oral swabs in sensitivity by a meaningful absolute margin, though the two sample types did not differ significantly in specificity. The vast majority of participants found both collection methods acceptable, supporting their potential as practical alternatives to sputum-based TB diagnosis.
items.venue: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
items.citation: Vargas DA, Fuertes-Bucheli JF, Sanchez-Hidalgo A et al.. Diagnostic Accuracy of Molecular Testing on Saliva and Oral Swabs for Pulmonary Tuberculosis.. Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America. 2026

items.title: Bioactive Gold Plasmonic Interfaces Meet Artificial Intelligence: Advancing Saliva-Based Surface-Enhanced Raman Spectroscopy Diagnostics.
items.summary: This review examines how bioactive gold plasmonic nanostructures combined with artificial intelligence can advance saliva-based surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy as a non-invasive diagnostic platform. The authors analyze how structural and chemical features of gold nanostructures—including geometry, surface functionalization, antifouling strategies, and protein-corona formation—govern molecular access to electromagnetic hot spots and ultimately determine spectral reproducibility and computational reliability. Saliva is framed as a broadly applicable liquid biopsy relevant to oncological, infectious, inflammatory, metabolic, neurodegenerative, and pulmonary diseases, with case studies illustrating how substrate engineering and dataset construction jointly shape diagnostic performance. The review identifies that human studies directly combining saliva, gold-enabled surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy, and artificial intelligence remain limited, prompting explicit criteria to distinguish direct salivary evidence from studies using related biospecimens. The authors conclude that clinically viable diagnostics in this space require coordinated co-design of plasmonic interfaces and computational pipelines alongside standardized pre-analytics, reproducible substrates, and rigorous multicenter validation.
items.citation: Dhal A, Aviña AE, Hang NLT et al.. Bioactive Gold Plasmonic Interfaces Meet Artificial Intelligence: Advancing Saliva-Based Surface-Enhanced Raman Spectroscopy Diagnostics.. Small (Weinheim an der Bergstrasse, Germany). 2026

items.title: Lethal hantavirus at sea: Infectious disease outbreaks on cruise ships and limits of preparedness
items.summary: This paper examines a lethal hantavirus outbreak aboard an expedition cruise ship traveling through the South Atlantic, representing an unusual occurrence of this zoonotic disease in a maritime setting. The authors analyze the epidemiological circumstances of the cluster, including the vessel's itinerary across ecologically diverse remote regions, and discuss the challenges of identifying the point-source exposure given that transmission may have occurred before embarkation, during shore excursions, or on board. Unlike typical cruise ship outbreaks driven by sustained person-to-person transmission, hantavirus is acquired primarily through inhalation of aerosolized rodent excreta, complicating the public health investigation and requiring laboratory confirmation and viral sequencing to establish the origin. The paper situates this incident within the broader context of infectious disease preparedness in maritime environments, highlighting the intersection of global travel, wildlife exposure, and emerging zoonotic risks. The authors conclude that the outbreak exposes important gaps in outbreak preparedness for cruise settings, particularly when the causative pathogen has an environmental rather than interpersonal transmission route.
items.citation: Alimuddin I. Zumla, Brian McCloskey, Giuseppe Ippolito et al.. Lethal hantavirus at sea: Infectious disease outbreaks on cruise ships and limits of preparedness. Travel Medicine and Infectious Disease. 2026

items.title: Andes virus outbreak linked to expedition cruise ship travel, multi-country investigation and response, April to June 2026
items.summary: The abstract describes an active outbreak investigation of Andes orthohantavirus linked to an expedition cruise ship, involving cases among both passengers and crew members across multiple nationalities. The investigation employed medical evacuation, repatriation, international contact tracing, isolation, quarantine, and laboratory testing to manage spread. A notable case fatality proportion was recorded, and the event highlighted the complexity of responding to a zoonotic hemorrhagic fever virus in a multi-national maritime travel setting. Ongoing work seeks to clarify the source of exposure, identify risk factors, and prevent further transmission. The abstract is preliminary in nature, reflecting an investigation still underway at the time of reporting.
items.citation: Oda E. van den Berg, UKHSA ANDV Team, Ettore Severi et al.. Andes virus outbreak linked to expedition cruise ship travel, multi-country investigation and response, April to June 2026. Eurosurveillance. 2026

items.title: Human infection with Andes hantavirus: an update for the general physician
items.summary: Andes virus (ANDV) is a zoonotic hantavirus transmitted to humans via inhalation of rodent excreta and is unique among hantaviruses in its capacity for sustained human-to-human transmission through respiratory droplets and close contact. This paper provides an updated clinical review of ANDV infection for general physicians, covering its epidemiology, transmission dynamics, clinical spectrum, and management. The most severe manifestation, Hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome, is characterized by acute respiratory failure, hemodynamic instability, organ involvement, and dysregulated immune responses, with disease severity linked to specific hematological and biochemical markers. No approved antiviral treatment or vaccine exists, leaving supportive care as the only management strategy, and case fatality rates have remained high in recent outbreaks. A cruise ship outbreak in 2026 involving passengers of multiple nationalities illustrates how ANDV's transmission potential, combined with international travel, can rapidly give a regionally endemic pathogen global reach, highlighting the need for clinician awareness and coordinated outbreak preparedness.
items.citation: Emanuele Durante‐Mangoni, Iolanda Cafarella, Silvia Mercadante et al.. Human infection with Andes hantavirus: an update for the general physician. European Journal of Internal Medicine. 2026

items.title: Current Challenges and Potential Strategies to Enhance Efficacy of Oral Phage Therapy in Food Animals: A Systematic Review with Quantitative Analysis
items.summary: This systematic review examined the current state of oral phage therapy in food animals, focusing on the barriers posed by the gastrointestinal environment and strategies to overcome them. Following established guidelines, the authors searched multiple databases and synthesized findings from over a hundred articles, extracting data on phage stability under gastrointestinal conditions and the methods used to assess it. Their quantitative analysis revealed that most phages targeting antimicrobial-resistant bacteria in food animals remain stable across a moderate pH range but are rapidly inactivated under the highly acidic conditions of the stomach, as well as by elevated temperatures, digestive enzymes, bile salts, and host immune responses. The review also identified considerable inconsistency in laboratory protocols used to simulate gastrointestinal conditions, complicating cross-study comparisons. The authors conclude that protective strategies such as microencapsulation with alginate or chitosan and enteric-coated delivery systems show promise, but that standardization of stability assessment methods, deeper understanding of immune responses to oral phage delivery, and improved scalability of encapsulation techniques are needed before oral phage therapy can be reliably implemented in food animal production.
items.citation: Md Ashiqur Rahman, Rebecca Jane Abraham, David John Hampson et al.. Current Challenges and Potential Strategies to Enhance Efficacy of Oral Phage Therapy in Food Animals: A Systematic Review with Quantitative Analysis. Viruses. 2026

items.title: SEMAC: Spherical Energy Matching Ambisonics Codec for Efficient Higher-Order Ambisonics Compression
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of efficiently compressing Higher-Order Ambisonics audio, a format used for immersive spatial audio that becomes increasingly expensive to transmit as spherical harmonic order grows because the channel count scales quadratically. The authors propose SEMAC, a codec that encodes a full-order directional energy envelope separately from a reduced set of transport channels coded using the CELT framework, rather than transmitting every Ambisonics channel individually. The key insight generalizes CELT's existing per-band energy/shape separation to the directional domain, allowing the decoder to restore the full spatial energy distribution even though only a lower-dimensional signal subspace is transmitted. Perceptual evaluation using MUSHRA listening tests on fifth-order material showed that SEMAC using roughly half the transport channels of a full-order representation was rated higher than the standard Opus Channel Mapping Family 3 approach at the tested bitrates. The results indicate that coding fewer transport channels at higher fidelity while preserving the directional energy envelope is perceptually superior to coding all Ambisonics channels at lower precision.
items.citation: Christoph Hold, Jan Buethe, Jean-Marc Valin et al.. SEMAC: Spherical Energy Matching Ambisonics Codec for Efficient Higher-Order Ambisonics Compression. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Comprehensive Visible and Near-infrared Keck and Gemini Monitoring and Characterization of Interstellar Comet 3I/ATLAS during its Encounter with the Solar System
items.summary: This paper presents an extensive multi-epoch observational campaign characterizing the interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS across visible and near-infrared wavelengths using the Keck and Gemini observatories, spanning nearly a year bracketing its perihelion passage. Optical colors remained stable through perihelion, while dust activity tracked a steeper power-law decline outbound than inbound, and estimated dust mass losses correspond to layers of material roughly tens of centimeters to about one meter deep across the nucleus surface. The coma morphology evolved from a concentrated, structured appearance before perihelion to a more extended dust distribution afterward, and gas abundance ratios showed measurable changes, with the C₂-to-CN ratio nearly doubling while the C₃-to-CN ratio fell between successive spectroscopic epochs. Near-infrared photometry and spectroscopy revealed moderately red colors, but no robust detection of water-ice absorption was found across any of the tested continuum and calibration scenarios. The authors present these observations as a comprehensive baseline record of an interstellar object's solar encounter and a reference point for understanding future interstellar visitors.
items.citation: Bryce T. Bolin, Jeffrey Cooke, Brian C. Lemaux et al.. Comprehensive Visible and Near-infrared Keck and Gemini Monitoring and Characterization of Interstellar Comet 3I/ATLAS during its Encounter with the Solar System. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Distributed Quantum-Centric Supercomputing with Multi-Layered Generative Learning for Intermolecular Interactions
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of performing accurate quantum chemistry calculations on large molecular systems using quantum-centric supercomputing, where quantum processors and classical high-performance computers work together to solve electronic structure problems. The authors developed a distributed framework that breaks complex molecular problems into smaller sub-problems requiring fewer qubits and shallower quantum circuits, then reconstructs the global electronic structure through a two-step aggregation scheme involving optimized bit mapping and recovery of inter-fragment correlations. A multi-layered generative machine learning architecture is central to the approach, combining a physics-informed generative solver for the distributed sub-problems with a secondary generative module that identifies dominant regions of the global Hilbert space. Applied to water and formamide dimers, the method dramatically reduces computational dimensionality while improving energy accuracy by an order of magnitude compared to conventional approaches. The framework successfully decomposes a large water hexamer calculation into manageable monomer subsystems, with results showing strong agreement against established classical reference methods.
items.citation: Chayan Patra, Prayas Ghosh, Adwait Patkhedkar et al.. Distributed Quantum-Centric Supercomputing with Multi-Layered Generative Learning for Intermolecular Interactions. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Shared clones make random cell halves look reproducible in pooled screens
items.summary: Pooled single-cell perturbation screens like Perturb-seq are widely used to train and evaluate models predicting the effects of genetic perturbations, with reproducibility typically assessed by randomly splitting each perturbation's cells into two halves. This paper demonstrates that such random splits are not independent replicates because cells sharing the same guide RNA descend from a limited pool of transduced progenitors, meaning both halves contain the same clones—a form of pseudoreplication invisible in the data. Using null perturbations as controls and comparing random halves against independent replicates from separate transductions, the authors showed that random halves agree far more often than true replicates, and that measuring more cells does not resolve this inflation. The excess agreement was eliminated by splitting cells into halves that share no clonal lineage, and its magnitude across many screens varied with clone diversity—being largest in primary T cells and smallest in non-dividing neurons, and orders of magnitude smaller in cell lines. As a consequence, published models predicting perturbation effects appear to outperform a perturbation-agnostic baseline when evaluated within a single transduction but fall below that baseline when tested against cells from an independent transduction, indicating that reproducibility in such screens must be assessed across separate transductions.
items.citation: Xuanrui Huang. Shared clones make random cell halves look reproducible in pooled screens. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Robotic Optical Coherence Tomography-Guided Geometric Modeling of Soft Tissue: 3D Representations for Data-Driven Closed-Loop Shape Control
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of controlling soft tissue deformation at microscale in medical robotics, where observation and representation of localized tissue changes are difficult and physics-based models are impractical. The researchers developed a data-driven framework that uses optical coherence tomography to provide high-resolution volumetric feedback, with policies learned from user demonstrations and executed in closed-loop. They systematically compared multiple three-dimensional tissue representations—full-volume, tissue-masked sparse-volume, and voxelized point-cloud—combined with or without residual conditioning, evaluated under both deterministic and generative diffusion policy architectures across depth and directional manipulation tasks. Residual conditioning consistently improved shape control accuracy, and voxelized point-cloud representations with residuals achieved the best performance, with results extending successfully to ex vivo porcine tissue at accuracy levels comparable to human demonstrations. The findings establish volumetric OCT-derived representations as effective current- and goal-state encodings for learned closed-loop tissue shape control.
items.citation: Chaoyu Zhang, Guangshen Ma, Mark Draelos. Robotic Optical Coherence Tomography-Guided Geometric Modeling of Soft Tissue: 3D Representations for Data-Driven Closed-Loop Shape Control. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A probabilistic approach to separate mergers and jellyfish galaxies: Application of morphological non-parametric indexes to the DESI Legacy Survey
items.summary: This paper investigates how non-parametric morphological indices can be used to classify galaxies into regular spirals, regular ellipticals, mergers, and jellyfish galaxies (ram-pressure stripping candidates) using imaging from the DESI Legacy Surveys. The authors measured ten non-parametric morphological indices and evaluated their discriminating power using a cross-validated Bayesian kernel-density classifier in two-dimensional diagnostic planes, as well as a more sophisticated probability-calibrated gradient boosting model combining all indices. They found that combining Shannon entropy with asymmetry or concentration indices provides the most informative diagnostics, and that the multi-index machine learning model substantially outperforms any single two-dimensional plane, achieving high balanced accuracy for three-class separation of regular versus perturbed systems. Distinguishing mergers from jellyfish galaxies specifically proved more difficult, as mergers occupy diverse and overlapping regions of morphological parameter space while jellyfish candidates cluster more coherently. The study delivers probabilistic classifications for nearly two million galaxies and establishes that non-parametric morphology reliably detects structural disturbance but struggles to identify its physical origin when comparing these two perturbation types.
items.citation: V. M. Sampaio, Y. Jaff'e, A. Moretti et al.. A probabilistic approach to separate mergers and jellyfish galaxies: Application of morphological non-parametric indexes to the DESI Legacy Survey. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Quarantine-associated viral pathogens in non-human primates: pathobiology, diagnostic surveillance, control strategies, and one health implications
items.citation: Bae G, Jeon E, Mo J et al.. Quarantine-associated viral pathogens in non-human primates: pathobiology, diagnostic surveillance, control strategies, and one health implications. Frontiers in veterinary science. 2026

items.title: Plasmonic Nanoarray Biosensors for Non-Invasive Cancer Diagnostics.
items.summary: This review examined the potential of plasmonic nanoarray biosensors as a platform for detecting cancer-associated biomarkers in non-invasive body fluids, specifically urine and saliva. The paper surveyed nanoarray architectures, fabrication strategies, surface functionalization approaches, and optical signal generation mechanisms—including localized surface plasmon resonance, surface-enhanced Raman scattering, and metal-enhanced fluorescence—as applied to nucleic acids, proteins, and extracellular vesicles relevant to several cancer types. The authors identified key analytical advantages of these biosensors, such as electromagnetic field concentration and capacity for multiplexed readout, which help address the challenges of low biomarker abundance and complex fluid matrices inherent to urine and saliva. However, the review also highlighted persistent obstacles to clinical translation, including biofouling, pre-analytical variability, inconsistent fabrication reproducibility, and insufficient validation with authentic clinical samples. The authors conclude that overcoming these barriers will require standardized biofluid processing, scalable manufacturing, and full integration with microfluidic sample-handling systems.
items.citation: Kim SE, Choi HK, Choi JH. Plasmonic Nanoarray Biosensors for Non-Invasive Cancer Diagnostics.. Biosensors. 2026

items.title: Group A Streptococcus molecular point of care testing in a paediatric emergency department.
items.summary: This pilot study investigated whether molecular point-of-care testing for Group A Streptococcus could improve antibiotic stewardship and clinical management in children presenting to a paediatric emergency department. Researchers enrolled children under sixteen years old who already had a conventional throat swab ordered by their clinician, collecting a second swab processed by a rapid molecular test whose results did not influence actual treatment decisions. The study found that the large majority of children who received antibiotics tested negative on the molecular point-of-care test, suggesting that many antibiotic prescriptions may have been unnecessary, while conventional culture results took several days to return compared to the near-immediate results from the molecular test. The authors conclude that a rapid "rule out" point-of-care test has potential to substantially reduce antibiotic use in this setting, provided that concern about streptococcal infection is the primary reason for prescribing, though they note that further research is needed to establish whether such testing delivers an overall net clinical benefit.
items.citation: Mills EA, Bingham R, Nijman RG et al.. Group A Streptococcus molecular point of care testing in a paediatric emergency department.. The Journal of antimicrobial chemotherapy. 2026

items.title: Biological characteristics and whole-genome sequencing analysis of an alpha-hemolytic Streptococcus pyogenes strain
items.summary: This study investigated an unusual alpha-hemolytic strain of *Streptococcus pyogenes*, a species that typically displays beta-hemolysis, isolated from erysipelas skin secretions at a tertiary care hospital. The researchers used whole-genome sequencing, mass spectrometry-based identification, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, multilocus sequence typing, and comprehensive bioinformatic analyses to characterize the strain's identity, resistance genes, virulence factors, and phylogenetic relationships. The isolate was confirmed as *S. pyogenes* sequence type ST176 with emm type 58.7, harboring multiple virulence-associated genes and resistance genes conferring resistance to macrolides and tetracycline while remaining susceptible to penicillins and cephalosporins. The atypical alpha-hemolytic phenotype was attributed to a single amino acid substitution in the sagB gene that likely disrupts functional expression of streptolysin S, yet this phenotypic deviation did not affect the organism's virulence potential or antibiotic resistance profile. The authors caution that the resemblance of this strain to commensal viridans streptococci creates a risk of clinical misidentification and advocate for combining antigen detection, serology, and molecular methods to improve detection of atypically presenting *S. pyogenes* strains.
items.citation: Mo Y, Wang Q, Qiu M. Biological characteristics and whole-genome sequencing analysis of an alpha-hemolytic Streptococcus pyogenes strain. 2026

items.title: Gut microbial-derived metabolites: key players in kidney disease and renal fibrosis
items.summary: This review examines the relationship between gut microbial-derived metabolites and kidney disease, including acute kidney injury and various forms of chronic kidney disease. The authors synthesize current evidence showing that kidney injury disrupts intestinal barrier function and gut microbial balance, leading to reduced beneficial short-chain fatty acids and excessive accumulation of uremic toxins such as indoxyl sulfate and trimethylamine-N-oxide. These metabolites influence renal pathology and fibrosis by modulating multiple signaling pathways, with tryptophan metabolites highlighted as particularly central to gut-kidney communication. The review maps the underlying pathophysiological mechanisms linking dysbiotic metabolite profiles to conditions including diabetic kidney disease, immunoglobulin A nephropathy, and membranous nephropathy. It also evaluates therapeutic strategies targeting gut microbiota dysbiosis, including natural products, prebiotics, probiotics, and renal replacement therapy, with the aim of guiding more precise and concept-driven treatment approaches.
items.citation: Wan-Ying Zhang, Yu-Lu Zhang, Qing-Qing Yu et al.. Gut microbial-derived metabolites: key players in kidney disease and renal fibrosis. International Journal of Biological Sciences. 2026

items.title: Editor's Choice – European Society for Vascular Surgery (ESVS) 2026 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections
items.summary: These guidelines, developed by the European Society for Vascular Surgery, address the clinical management of vascular graft and endograft infections, updating a previous version to reflect current evidence. The guideline development process combined systematic evaluation of the best available scientific evidence with expert opinion, with recommendations graded by both strength and level of evidence according to an established classification system. A substantial set of recommendations was produced covering key domains including definitions, diagnosis, multidisciplinary team management, antimicrobial therapy, management of intracavitary and extracavitary infections, and follow-up care. The guidelines also incorporate shared decision-making principles and patient-facing information, as well as a discussion of unresolved clinical questions. The stated aim is to provide clinicians and patients with comprehensive, up-to-date guidance for selecting optimal management strategies in this challenging condition.
items.venue: European Journal of Vascular and Endovascular Surgery
items.citation: Anne Lejay, Ben R. Saleem, Tara D. Barwick et al.. Editor's Choice – European Society for Vascular Surgery (ESVS) 2026 Clinical Practice Guidelines on the Management of Vascular Graft and Endograft Infections. European Journal of Vascular and Endovascular Surgery. 2026

items.title: The Gut–Vagina Axis
items.summary: This review paper examines the emerging concept of the gut–vagina axis, focusing on the bidirectional relationship between the gut and vaginal microbiomes in female health. The authors synthesize recent advances in microbiome research to characterize how these two distinct microbial communities may communicate through mechanisms including microbial migration, hormonal and immune regulation, and metabolite exchange. The review identifies the most promising features of this gut–vaginal relationship and discusses how disruptions or changes in this bidirectional communication could influence microbial composition, immune responses, and hormonal balance at both local and systemic levels. The authors argue that understanding these interactions may have important implications for female physiological processes and overall health.
items.citation: Lorenzo Agoni, Elena Roselletti, Giovanni Marasco et al.. The Gut–Vagina Axis. Microorganisms. 2026

items.title: Biodiversity and biogeography of the multi-kingdom cancer microbiome
items.citation: Anders B. Dohlman, Robin Mjelle, Henry M. Wood et al.. Biodiversity and biogeography of the multi-kingdom cancer microbiome. Cell. 2026

items.title: Gut Microbial Metabotypes Shape Polyphenol Bioactivity: Toward Precision Nutrition Strategies for Human Health
items.summary: This review examines how the gut microbiota transforms dietary polyphenols into bioactive metabolites and how individual differences in this capacity influence health outcomes. Because many polyphenols are poorly absorbed in the upper gut, colonic microorganisms convert them into smaller compounds such as urolithins, equol, and enterolignans, which may have distinct biological activities compared to their parent molecules. The authors introduce the concept of microbial metabotypes, which classify individuals according to their ability to produce specific microbiota-derived metabolites, and critically assess the evidence linking these metabotypes to effects on mitochondrial function, inflammation, endothelial health, metabolic regulation, gut barrier integrity, and gut-brain communication. The review distinguishes well-characterized metabotype models from those with insufficient standardization and separates human clinical evidence from preclinical findings. While metabotype-guided stratification holds promise for precision nutrition and improving the identification of dietary responders, the authors conclude that clinical translation is currently constrained by inconsistent protocols, non-standardized analytical thresholds, and limited long-term intervention data, positioning microbial metabotypes as valuable research tools rather than established instruments for personalized dietary prescription.
items.citation: Pasquale Perrone, Stefania D’Angelo. Gut Microbial Metabotypes Shape Polyphenol Bioactivity: Toward Precision Nutrition Strategies for Human Health. Nutrients. 2026

items.title: ECCO Guidelines on the Prevention, Diagnosis, and Management of Infections in Inflammatory Bowel Disease
items.summary: These guidelines address the growing challenge of infection risk in inflammatory bowel disease patients who require immunosuppressive therapies, an issue made more complex by the rapid introduction of newer biologic agents and small molecules with distinct immune-modulating profiles. The European Crohn's and Colitis Organisation undertook a structured, evidence-based update to their previous consensus documents to reflect the expanded therapeutic landscape and evolving understanding of infection risk. The guidelines cover risk stratification alongside the prevention, diagnosis, and management of viral, bacterial, mycobacterial, and vaccine-preventable infections in this patient population. A central emphasis is placed on preventative strategies tailored to the contemporary range of treatments, from traditional thiopurines and anti-tumor necrosis factor agents to advanced biologics and small molecules. The update aims to provide clinicians with actionable, current guidance for minimizing infectious morbidity and mortality in immunocompromised inflammatory bowel disease patients.
items.venue: Journal of Crohn s and Colitis
items.citation: Henit A. Yanai, Pierre Ellul, Bram Verstockt et al.. ECCO Guidelines on the Prevention, Diagnosis, and Management of Infections in Inflammatory Bowel Disease. Journal of Crohn s and Colitis. 2026

items.title: SEMAC: Spherical Energy Matching Ambisonics Codec for Efficient Higher-Order Ambisonics Compression
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of efficiently compressing Higher-Order Ambisonics audio, a format used for immersive spatial audio that becomes increasingly expensive to transmit as the spherical harmonic order grows. The authors developed SEMAC, a codec that represents an Ambisonics signal using a quantized directional energy envelope at full spherical harmonic order combined with a reduced number of lower-dimensional transport channels coded with the CELT framework, generalizing CELT's per-band energy separation principle to directional signals. At the decoder, the full-order directional energy distribution is restored by re-imposing the envelope captured at the encoder input onto the lower-dimensional decoded signal. Perceptual listening tests using the MUSHRA methodology on fifth-order material showed that SEMAC using roughly half the transport channels of the full Ambisonics representation was rated above the standard Opus Channel Mapping Family 3 approach at both tested bitrates. The results indicate that coding fewer transport channels at higher precision while preserving the directional energy envelope is perceptually superior to coding all Ambisonics channels at lower precision.
items.citation: Christoph Hold, Jan Buethe, Jean-Marc Valin et al.. SEMAC: Spherical Energy Matching Ambisonics Codec for Efficient Higher-Order Ambisonics Compression. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Separating Thinking from Spelling for Efficient Generative Recommendation
items.summary: This paper addresses the computational inefficiency of generative recommender systems that retrieve items by generating semantic ID codes through trie-constrained beam search, where the cost of decoding candidates scales poorly with sequence length, beam size, and model size. The authors propose Deco, a method that separates the two main operations: a backbone language model reads user history by compressing each item into a single fused token and produces a compact "next-item concept," while a lightweight decoder conditioned on this concept handles all beam search decoding using cached key-value representations. This architectural split means the expensive backbone runs only once per user rather than repeatedly across all beam search steps, with the trie structure and autoregressive factorization remaining intact. Training combines cross-entropy with distillation from the full backbone teacher, and the lightweight decoder closely matches or exceeds the accuracy of full backbone decoding. Across multiple recommendation domains, Deco achieves comparable or superior accuracy while delivering substantially higher throughput under production latency constraints, and it can generate very large candidate pools faster than conventional systems generate much smaller ones.
items.citation: Danil Gusak, Anna Volodkevich, Ivan Oseledets et al.. Separating Thinking from Spelling for Efficient Generative Recommendation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Comprehensive Visible and Near-infrared Keck and Gemini Monitoring and Characterization of Interstellar Comet 3I/ATLAS during its Encounter with the Solar System
items.summary: This paper presents an extensive observational campaign monitoring interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS across visible and near-infrared wavelengths using multiple large ground-based telescopes, covering the object's journey through and past the inner Solar System. The study measured optical colors, dust activity, gas emission ratios, and near-infrared photometry and spectroscopy across many epochs spanning nearly a year. The comet's optical colors remained stable through perihelion, while dust activity declined more steeply after closest solar approach than before, and the spatial structure of the coma and tail evolved from a compact configuration to a more extended one over the following months. Gas emission ratios between carbon-bearing molecules changed significantly across the perihelion passage, suggesting evolving surface or sublimation conditions, and dust mass losses were estimated to correspond to erosion of roughly meter-scale surface layers. No robust detection of water-ice absorption was found in the near-infrared spectra, and the authors present these observations as a comprehensive baseline record for understanding interstellar objects and guiding study of future such visitors.
items.citation: Bryce T. Bolin, Jeffrey Cooke, Brian C. Lemaux et al.. Comprehensive Visible and Near-infrared Keck and Gemini Monitoring and Characterization of Interstellar Comet 3I/ATLAS during its Encounter with the Solar System. arXiv. 2026

items.title: RobustRLlib: A Unified Library and Benchmark for Robust Reinforcement Learning Algorithms
items.summary: This paper addresses two key barriers in robust reinforcement learning: the difficulty of reusing existing algorithms and the unclear empirical performance boundaries of current methods. The authors developed RobustRLlib, a unified open-source library that integrates a broad collection of representative robust online, offline, and safe reinforcement learning algorithms under a common interface. The benchmark evaluates these algorithms across an extensive range of perturbation configurations, including diverse real-world distributional shifts and challenging tasks involving humanoid control and vision-language-action systems. Through systematic evaluation, the work produces a capability map revealing where existing robust reinforcement learning algorithms remain effective and where significant robustness gaps persist. The platform is designed to be reproducible and extensible, lowering the barrier for both applying current methods to new problems and developing novel robust reinforcement learning approaches.
items.citation: Xi Chen, Fengqi Hu, Zeyu Shen et al.. RobustRLlib: A Unified Library and Benchmark for Robust Reinforcement Learning Algorithms. arXiv. 2026

items.title: On the continuity of conditional distributions and stratification for derivative pricing
items.summary: This paper investigates the use of neural networks to construct effective stratification factors for variance reduction in Monte Carlo pricing of path-dependent financial derivatives. Stratification reduces estimator variance by partitioning the sample space along a low-dimensional factor and sampling separately within each stratum, but identifying good factors in high-dimensional continuous-time models is challenging. The authors develop a theoretical foundation by establishing continuity results for conditional expectations and conditional distributions with respect to the stratification factor, along with counterexamples delineating the limits of this theory, and combine these with neural network density results to prove a universal approximation theorem for admissible stratification factors. Numerical experiments on a constant-maturity-swap range accrual in a two-factor Gaussian short-rate model and a worst-of autocallable in a Wishart stochastic covariance model demonstrate that the learned neural stratification factors outperform all considered benchmarks. The work thus provides both rigorous mathematical justification and practical evidence for the effectiveness of neural network-based stratification in complex derivative pricing settings.
items.citation: Aleksandar Arandjelovic, Patrick Cheridito. On the continuity of conditional distributions and stratification for derivative pricing. arXiv. 2026

items.title: DexPort: A Hand-Held Skill Interface for Dexterous Hand Data Collection
items.summary: The paper addresses the challenge of collecting high-quality demonstration data for training dexterous robotic hands, which is bottlenecked by the difficulty of teleoperation and the embodiment gap in human demonstrations. The authors introduce DexPort, a portable handheld interface that uses the same hardware as the deployment robot hand, allowing operators to specify wrist motion directly while selecting from a small set of predefined finger skills rather than controlling each joint independently. This design eliminates the need for a full robot arm setup and enables data collection in unstructured, real-world environments. Using behavior cloning, visuomotor policies were trained directly from the recorded wrist motions and hand commands across tasks including pick-and-place, screwing, drawer stowage, and bimanual scanning. The results show substantial performance gains when using recorded robot commands rather than states, and when incorporating data collected in naturalistic settings compared to laboratory-only data.
items.citation: Amber Xie, Jiawei Fu, Xiaofeng Guo et al.. DexPort: A Hand-Held Skill Interface for Dexterous Hand Data Collection. arXiv. 2026

items.title: A Rapid Molecular Detection Method for Streptococcus agalactiae Based on Bacteriophage Lysin Lysis and Real-Time PCR.
items.summary: This study developed a rapid point-of-care molecular diagnostic method for detecting Group B Streptococcus, a major cause of neonatal infections, in vaginal swab samples. The approach used a bacteriophage lysin to achieve complete bacterial cell lysis and nucleic acid extraction within five minutes, followed by real-time fluorescence quantitative PCR targeting the GBS cylA gene, bringing total turnaround time to approximately thirty-five minutes compared to the eighteen to forty-eight hours required by conventional culture. Specific primers and probes were designed with no observed cross-reactivity, and the assay was validated across two clinical cohorts totaling over five hundred vaginal swab samples. The method demonstrated perfect sensitivity in both cohorts and high specificity that improved further after sequencing-based resolution of discordant samples, and it substantially outperformed antigen testing in sensitivity. The authors conclude that this bacteriophage lysin-based assay shows strong diagnostic performance and holds promise for intrapartum or near-patient GBS screening, pending further validation in real-world clinical workflows.
items.venue: European journal of clinical microbiology & infectious diseases : official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology
items.citation: Zhu H, Zeng X, Huang X et al.. A Rapid Molecular Detection Method for Streptococcus agalactiae Based on Bacteriophage Lysin Lysis and Real-Time PCR.. European journal of clinical microbiology & infectious diseases : official publication of the European Society of Clinical Microbiology. 2026

items.title: Temporal trends in pediatric group A streptococcal pharyngitis across the coronavirus disease 2019 era: A large retrospective cohort study.
items.summary: This study examined how the COVID-19 pandemic and its associated public health measures affected rates of Group A Streptococcus pharyngitis in children over time. Researchers conducted a large retrospective cohort study of pediatric patients presenting with suspected acute tonsillopharyngitis at a tertiary outpatient clinic, comparing positivity rates across pre-pandemic, pandemic, and post-pandemic periods spanning from late 2018 through late 2025. Group A Streptococcus positivity increased progressively across all three periods, rising from the pre-pandemic era through the pandemic and reaching its highest level in the post-pandemic period, with older age and male sex also independently associated with positivity. The authors suggest these trends likely reflect a combination of factors including changes in healthcare utilization, diagnostic practices, age distribution, and transmission dynamics rather than any single cause. They conclude that ongoing epidemiological surveillance is necessary to better understand the evolving burden of pediatric Group A Streptococcus pharyngitis.
items.venue: The Journal of international medical research
items.citation: Nas Y, Gözüküçük S, Bayırlı H et al.. Temporal trends in pediatric group A streptococcal pharyngitis across the coronavirus disease 2019 era: A large retrospective cohort study.. The Journal of international medical research. 2026

items.title: Rapid molecular culture versus conventional culture for periprosthetic joint infection: diagnostic performance and clinical relevance.
items.summary: This study evaluated a rapid PCR-based assay called Molecular Culture as a diagnostic tool for periprosthetic joint infection, comparing it against conventional culture of sonication fluid obtained during revision hip and knee arthroplasty. Samples from patients undergoing revision surgery over a multi-year period were retrospectively analysed, with infection status classified according to established European criteria, and diagnostic agreement was assessed both analytically and after clinical correlation. The rapid assay delivered results within approximately four hours, compared to the prolonged turnaround of conventional culture, and after clinical correlation demonstrated high negative percentage agreement, suggesting strong performance in ruling out infection. Molecular Culture also identified additional clinically relevant pathogens not detected by conventional culture, particularly benefiting patients who had received prior antibiotic therapy, which is known to reduce culture sensitivity. The authors conclude that the assay performs best as an adjunctive rather than standalone diagnostic tool, with its greatest utility in cases of diagnostic uncertainty or prior antimicrobial exposure where rapid pathogen exclusion could guide earlier treatment optimisation.
items.venue: Journal of bone and joint infection
items.citation: Morreel E, Savelkoul P, van Loo I. Rapid molecular culture versus conventional culture for periprosthetic joint infection: diagnostic performance and clinical relevance.. Journal of bone and joint infection. 2026

items.title: Diagnosing Sepsis and Identifying Bacterial Resistance Genes Directly from Whole Blood Using a Rapid Real-Time PCR System.
items.summary: This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of a rapid real-time PCR approach capable of detecting multiple pathogens and antimicrobial resistance genes directly from whole blood within four hours in adult patients with sepsis. Whole-blood samples were tested in parallel using both the rapid PCR panel and conventional automated blood culture systems, allowing direct comparison of the two methods. The most commonly identified organisms by blood culture included Staphylococcus aureus, Klebsiella pneumoniae, and Escherichia coli, while resistance genes such as mecA, OXA-48, and CTX-M were among those detected by the PCR panel. Agreement between the two diagnostic approaches was statistically significant, and the PCR method demonstrated high specificity alongside moderate sensitivity. The authors conclude that the ability to identify causative pathogens and resistance genes within four hours offers a meaningful clinical advantage by enabling earlier targeted therapy, potentially preventing progression to septic shock and reducing mortality.
items.citation: Begmyradova S, Öksüz L, Aktas Z et al.. Diagnosing Sepsis and Identifying Bacterial Resistance Genes Directly from Whole Blood Using a Rapid Real-Time PCR System.. International journal of molecular sciences. 2026
