items.title: Advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarkers, 2020-26: scientific evidence, recommendations, gaps, and developmental priorities.
items.summary: This paper reviews advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarker research from 2020 to 2025, synthesizing the evidence base that has informed updated WHO policy guidance consolidating recommendations for detecting tuberculosis disease and drug resistance. The review covers a broad range of diagnostic tools and specimen types, including digital chest radiography with computer-aided detection, decentralised molecular platforms such as low-complexity automated and manual nucleic acid amplification tests, near point-of-care molecular diagnostics, and expanded use of non-sputum specimens to improve diagnosis in children and other sputum-scarce populations. Advances in rapid molecular drug-resistance testing and the endorsement of targeted next-generation sequencing for comprehensive drug-susceptibility testing at reference laboratory level are also highlighted, alongside urine lipoarabinomannan assays for people with HIV. The review finds that host blood transcriptomic signatures show promise for triage and short-term prognosis, and that proteomic, metabolomic, cellular, and pathogen-derived biomarkers are progressing through evaluation, yet no biomarker has met WHO target product profile criteria for a point-of-care test capable of reliably distinguishing infection from disease, including subclinical tuberculosis. Substantial gaps in diagnostic performance, implementation, and health equity are identified as persistent priorities for further development.
items.citation: Walzl G, McHugh TD, Chakaya J et al.. Advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarkers, 2020-26: scientific evidence, recommendations, gaps, and developmental priorities.. The Lancet. Microbe. 2027

items.title: Molecular point-of-care: technological evolution, clinical applications, and future perspectives
items.citation: Zhang D, Cui X, Zhang R et al.. Molecular point-of-care: technological evolution, clinical applications, and future perspectives. Frontiers in bioengineering and biotechnology. 2026

items.title: Finger-actuated microfluidic device for point-of-care circulating cell-free nucleic acid extraction.
items.summary: This paper developed and evaluated a fully finger-actuated microfluidic device designed to extract cell-free nucleic acids from plasma without requiring laboratory instruments or power. The device integrates manual valves, a finger-driven pump, and on-board blister packs containing all necessary reagents, enabling a complete sample-to-eluate workflow through lysis, binding, washing, and elution steps performed by hand. Performance was benchmarked against both a commercial benchtop magnetic bead extraction method and an automated robotic workflow using DNA-spiked aqueous samples and human pooled plasma, with the device achieving recovery rates comparable to or exceeding the benchtop approach depending on input sample volume. Clinical utility was demonstrated using patient samples positive for three different viruses, where the device produced quantitative PCR results closely matching those from standard protocols. The authors propose this instrument-free tool as a scalable solution to bridge the gap between existing nucleic acid amplification technologies and decentralised diagnostics in resource-limited settings.
items.citation: Musaddaq G, Ehsan L, Yoga Y et al.. Finger-actuated microfluidic device for point-of-care circulating cell-free nucleic acid extraction.. Lab on a chip. 2026

items.title: Molecular Diagnostics of Infectious Diseases.
items.summary: This review paper examines the current state and development of molecular diagnostic methods for detecting and characterizing pathogens responsible for infectious diseases. The paper covers nucleic acid amplification technologies, including polymerase chain reaction variants optimized for speed, quantification, automation, and point-of-care use, as well as isothermal amplification methods that operate without thermal cycling equipment. It also addresses CRISPR-based detection systems, which are frequently combined with isothermal amplification to identify amplified nucleic acids at constant temperatures. Next-generation sequencing is highlighted for its capacity to detect novel pathogens, diagnose complex infections, trace outbreak transmission routes, monitor pathogen evolution, and analyze microbiomes as potential disease biomarkers. The authors conclude that future advances in infectious disease molecular diagnostics will come from addressing current limitations and integrating these diverse technologies into hybrid platforms.
items.citation: Takata M, Chikumi H, Yoshifuji A. Molecular Diagnostics of Infectious Diseases.. Yonago acta medica. 2026

items.title: QMini: A Portable Device for Infectious Disease Testing.
items.summary: The paper studied the development of a portable device for nucleic acid-based infectious disease testing, aiming to address the limitation that conventional testing equipment is too large for field deployment. The researchers designed the QMini by simplifying its fluidic module through direct pump-to-reaction-chamber connections and shielding its optical module from ambient light using a three-dimensional-printed enclosure. They tested the device's ability to detect synthetic nucleic acid sequences from respiratory syncytial virus B, SARS-CoV-2, and influenza A using a bead-based assay with quantum dot barcodes. The device successfully detected low copy numbers of all three viral targets while showing limited cross-reactivity against non-target viral sequences. The authors conclude that the QMini advances the portability of quantum dot barcode-based nucleic acid testing through miniaturization.
items.citation: Mahbub N, Osborne M, Chen H et al.. QMini: A Portable Device for Infectious Disease Testing.. ACS nanoscience Au. 2026

items.title: Molecular Detection of Feline Hemotropic <i>Mycoplasma</i> from Blood Samples of Sick Cats: A Comparative Study Between a Commercial Nucleic Acid Test Card and Conventional Polymerase Chain Reaction.
items.summary: This study evaluated a commercial rapid nucleic acid test card for detecting feline hemotropic *Mycoplasma* species in clinically ill cats, comparing it against conventional polymerase chain reaction targeting the 16S rRNA gene as the reference standard. Blood samples from sick cats presenting to a veterinary teaching hospital in Thailand were analyzed, and conventional PCR identified *'Candidatus* Mycoplasma haemominutum' as the most prevalent species, with *Mycoplasma haemofelis* and *'Candidatus* Mycoplasma turicensis'* detected at lower frequencies. The commercial nucleic acid test card demonstrated high sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, and precision relative to conventional PCR, with results available within thirty minutes. False-negative results from the rapid assay were confirmed by sequence analysis to contain the predominant species, likely reflecting low bacterial burdens or other technical factors. The authors conclude that the commercial test card represents a practical and accurate point-of-care molecular tool to support rapid clinical decision-making in cats with suspected hemotropic mycoplasmosis.
items.citation: Nimsuphan B, Ruenphet S, Kengradomkij C et al.. Molecular Detection of Feline Hemotropic <i>Mycoplasma</i> from Blood Samples of Sick Cats: A Comparative Study Between a Commercial Nucleic Acid Test Card and Conventional Polymerase Chain Reaction.. Veterinary sciences. 2026

items.title: Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications
items.summary: This review examines how the integration of multiomics technologies and artificial intelligence is reshaping precision drug discovery and translational medicine. The authors synthesize how approaches spanning genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics generate deep insights into disease mechanisms, and how deep learning architectures can extract meaningful patterns from these complex, high-dimensional biological datasets. The review covers the application of this combined framework across the full drug development pipeline, including target identification, drug repositioning, de novo compound discovery, virtual screening, pharmacokinetic modeling, and safety assessment. Case studies in oncology, neurodegenerative diseases, and cardiovascular conditions are used to illustrate the practical potential of these convergent technologies. The authors also highlight persistent challenges such as harmonizing disparate omics data, ensuring reproducibility, and addressing algorithmic bias, while arguing that the fusion of multiomics and artificial intelligence opens transformative new avenues for therapeutic innovation and bench-to-clinic translation.
items.citation: Yuqing Liu, Kun Zhu, Weijun Peng et al.. Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: Loss-of-function mutation in Omicron variants reduces spike protein expression and attenuates SARS-CoV-2 infection
items.citation: Michelle N. Vu, R. Elias Alvarado, Dorothea R. Morris et al.. Loss-of-function mutation in Omicron variants reduces spike protein expression and attenuates SARS-CoV-2 infection. Nature Communications. 2026

items.title: mRNA vaccine immunity is enhanced by hepatocyte detargeting and not dependent on dendritic cell expression
items.summary: This study investigated how cell-type-specific expression of mRNA vaccine-encoded proteins influences immune responses, addressing a gap in understanding given that lipid nanoparticle-delivered mRNA can transfect diverse cell types. Researchers used synthetic microRNA target sites incorporated into mRNA vaccines to selectively silence expression in professional antigen-presenting cells, hepatocytes, or myocytes. They found that direct mRNA expression in professional antigen-presenting cells was dispensable for priming antigen-specific T cells, while myocyte expression drove similar or stronger immune responses, implicating antigen cross-presentation or cross-dressing as key mechanisms. Hepatocyte expression, however, suppressed antigen-specific T cell responses partly through the PD1/PDL1 pathway, and silencing hepatocyte expression enhanced immune responses and reduced tumor burden in a lymphoma model. These findings demonstrate that non-antigen-presenting cell expression critically shapes mRNA vaccine immunogenicity, and that incorporating microRNA target sites to detarget hepatocytes represents a strategy to boost vaccine efficacy.
items.citation: Adam R. Marks, Sophia Siu, Filippo Bianchini et al.. mRNA vaccine immunity is enhanced by hepatocyte detargeting and not dependent on dendritic cell expression. Nature Biotechnology. 2026

items.title: Regulatory Challenges and Opportunities for Cell‐Derived Extracellular Vesicles in Pharmaceutical Development: A European and Global Perspective
items.summary: This paper examined the regulatory landscape governing cell-derived extracellular vesicles as therapeutic and diagnostic products, with particular attention to how their acellular nature creates classification difficulties under existing medicinal product frameworks. The authors conducted a critical review of current and emerging regulatory approaches across major jurisdictions, finding that different agencies apply divergent classification criteria, creating heterogeneity that complicates regulatory positioning, quality assessment, and cross-regional clinical development. A key development highlighted is a recent European guidance clarifying that minimally modified extracellular vesicles fall outside the advanced therapy medicinal products definition, contrasting with the approach of other regulators who treat such products as drugs or biologics subject to premarket requirements. The authors argue that extracellular vesicle products should be developed within existing medicinal product frameworks provided regulatory tools are applied consistently, and they identify specific operational grey zones—including classification criteria, critical quality attributes, potency strategies, and comparability—that require clarification. The review is intended to support regulatory dialogue among international agencies and scientific societies to advance extracellular vesicle therapies toward safe and internationally credible clinical use.
items.citation: Tania Limongi, Paola Milla, Barbara Stella et al.. Regulatory Challenges and Opportunities for Cell‐Derived Extracellular Vesicles in Pharmaceutical Development: A European and Global Perspective. Journal of Extracellular Vesicles. 2026

items.title: Dairy cows infected with influenza A(H5N1) reveals low infectious dose and transmission barriers
items.citation: Carolyn M. Lee, Natalie N. Tarbuck, Hannah J. Cochran et al.. Dairy cows infected with influenza A(H5N1) reveals low infectious dose and transmission barriers. Nature Communications. 2026

items.title: Evolutionary characterization of lung cancer metastasis
items.summary: This study investigated how non-small cell lung cancer evolves from initial diagnosis through metastatic spread to death, using extensively sampled primary and metastatic tumour tissue collected longitudinally from patients enrolled in two complementary clinical programmes. By applying DNA sequencing across a large collection of primary and metastatic samples that accounted for the majority of radiologically detectable metastases, the researchers reconstructed detailed evolutionary histories of tumour dissemination. They found that metastatic genomes diverge substantially from their primary tumour ancestors, acquiring additional driver alterations and genome doubling events after leaving the primary site, and that in most patients multiple distinct subclones from the primary tumour independently seeded separate metastases. Critically, more than half of metastases were themselves seeded by other metastases rather than directly by the primary tumour, and the time a metastasis had existed influenced its propensity for onward spread, with most metastatic migration remaining within the same anatomical cavity. Subclones that spread beyond the thorax were enriched for somatic copy-number alterations, implicating chromosomal instability as a potential facilitator of extrathoracic dissemination and highlighting that single metastasis biopsies substantially underestimate the genomic diversity present in advanced disease.
items.citation: Sonya Hessey, Abigail Bunkum, Ariana Huebner et al.. Evolutionary characterization of lung cancer metastasis. Nature. 2026

items.title: SEMAC: Spherical Energy Matching Ambisonics Codec for Efficient Higher-Order Ambisonics Compression
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of efficiently compressing Higher-Order Ambisonics audio, a spatial audio format whose channel count grows quadratically with spherical harmonic order, making it costly to transmit at high fidelity. The authors introduce SEMAC, a codec that represents an Ambisonics signal using a quantized directional energy envelope computed at full order combined with a reduced set of lower-dimensional transport channels coded with the CELT algorithm, generalizing CELT's per-band energy separation principle to the spatial domain. At the decoder, the full-order directional energy distribution is restored by re-imposing the envelope captured at the encoder, compensating for the information lost by reducing the number of transport channels. Perceptual evaluation using a MUSHRA listening test on fifth-order Ambisonics material showed that SEMAC using roughly half the transport channels of a full-order representation was rated above the standard Opus Channel Mapping Family approach at matched bitrates, and outperformed simple order truncation when the number of transport channels was equalized. The results indicate that coding fewer channels at higher precision while preserving the directional energy envelope is perceptually superior to coding all Ambisonics channels at lower precision.
items.citation: Christoph Hold, Jan Buethe, Jean-Marc Valin et al.. SEMAC: Spherical Energy Matching Ambisonics Codec for Efficient Higher-Order Ambisonics Compression. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Comprehensive Visible and Near-infrared Keck and Gemini Monitoring and Characterization of Interstellar Comet 3I/ATLAS during its Encounter with the Solar System
items.summary: This paper presents an extensive multi-wavelength observational campaign of the interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS using large ground-based telescopes, covering both optical and near-infrared imaging and spectroscopy across nearly a year spanning its perihelion passage. The study tracked the comet's dust activity, color evolution, and gas composition as it traversed the inner Solar System. The comet's optical colors remained stable through perihelion, while dust activity declined more steeply after closest approach to the Sun than before, and estimated dust mass losses imply the erosion of meter-scale surface layers under plausible grain and nucleus assumptions. Gas emission ratios evolved over time, with the relative abundance of certain carbon-bearing species shifting noticeably across the observing window, and near-infrared spectroscopy revealed no robust evidence for water-ice absorption features. The authors present these observations as a comprehensive reference dataset for understanding 3I/ATLAS's physical and compositional properties and as a benchmark for studying future interstellar visitors to the Solar System.
items.citation: Bryce T. Bolin, Jeffrey Cooke, Brian C. Lemaux et al.. Comprehensive Visible and Near-infrared Keck and Gemini Monitoring and Characterization of Interstellar Comet 3I/ATLAS during its Encounter with the Solar System. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Shared clones make random cell halves look reproducible in pooled screens
items.summary: Pooled single-cell perturbation screens such as Perturb-seq are widely used to train and evaluate models that predict how genetic perturbations affect gene expression, with model performance judged by how reproducibly perturbation effects are measured. The standard practice of splitting a perturbation's cells into two random halves to assess reproducibility assumes those halves are independent, but because cells sharing a guide RNA descend from a limited number of transduced ancestors, both halves contain the same clonal lineages, creating pseudoreplication. Using null perturbations as controls, the authors compared random half-splits against truly independent replicates from separate transductions and against half-splits designed to exclude shared clones, finding that random halves showed near-perfect agreement for null perturbations while independent replicates agreed only at the rate expected from noise. The degree of inflation from shared clones varied across screens by orders of magnitude, being largest in primary T cells and smallest in non-dividing neurons, and was largely eliminated by splitting cells according to clone-distinguishing features such as T-cell receptor constant region or clone barcodes. Critically, published models that predict perturbation effects in new cell states appeared to outperform a perturbation-agnostic baseline when evaluated within a single transduction, but fell below that baseline when evaluated against cells from an independent transduction, demonstrating that reproducibility in pooled screens must be assessed across separate transductions to avoid inflated benchmarks.
items.citation: Xuanrui Huang. Shared clones make random cell halves look reproducible in pooled screens. arXiv. 2026

items.title: CoupleFlow: Null-Calibrated Auditory Attention Decoding With Time-Locked Brain-Speech Coupling and Flow-Matching Likelihood Ratios
items.summary: This paper addresses auditory attention decoding, the problem of identifying which talker a listener is attending to based on brief noninvasive brain recordings, and demonstrates that previously reported near-perfect accuracy from existing electroencephalography decoders does not generalize because those models exploit data leakage, eye gaze, and acoustic artifacts rather than genuine neural responses to speech. The authors introduce CoupleFlow, a method that decodes attention by measuring temporal coupling between neural and acoustic embeddings using a conditional flow matching head that implements a likelihood ratio decision rule based on pointwise mutual information, ensuring predictions remain at chance when no informative brain-speech coupling is present. To rigorously evaluate generalization, the authors developed content-disjoint evaluation splits and null tests that distinguish genuine temporal coupling from incidental trial recognition, applying these across nine electroencephalography and magnetoencephalography datasets spanning multiple languages, recording modalities, listener populations, and acoustic environments. CoupleFlow outperformed both linear and deep learning baselines across all datasets while consistently passing the null tests. Additionally, the authors derived an evidence accumulation law that predicts decoding accuracy across window lengths from a single dataset-specific parameter tied to the strength of neural speech tracking, identifying recording signal-to-noise ratio as the fundamental bottleneck on decoding speed and reliability.
items.citation: Ali Alavi, Donald S. Williamson. CoupleFlow: Null-Calibrated Auditory Attention Decoding With Time-Locked Brain-Speech Coupling and Flow-Matching Likelihood Ratios. arXiv. 2026

items.title: If at First You Don't Succeed, Backtrack: Lightweight Recovery for Frozen VLAs
items.summary: This paper addresses the brittleness of Vision-Language-Action models in robotic manipulation, specifically their tendency to fail when their own actions push them into states underrepresented in training data. The authors propose Backtrack, a lightweight mechanism that attaches a small failure prediction head to a frozen VLA, trained solely on outcome-labeled rollouts without requiring recovery demonstrations, policy retraining, or auxiliary models at inference time. The failure prediction head reads the VLA's existing internal representations to estimate the probability of episode failure, and when this probability exceeds a threshold, a controller pauses the policy, physically retraces the robot arm's recent motion, and restores control to the original policy for a retry from an earlier configuration. Evaluated across multiple VLA architectures spanning both flow-matching and autoregressive action generation on the LIBERO and MetaWorld benchmarks, Backtrack consistently reduces failure rates, with the largest gains observed on long-horizon multi-step tasks where base policies fail most frequently. The method achieves meaningful improvements while adding only a negligible fraction of additional parameters to the original policy.
items.citation: Thomas Landeg, Thierry Tambe. If at First You Don't Succeed, Backtrack: Lightweight Recovery for Frozen VLAs. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Certain Quantum States Already Require Quantum Time Evolution
items.summary: The paper investigates whether the dynamical laws of quantum mechanics can be tested in a model-independent way, analogous to how Bell inequality violations test static properties of the theory. The authors work within a class of generalized phase-space theories and examine the consistency between allowed quantum states and possible dynamical evolution laws. They find that certain quantum states are incompatible with non-quantum time evolution, because evolving them under anharmonic potentials using alternative dynamical brackets would produce unphysical negative marginal distributions. Notably, the existence of the first excited state of the harmonic oscillator alone is shown to be sufficient to single out the Moyal bracket — the standard quantum dynamical structure — to leading order in the semiclassical expansion. The authors propose that theory-independent Wigner tomography of such states could provide an empirical means to exclude non-quantum dynamical theories.
items.citation: Joel D. Huber, Matthias Kleinmann. Certain Quantum States Already Require Quantum Time Evolution. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic yield of reflex multiplex PCR after a negative rapid antigen test in children hospitalized with presumed viral acute respiratory tract infection: a prospective cohort study.
items.summary: This study investigated whether adding reflex multiplex PCR testing after a negative rapid antigen test improves the identification of respiratory viruses in children hospitalized with presumed viral acute respiratory infections. In a prospective single-center cohort, children first underwent a five-target rapid antigen test, and those who tested negative could then receive multiplex PCR at the physician's discretion. The study found that antigen testing alone identified less than a quarter of children with a detectable virus, while reflex PCR substantially increased diagnostic yield, with the large majority of antigen-negative children who underwent PCR testing positive for a respiratory virus. Rhinovirus/enterovirus, which is not covered by standard antigen panels, was the most commonly identified pathogen overall. Antibiotic use was high across the cohort regardless of whether a virus was detected, and the appropriateness of this prescribing could not be assessed because systematic bacterial testing was not performed.
items.citation: Bedir AZ, Saf C, Yörük MA. Diagnostic yield of reflex multiplex PCR after a negative rapid antigen test in children hospitalized with presumed viral acute respiratory tract infection: a prospective cohort study.. Irish journal of medical science. 2026

items.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of the RapidFor™ RSV/ADV Rapid Test Kit Compared with PCR for the Detection of Respiratory Syncytial Virus and Adenovirus in Nasopharyngeal Swab Samples
items.summary: This study evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of a dual rapid antigen test kit for simultaneously detecting respiratory syncytial virus and adenovirus in children presenting to a pediatric emergency department with acute respiratory symptoms. Using multiplex real-time PCR as the reference standard, researchers prospectively enrolled children up to eighteen years of age and compared point-of-care rapid test results against PCR findings from paired nasopharyngeal swabs. The rapid test demonstrated very high sensitivity, specificity, and predictive values for both pathogens, with excellent agreement with PCR for each. Age-stratified analysis revealed that RSV positivity was most common in infants under one year, while adenovirus peaked in school-aged children, and distinct clinical predictors were identified for each pathogen. The authors conclude that this rapid test offers diagnostic performance comparable to PCR and may support timely clinical decision-making in pediatric emergency settings.

items.title: Respiratory multi-viral rapid-antigen point-of-care tests in New Zealand primary care: a mixed-methods pilot.
items.summary: This study piloted the integration of multi-viral rapid-antigen point-of-care tests into routine primary care settings in New Zealand to assess their feasibility, acceptability, and clinical utility for diagnosing acute respiratory infections. A prospective mixed-methods design was used across seven primary care clinics during winter, combining electronic medical record audits with clinician and patient surveys, interviews, and focus groups. Patients presenting with acute respiratory symptoms received a multi-viral test rather than a COVID-19-only test, enabling detection of a broader range of respiratory viruses. The tests were well-received by both clinicians and patients, with the majority of prescribers reporting that results influenced their antibiotic prescribing decisions and supported secondary care referral choices. The authors conclude that routine integration of these tests into primary care could improve management of common respiratory illnesses and encourage patient behaviour change to reduce disease transmission.
items.citation: Bibby S, Marsh S, Dowell A et al.. Respiratory multi-viral rapid-antigen point-of-care tests in New Zealand primary care: a mixed-methods pilot.. BJGP open. 2026

items.title: Can exercise affect immune function to increase susceptibility to infection?
items.summary: This debate article examined the long-standing question in exercise immunology of whether exercise itself can suppress immune function and increase susceptibility to infection. The authors structured opposing arguments around four contested issues: whether athletes are more infection-prone than the general population, whether exercise independently alters immunity beyond confounding factors such as sleep disruption, nutritional deficits, and travel, whether specific biomarkers and in vitro data adequately reflect immune health in those performing arduous exercise, and whether the existing scientific evidence is sufficiently robust to support claims about exercise-induced immunosuppression. While regular moderate-intensity exercise of relatively short duration is broadly accepted as beneficial for immune defense, particularly in older adults and those with chronic disease, the picture is more complex for high-performance athletes and military personnel who engage in prolonged, intense physical activity and experience elevated infection burdens. Both debating groups agreed that infection susceptibility is multifactorial in nature, but disagreed on whether exercise per se constitutes an independent causative factor in elevated infection risk. The article concludes that the question remains unresolved and calls for more rigorous empirical research to disentangle the specific contribution of exercise from the many co-occurring stressors in these populations.
items.citation: Richard J. Simpson, Richard J. Simpson, Maree Gleeson et al.. Can exercise affect immune function to increase susceptibility to infection?. PubMed. 2026

items.title: Spinal cord injury: Known and possible influences on the immune response to exercise
items.summary: This review paper examined how spinal cord injury affects immune function, with particular focus on the immune response to exercise. The authors conducted a comprehensive literature search to gather existing evidence from studies involving individuals with spinal cord injury across patient, recreationally active, and athlete populations, grounding their analysis in the anatomical and physiological relationships between neural, neuroendocrine, and immune systems. A central finding is that loss of autonomic function following spinal cord injury, especially in tetraplegia, alters catecholamine concentrations and likely depresses immunity through effects on adrenergic receptors expressed on lymphoid cells, while other factors such as altered muscular, endocrine, and cardiovascular function further contribute to immune disruption. However, the review also highlights that certain immune responses to exercise, including natural killer cell cytotoxicity and mucosal immunity, appear preserved or unrelated to catecholamine changes in individuals with tetraplegia, suggesting compensatory mechanisms such as sympathetic reflex activity, receptor hypersensitivity, or parasympathetic and neuroendocrine adjustments may offset some immune deficits. The authors conclude that exercise and rehabilitation can improve some measures of immunity and autonomic function in this population, and that better understanding these mechanisms could help develop strategies to maintain or improve health following spinal cord injury.
items.citation: Christof A. Leicht, Victoria Louise Goosey-Tolfrey, NICOLETTE CLAIRE BISHOP. Spinal cord injury: Known and possible influences on the immune response to exercise. PubMed. 2026

items.title: Understanding graft-versus-host disease. Preliminary findings regarding the effects of exercise in affected patients
items.summary: This paper examined graft-versus-host disease, a serious multi-systemic complication arising from allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation in which donor lymphocytes attack host tissues, with particular focus on its chronic form and its impact on patients' physical capacity. The authors reviewed the pathophysiological mechanisms underlying the disease alongside available evidence from both animal and human studies on the potential role of exercise as an adjunct therapy. Their review suggests that exercise training holds promise for improving physical fitness, potentially enhancing immune function, and reducing fatigue in patients who have undergone transplantation. However, the authors conclude that the evidence base remains insufficient and that more randomized controlled trials specifically targeting patients with graft-versus-host disease are needed before firm recommendations can be made.
items.citation: Carmen Fiuza‐Luces, Nuria Garatachea, Nathan A. Berger et al.. Understanding graft-versus-host disease. Preliminary findings regarding the effects of exercise in affected patients. PubMed. 2026

items.title: EHA Guidelines on management of chronic lymphocytic leukemia and Richter transformation
items.summary: These guidelines address the clinical management of chronic lymphocytic leukemia and, for the first time explicitly, Richter transformation, representing an updated European framework for care of patients with these conditions. Developed under the European Hematology Association rather than its previous institutional home, the guidelines were produced through expert consensus spanning multiple European countries and, for the first time, incorporated patient advocacy representatives in their development. The recommendations advocate a holistic approach to disease management, from initial diagnosis and active surveillance through treatment decisions informed by both disease- and patient-specific factors. Notable treatment updates include newly approved time-limited combination therapy with acalabrutinib and venetoclax with or without obinutuzumab as a first-line option, as well as continuous pirtobrutinib for patients with relapsed or refractory disease who have been previously exposed to covalent Bruton's tyrosine kinase inhibitors. The guidelines are intended to be updated annually to keep pace with the rapidly evolving landscape of research and clinical applications in this field.
items.citation: Barbara F. Eichhorst, Paolo Ghia, Francesc Bosch et al.. EHA Guidelines on management of chronic lymphocytic leukemia and Richter transformation. HemaSphere. 2026

items.title: The neuroimmune axis in breast cancer: from mechanistic insights to clinical applications
items.summary: This review examines the neuroimmune axis as a critical but underappreciated regulator of breast cancer progression and treatment resistance. The authors synthesize evidence showing that bidirectional crosstalk between the nervous and immune systems, mediated by neurotransmitters, neuropeptides, and neurotrophins, shapes key tumor behaviors including proliferation, epithelial-mesenchymal transition, angiogenesis, and metastasis, while immune-derived cytokines reciprocally remodel neural circuits to sustain a pro-tumor microenvironment. The review outlines emerging therapeutic strategies that exploit this axis, including repurposing neuroactive drugs, targeted drug delivery systems, combining neural stimulation with immune checkpoint blockade, and microbiota-neuroimmune interventions. The authors also highlight major obstacles to clinical translation, such as spatiotemporal heterogeneity of neuroimmune regulation, narrow therapeutic windows of neuropharmacological agents, and the absence of standardized biomarkers. They conclude that deeper mechanistic understanding of the neuroimmune axis could underpin precision therapeutic approaches, particularly for difficult-to-treat subtypes such as triple-negative breast cancer.
items.citation: Yimao Wu, Kaiyu Zhang, Xinya Xia et al.. The neuroimmune axis in breast cancer: from mechanistic insights to clinical applications. BMC Medicine. 2026

items.summary: This paper presents an extensive observational campaign monitoring interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS across both visible and near-infrared wavelengths during its passage through the Solar System, using multiple instruments on the Keck and Gemini telescopes. items.title: Pulmonary Tuberculosis Detection with MiniDock MTB Using Swab Samples
items.summary: The study evaluated the diagnostic accuracy and usability of MiniDock MTB, a novel test intended for near-point-of-care detection of pulmonary tuberculosis using swab-based sampling rather than conventional processed sputum. Researchers conducted a prospective, cross-sectional study across multiple countries in Africa and Asia, enrolling adults and adolescents with presumptive pulmonary tuberculosis and assessing the test using both sputum swabs and tongue swabs against a sputum-culture reference standard. MiniDock MTB achieved sensitivity exceeding eighty-five percent with sputum swabs and nearly eighty percent with tongue swabs, with specificity above ninety-seven percent for both sample types, performance that closely matched the Xpert MTB/RIF Ultra assay and substantially exceeded sputum-smear microscopy. The test met World Health Organization accuracy targets for near-point-of-care tuberculosis diagnostics across both sputum and nonsputum sample types, and usability assessments indicated it was perceived as a good-quality tool by users at peripheral health facilities. The authors conclude that MiniDock MTB represents a promising diagnostic option suitable for deployment in diverse clinical settings where conventional laboratory infrastructure is limited.
items.citation: Seda Yerlikaya, Masuzyo Chirwa, Bukola Ajide et al.. Pulmonary Tuberculosis Detection with MiniDock MTB Using Swab Samples. New England Journal of Medicine. 2026

items.title: Advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarkers, 2020-26: scientific evidence, recommendations, gaps, and developmental priorities.
items.summary: This paper reviews advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarker research from 2020 to 2025, summarizing how new scientific evidence has informed updated WHO policy recommendations that consolidate guidance on disease detection and drug-resistance testing into a single framework. Key developments include the expanded role of digital chest radiography with computer-aided detection as a screening and triage tool, and the broadened deployment of rapid molecular diagnostics—particularly low-complexity automated and manual nucleic acid amplification tests—across decentralised settings and diverse specimen types including stool, gastric aspirate, nasopharyngeal samples, and tongue swabs. Drug-resistance testing has been strengthened through new molecular platforms and the WHO endorsement of targeted next-generation sequencing for comprehensive susceptibility profiling at reference laboratories, while urine lipoarabinomannan assays offer incremental benefit in people with HIV and advanced disease despite performance limitations. Host blood transcriptomic and other biomarkers show promise for prognosis and triage but none yet meets WHO target product profile criteria for a point-of-care test capable of reliably distinguishing infection from disease, including subclinical tuberculosis. The paper concludes that significant gaps in diagnostic performance, implementation, and equity remain, and identifies these as priorities for further development.
items.citation: Walzl G, McHugh TD, Chakaya J et al.. Advances in tuberculosis diagnostics and biomarkers, 2020-26: scientific evidence, recommendations, gaps, and developmental priorities.. The Lancet. Microbe. 2027

items.title: Concordance Between Fingerprick and Venous Whole Blood CD4 Counts Using the Visitect CD4 Advanced Disease Platform.
items.summary: The study evaluated whether fingerprick blood sampling could reliably substitute for venous whole blood collection when using the Visitect CD4 Advanced Disease platform, a rapid semi-quantitative assay that classifies CD4 counts as above or below a clinically important threshold. The researchers conducted a prospective validation study directly comparing results obtained from fingerprick samples against those from venous whole blood using the same platform. They found a very high level of agreement between the two sampling methods, supporting the potential use of fingerprick collection as a reliable point-of-care approach in resource-limited settings where conventional venous blood draw may not be feasible.
items.citation: Adzemovic T, Nalintya E, Onencan P et al.. Concordance Between Fingerprick and Venous Whole Blood CD4 Counts Using the Visitect CD4 Advanced Disease Platform.. The Journal of infectious diseases. 2026

items.title: Molecular point-of-care: technological evolution, clinical applications, and future perspectives.
items.summary: This review examines the technological development and clinical utility of molecular point-of-care testing platforms as diagnostics shift away from centralized laboratory models. The authors surveyed isothermal nucleic acid amplification approaches, including loop-mediated isothermal amplification, recombinase polymerase amplification, and rolling circle amplification, alongside CRISPR/Cas-based detection systems integrated with microfluidic chips and smartphone-based digital readouts to achieve automated sample-to-answer workflows. They mapped the clinical applications of these platforms across infectious disease management, cancer screening, cardiovascular triage, and metabolic disease monitoring. Despite substantial advances, the review identifies persistent barriers to widespread adoption, including multiplexed detection interference, enzyme instability outside cold-chain conditions, component costs, and absent regulatory frameworks tailored to these technologies. The authors argue that convergence of synthetic biology, system integration, and artificial intelligence will be necessary to translate molecular point-of-care diagnostics into accessible, precise tools for resource-limited settings.
items.citation: Zhang D, Cui X, Zhang R et al.. Molecular point-of-care: technological evolution, clinical applications, and future perspectives.. Frontiers in bioengineering and biotechnology. 2026

items.title: Next-generation CRISPR-based molecular diagnostics for veterinary parasitology: From laboratory innovation to one health surveillance.
items.summary: This review examines the application of CRISPR-based diagnostic technologies to the detection of veterinary parasites, encompassing protozoan, helminthic, and arthropod-borne organisms affecting livestock, companion animals, and wildlife. The authors synthesize current knowledge on how CRISPR systems utilizing Cas12, Cas13, and emerging Cas14 effectors can be combined with isothermal amplification, lateral flow assays, fluorescence detection, and portable biosensors to create rapid, sensitive, and field-deployable diagnostic platforms. The review critically compares these approaches against conventional methods such as microscopy, serology, and culture, which are often limited by poor sensitivity, slow turnaround, and reliance on centralized laboratory infrastructure. The authors identify key barriers to broader implementation, including challenges in sample preparation, assay standardization, multiplex detection, and regulatory and commercialization hurdles. Looking forward, the review highlights the promise of amplification-free CRISPR assays and artificial intelligence-assisted diagnostics as pathways toward transforming point-of-care parasite surveillance within a One Health framework.
items.citation: Basit A, Hanif M. Next-generation CRISPR-based molecular diagnostics for veterinary parasitology: From laboratory innovation to one health surveillance.. Molecular and biochemical parasitology. 2026

items.title: Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications
items.summary: This review examines how the integration of multiomics technologies and artificial intelligence is reshaping precision drug discovery and clinical translation. The authors survey a broad range of multiomics approaches — including genome-wide association studies, transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics — alongside advanced deep learning methodologies, assessing how these tools illuminate the molecular underpinnings of disease. Together, they argue, these technologies can accelerate target identification, lead optimization, drug repositioning, and de novo compound design, while also improving virtual screening, pharmacokinetic modeling, and safety assessment. The review highlights applications in oncology, neurodegenerative diseases, and cardiovascular conditions, but also acknowledges persistent challenges such as harmonizing disparate data streams, ensuring reproducibility, and addressing algorithmic bias. The authors conclude that the convergence of multiomics and artificial intelligence represents a foundational shift toward more precise, data-driven therapeutic development and bench-to-clinic translational medicine.
items.citation: Yuqing Liu, Kun Zhu, Weijun Peng et al.. Multi-omics and artificial intelligence for precision drug discovery and potential clinical applications. Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy. 2026

items.title: Regulatory Challenges and Opportunities for Cell‐Derived Extracellular Vesicles in Pharmaceutical Development: A European and Global Perspective
items.summary: This paper examines the regulatory landscape surrounding cell-derived extracellular vesicles as therapeutic and diagnostic products, identifying how their acellular nature creates classification ambiguities across existing medicinal product frameworks. The authors analyze divergent regulatory approaches across major jurisdictions, noting that the European Union has issued guidance placing minimally modified extracellular vesicles outside advanced therapy medicinal product definitions, while other regulatory bodies apply drug and biological product frameworks with varying criteria. By comparing these regional approaches, the review identifies key operational challenges including inconsistent classification criteria, undefined critical quality attributes, and unresolved comparability standards that complicate international clinical development. The authors argue that extracellular vesicle products can be accommodated within existing regulatory instruments provided those tools are applied consistently and areas of ambiguity are systematically clarified through ongoing regulatory dialogue. The work is intended as a synthesis to support international harmonization efforts among regulatory agencies and scientific societies rather than to propose new normative frameworks.
items.citation: Tania Limongi, Paola Milla, Barbara Stella et al.. Regulatory Challenges and Opportunities for Cell‐Derived Extracellular Vesicles in Pharmaceutical Development: A European and Global Perspective. Journal of Extracellular Vesicles. 2026

items.title: A framework for developing university policies on generative AI governance: a cross-national comparative study
items.summary: This study examined how universities across different national contexts are approaching the governance of generative AI in higher education, focusing on institutions in the United States, Japan, and China. The researchers conducted a cross-national comparative analysis of generative AI guidelines from leading universities in these three countries, using an extended Technology Acceptance Model as an analytical lens and applying thematic coding to identify key policy themes across five domains. The analysis revealed distinct national patterns: universities in the American sample prioritized faculty autonomy, practical application, and policy flexibility; Japanese institutions aligned more closely with government directives, emphasizing ethics and risk management while offering limited implementation guidance; and Chinese institutions reflected a centralized, government-led model focused on technology application and active integration into education and research. Drawing on these comparative findings, the researchers developed the University Policy Development Framework for Generative AI, which integrates technological, organizational, and social dimensions to help institutions balance innovation against risk. The proposed framework is intended to guide universities in assessing policy priorities and building institutional capacity for sustainable generative AI governance.
items.citation: Ming Li, Qin Xie, Ariunaa Enkhtur et al.. A framework for developing university policies on generative AI governance: a cross-national comparative study. Studies in Higher Education. 2026

items.title: A probabilistic approach to separate mergers and jellyfish galaxies: Application of morphological non-parametric indexes to the DESI Legacy Survey
items.summary: This paper investigated the classification of galaxy morphological types — regular spirals, regular ellipticals, mergers, and jellyfish galaxies undergoing ram-pressure stripping — using non-parametric morphological indices measured from the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys. The researchers applied ten non-parametric indices to evaluate two-dimensional diagnostic planes using a Bayesian kernel-density classifier and combined all indices through calibrated gradient boosting machine learning models. They found that combining Shannon entropy with asymmetry or concentration indices provided the most informative separations, with the multi-class machine learning model achieving strong performance for broad structural classification. While non-parametric morphology reliably identifies general structural disturbance, distinguishing the physical origin of that disturbance proved more difficult, as jellyfish candidates occupy a relatively coherent region of parameter space whereas mergers exhibit diverse and overlapping morphologies. The study delivers probabilistic classifications for over a million galaxies and provides survey-specific diagnostic boundaries applicable to future large-scale morphological studies.
items.citation: V. M. Sampaio, Y. Jaff'e, A. Moretti et al.. A probabilistic approach to separate mergers and jellyfish galaxies: Application of morphological non-parametric indexes to the DESI Legacy Survey. arXiv. 2026

items.title: What Mean Error Misses: Device-Clock Diagnostics for Evaluating Eye Tracking across Three Virtual Reality Headsets
items.summary: This paper evaluated the accuracy and reliability of eye trackers embedded in three virtual reality headsets by having participants complete identical gaze protocols on each device. Beyond standard mean angular error, the researchers examined device-clock timing, data loss patterns, and validity flagging during deliberate eye closures to expose problems that average error metrics conceal. They found substantial differences in spatial accuracy across headsets, with one device remaining least accurate even after corrective recalibration and another showing increased error under darker display conditions, while one device produced highly autocorrelated gaze samples indicative of smoothing artifacts. Critically, timing analyses revealed serious hidden issues: one headset experienced multi-second recording pauses, another skipped individual samples, and one incorrectly flagged gaze data as valid during eye closures while the reported gaze position shifted substantially. The authors argue that eye tracker evaluations should routinely report repeated timestamps, detailed loss composition derived from device clocks, and validity behavior during eye closures rather than relying solely on mean spatial error.
items.citation: Aleksandr Chernysh, Mehedi Hasan Raju, Kamrul Hasan et al.. What Mean Error Misses: Device-Clock Diagnostics for Evaluating Eye Tracking across Three Virtual Reality Headsets. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Multimodal Generative AI Assists Comprehensive Echocardiographic Interpretation
items.summary: This paper introduces EchoChat, a generative multimodal vision-language model designed to perform comprehensive echocardiographic interpretation by emulating the cognitive workflow of a cardiologist. The system was trained on a large dataset of echocardiography-instruction pairs and incorporates a chain-of-thought reasoning mechanism to ground its diagnostic conclusions in visual evidence rather than operating as an opaque black box. EchoChat was evaluated across diverse cohorts from multiple international medical centers, where it achieved state-of-the-art performance in recognizing a broad range of cardiac conditions and quantifying cardiac measurements, outperforming existing foundation models on shared tasks. In a reader study where senior echocardiographers evaluated reports blinded to their source, reports co-generated with EchoChat were rated superior in diagnostic accuracy and completeness, and meaningfully improved diagnostic performance compared to reports produced by routine readers alone. The authors conclude that embedding clinical reasoning into multimodal AI can help address the global shortage of experienced echocardiography interpreters and broaden access to specialist cardiovascular expertise.
items.citation: Yi Qin, Marawan Elbatel, Shanshan Song et al.. Multimodal Generative AI Assists Comprehensive Echocardiographic Interpretation. arXiv. 2026

items.title: CARES: Coverage-Aware Replay Exemplar Selection for Continual Learning
items.summary: This paper addresses the challenge of catastrophic forgetting in continual learning by improving how replay buffers are constructed under fixed memory constraints. The authors propose CARES, a method that selects buffer exemplars without relying on gradients, losses, or optimization signals from the continually training model, instead leveraging the geometry of a frozen pretrained feature space through class-aware, density-weighted coverage. This design choice eliminates the computational overhead associated with existing coreset-based approaches that repeatedly update memory using model-derived signals. CARES was evaluated across a range of challenging conditions including balanced, imbalanced, and label-noisy data streams in both online class-incremental and task-incremental settings. Despite requiring no training signal from the continual learner, CARES achieves substantial speed improvements over competing coreset selectors while matching or exceeding state-of-the-art accuracy, with particularly strong gains under class imbalance conditions.
items.citation: Arundhati S. Shanbhag, Brian B. Moser, Federico Raue et al.. CARES: Coverage-Aware Replay Exemplar Selection for Continual Learning. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Computational De Novo Design of Miniprotein Candidate Neutralizers Targeting the IL-23 Cytokine Subunit p19
items.summary: This paper addresses the design of small protein-based neutralizers targeting the p19 subunit of interleukin-23, a cytokine implicated in inflammatory bowel disease and psoriasis, as an alternative to large, expensive antibody therapies. The researchers developed a computational pipeline using tools including RFdiffusion, ProteinMPNN, and BindCraft, and introduced a length-robust interface scoring metric called ipSAE to overcome a limitation of the standard confidence score that conflates construct length with interface quality. A conventional design pipeline failed to produce reliable binders across nearly a thousand designs, and the authors identified a scoring artifact that had previously generated misleading signals about binder folding quality. An interface-optimized hallucination approach substantially outperformed the conventional pipeline, yielding a majority of designs above a high-confidence threshold, with five all-alpha-helical lead candidates collectively engaging all targeted binding hotspots on p19 and showing no spurious interactions with the p40 subunit. The authors claim these are the first computationally proposed de novo miniprotein candidates designed to block the receptor-binding face of IL-23 p19, though they emphasize all findings require experimental validation.
items.citation: Raghav Paladugu, Fardina Fathmiul Alam. Computational De Novo Design of Miniprotein Candidate Neutralizers Targeting the IL-23 Cytokine Subunit p19. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Cross-Architectural Feature Fusion for Coronary Artery Stenosis Detection in X-ray Angiography
items.summary: This paper investigated automated detection of coronary artery stenosis in X-ray coronary angiography images, addressing the limitations of manual interpretation and single-task deep learning approaches. The authors developed a hybrid framework called Fusion-YOLOv11-L, which combines a YOLOv11-L object detector with a pretrained UNet++ segmentation network through a channel attention gating module, allowing the system to integrate semantic detection features with anatomically informed vessel-structural representations. The UNet++ component was pretrained on a vessel segmentation dataset to provide richer anatomical context, and the combined model was evaluated on a relabeled version of that dataset as well as an independent clinical dataset from an acute myocardial infarction study. The proposed fusion architecture outperformed the standalone detector on the primary dataset, and test-time augmentation was shown to partially mitigate performance degradation caused by cross-domain shift when evaluating on the independent clinical cohort. The authors conclude that combining cross-architecture feature fusion with lightweight test-time adaptation strategies improves both detection accuracy and generalisability across different imaging domains.
items.citation: Haobo Zhu, Mojtaba Lashgari, Jason Chai et al.. Cross-Architectural Feature Fusion for Coronary Artery Stenosis Detection in X-ray Angiography. arXiv. 2026

items.title: Alveolar stem cells go beyond making gas-exchange cells to repair damaged airways
items.summary: Alveolar type 2 cells, which normally function as stem cells maintaining the lung's air sacs and enabling gas exchange, were investigated for their potential roles beyond their home compartment. Using cell-tracking approaches, researchers followed the fate of these cells following airway injury. The study found that alveolar type 2 cells can migrate out of the alveolar compartment and into the airways, where they differentiate into bronchiolar cells to contribute to airway repair. These findings expand the known functional repertoire of alveolar type 2 cells, demonstrating that their regenerative capacity is not restricted to the alveoli but extends to damaged bronchiolar tissue.

This unexpected plasticity expands the understood regenerative role of these cells beyond gas exchange.

items.title: Global conservation area coverage substantially exceeds current estimates
items.summary: The paper examined how much of Earth's terrestrial surface is currently protected by conservation areas, a figure central to international biodiversity commitments. The researchers evaluated progress toward the area component of the Global Biodiversity Framework's thirty-percent target by assembling a globally representative sample across numerous countries and territories, incorporating national datasets that are typically excluded from global reporting. Their analysis revealed that conservation areas likely already cover substantially more land than official figures suggest, placing current coverage far closer to the thirty-percent goal than previously recognized. However, the study also found that this additional protected land does little to address gaps in ecological representativeness, meaning that simply meeting the area target would not meaningfully reduce ongoing global biodiversity loss. The authors conclude that greater focus and resources must be directed toward the qualitative and strategic components of the target, rather than emphasizing area coverage alone.
items.why_notable: This work is drawing attention because it suggests that existing conservation area coverage is considerably larger than official figures indicate, implying the global "30 by 30" biodiversity target may already be closer to being met than previously thought.
items.citation: Helen M. K. O’Neill, Joe Beeken, Heather C. Bingham et al.. Global conservation area coverage substantially exceeds current estimates. Nature. 2026

items.title: Engineered TYK2 dependence enables myeloid-selective IL-10 receptor agonism
items.summary: The paper investigated how to achieve cell-type-selective signaling for interleukin-10 (IL-10), an anti-inflammatory cytokine whose therapeutic potential is limited because it activates both beneficial myeloid suppression and unwanted T cell stimulation. The researchers discovered that myeloid cells and T cells differ in their dependence on specific JAK-family kinase pairings for IL-10 signaling, and exploited this difference to engineer a tetravalent nanobody-based myeloid-selective IL-10 receptor agonist. Cryo-electron microscopy revealed that this engineered molecule cross-links receptors in a geometry distinct from native IL-10 cytokines, rendering signaling strictly TYK2-dependent and highly sensitive to receptor abundance, thereby conferring selectivity for myeloid cells over T cells. The agonist effectively suppressed monocytes, macrophages, and dendritic cells while reducing inflammation in humanized mouse models of multiple inflammatory conditions. A humanized version demonstrated IgG-like pharmacokinetics and durable myeloid suppression without T cell activation or blood toxicities in non-human primates, establishing this geometry-based approach as a promising therapeutic strategy for myeloid-driven inflammatory diseases.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it describes an engineered nanobody-based agonist that selectively activates the IL-10 receptor on myeloid immune cells—such as monocytes, macrophages, and dendritic cells—while sparing T cells, potentially enabling the therapeutic anti-inflammatory benefits of IL-10 without its broader immunosuppressive side effects.
items.citation: D. Alejandro Canaria, Trang T. T. Nguyen, Huang Huang et al.. Engineered TYK2 dependence enables myeloid-selective IL-10 receptor agonism. Nature. 2026

items.title: Elp1 is required for myeloid differentiation and brain repopulation

items.citation: Marius Marc-Daniel Mader, Wanhua Li, Alexa Scavetti et al.. Elp1 is required for myeloid differentiation and brain repopulation. Nature. 2026

items.title: Modelling mouse embryogenesis from chemically induced totipotent stem cells

The advance offers a powerful platform for studying early mammalian embryogenesis without relying on natural embryos.
items.citation: Hua Wu, Yanyan Hu, Hanzhi Yu et al.. Modelling mouse embryogenesis from chemically induced totipotent stem cells. Nature. 2026

items.title: Competing mechanisms toughen bcc binary and medium-entropy alloys at 20 K
items.summary: This paper investigated the low-temperature mechanical behavior of body-centred cubic refractory alloys composed of group IV–V elements with similar electronic structures, focusing on their properties down to extremely low temperatures. Conventionally, bcc metals become brittle at low temperatures because screw dislocation motion becomes increasingly difficult, constricting plastic zones at crack tips and producing a ductile-to-brittle transition. The researchers found that these binary and medium-entropy alloys instead show a plateau in both tensile yield strength and fracture toughness as temperature decreases, with no ductile-to-brittle transition observed. This unusual behavior is explained by the activation of deformation twinning and an omega-phase transformation, which nucleate dislocations at their interfaces prior to global dislocation motion. Because this initial deformation mechanism is temperature insensitive, it controls yielding and prevents the crack-tip plastic zone from shrinking at low temperatures, thereby maintaining toughness.
items.why_notable: This work is attracting attention because it reveals that medium-entropy alloys maintain their fracture toughness and tensile yield strength at extremely low temperatures without undergoing the ductile-to-brittle transition typically expected in body-centered cubic metals. The finding challenges conventional understanding of how this class of alloys behaves under cryogenic conditions and points to competing deformation mechanisms as the source of this unusual toughening.
items.citation: David H. Cook, Xiaoyu Chen, Michael D O'Leary et al.. Competing mechanisms toughen bcc binary and medium-entropy alloys at 20 K. Nature. 2026

items.title: Parity-dependent coupling of molecular spin chains to a superconductor

items.citation: Katerina Vaxevani, Jon Ortuzar, Stefano Trivini et al.. Parity-dependent coupling of molecular spin chains to a superconductor. Nature. 2026

By demonstrating improved survival in animal models of both heart attack and acute kidney injury, it suggests a potential strategy for halting ischaemic damage across multiple organs.
